at falde.explanation: "At falde" means "to fall". To say rain or snow comes down, use it: "Sneen falder" (The snow is falling). To say someone fell, use the past form "faldt": "Han faldt på isen" (He fell on the ice).

sentence.da: Der kan **falde** meget sne i nat.
sentence.en: A lot of snow can fall tonight.

at falde for.explanation: "At falde for" means "to fall for". To say you suddenly love someone or something, use it: "Jeg faldt for hende" (I fell for her). Do not mix it up with plain "at falde" (to fall down): "Sneen falder" (The snow is falling).

sentence.da: Alle vil **falde for** hendes smil.
sentence.en: Everyone will fall for her smile.

at falde i god jord.explanation: "At falde i god jord" means "to go down well". Literally, it means "to fall in good soil", like a seed that will grow. To say a joke was well received, say: "Vittigheden faldt i god jord" (The joke went down well).

forms.da: det er faldet i god jord

sentence.da: Forslaget kan **falde i god jord** hos ledelsen.
sentence.en: The proposal may go down well with the management.

at falde i søvn.explanation: "At falde i søvn" means "to fall asleep". Literally, it means "to fall in sleep". To say someone is already asleep, use "at sove" (to sleep): "Hun sover" (She is sleeping).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget træt og vil snart **falde i søvn**.
sentence.en: I am very tired and will soon fall asleep.

at falde med næsen i smøret.explanation: "At falde med næsen i smøret" means "to land in clover". Literally, it means "to fall with the nose in the butter".

forms.da: Han faldt med næsen i smøret.
Hun faldt med næsen i smøret med det job.
forms.en: She landed in clover with that job.

forms.da: Vi faldt med næsen i smøret.

sentence.da: Man kan **falde med næsen i smøret**, når man arver et helt hus.
sentence.en: You can land in clover when you inherit a whole house.

at falde ned.explanation: "At falde ned" means "to fall down". To say where someone fell down from, add "fra" (from): "Barnet faldt ned fra træet" (The child fell down from the tree).

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **falde ned**!
sentence.en: Be careful, you can fall down!

at falde over.explanation: "At falde over" means "to trip over or come across". To say you trip on something while walking, use it: "Jeg faldt over en sten" (I tripped over a stone). To say you find something by chance, use it too: "Jeg faldt over en gammel bog" (I came across an old book).

forms.en: I have tripped over / come across

sentence.da: Jeg er bange for at **falde over** hunden.
sentence.en: I am afraid of tripping over the dog.

at falde til ro.explanation: "At falde til ro" means "to calm down". To say a child calms down, say: "Barnet faldt til ro" (The child calmed down). To calm someone else, use "at berolige" (to soothe): "Jeg beroliger barnet" (I soothe the child).

sentence.da: Hunden kan ikke **falde til ro**, når der er fest.
sentence.en: The dog cannot calm down when there is a party.

at fange.explanation: "At fange" means "to catch". To say you catch something moving, use it: "Politiet fanger tyven" (The police catch the thief). To say you catch a bus or train, use "at nå" (to make it) instead: "Jeg når toget" (I catch the train).

sentence.da: Kan du **fange** bolden, når jeg kaster?
sentence.en: Can you catch the ball when I throw?

at fare.explanation: "At fare" means "to rush". To say something shot past, use the past form "for": "Bilen for forbi" (The car shot past). Do not mix it up with the small word "for" (for): "Gaven er for dig" (The gift is for you).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **fare** rundt i haven i timevis.
sentence.en: The children can rush around in the garden for hours.

at fare vild.explanation: "At fare vild" means "to get lost". To say you lost a thing, use "at miste" (to lose) instead: "Jeg mistede min nøgle" (I lost my key). "Vild" means "wild" in other words: "vilde dyr" (wild animals).

sentence.da: Uden kort kan vi nemt **fare vild**.
sentence.en: Without a map, we can easily get lost.

at farve.explanation: "At farve" means "to color or dye". To say you change your hair color, say: "Hun farver sit hår" (She is dyeing her hair). To say you color in a picture, use it too: "Børnene farver tegningen" (The children are coloring the drawing).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **farve** sit hår rødt.
sentence.en: She would like to dye her hair red.

at faste.explanation: "At faste" means "to fast". To talk about Lent, the time before Easter, use "fasten" (Lent): "Fasten begynder før påske" (Lent begins before Easter).

sentence.da: Mange vælger at **faste** i en dag og kun drikke vand.
sentence.en: Many choose to fast for a day and only drink water.

at fastholde.explanation: "At fastholde" means "to maintain or hold on to". It is built from "fast" (firm) and "at holde" (to hold). To say you do not change your opinion, say: "at fastholde sin mening" (to stick to your opinion).

forms.en: I have maintained / held on to

sentence.da: Hun vil **fastholde** sin pris, selvom kunden klager.
sentence.en: She wants to maintain her price even though the customer complains.

at fastslå.explanation: "At fastslå" means "to establish or determine". To say someone states a fact after checking, say: "Politiet har fastslået, at han var alene" (The police have established that he was alone).

sentence.da: Eksperterne kan **fastslå**, hvor gammel bygningen er.
sentence.en: The experts can determine how old the building is.

at fastsætte.explanation: "At fastsætte" means "to fix or set". To say you choose a date, say: "at fastsætte en dato" (to set a date). To state a fact that is already true, use "at fastslå" (to establish) instead: "Eksperterne fastslår årsagen" (The experts establish the cause).

sentence.da: Kommunen skal **fastsætte** en pris for parkering.
sentence.en: The municipality must set a price for parking.

at fatte.explanation: "At fatte" means "to grasp or understand". To ask if someone understands, say: "Fatter du det?" (Do you get it?). To say you make a decision, use it with "en beslutning" (a decision): "Vi fatter en beslutning" (We make a decision).

sentence.da: Reglerne er så svære, at ingen kan **fatte** dem.
sentence.en: The rules are so difficult that no one can understand them.

at feje.explanation: "At feje" means "to sweep". To clean a wet floor, use "at vaske" (to wash) instead: "Jeg vasker gulvet" (I wash the floor).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **feje** køkkenet i dag.
sentence.en: I have to sweep the kitchen today.

at feje noget ind under gulvtæppet.explanation: "At feje noget ind under gulvtæppet" means "to sweep the problem under the rug". Literally, it means "to sweep something in under the floor carpet". To say a company hides a mistake, say: "Firmaet fejer fejlen ind under gulvtæppet" (The company sweeps the mistake under the rug).

forms.en: to sweep the problem under the rug

forms.da: Politikeren fejede sagen ind under gulvtæppet.
forms.en: The politician swept the case under the rug.

forms.da: Vi kan ikke feje det ind under gulvtæppet.
forms.en: We cannot sweep it under the rug.

sentence.da: Firmaet prøvede at **feje noget ind under gulvtæppet**, men det kom frem.
sentence.en: The company tried to sweep something under the rug, but it came out.

at fejle.explanation: "At fejle" means "to fail". To say a plan did not work, use it with the plan: "Planen fejlede" (The plan failed). To ask what is wrong with someone's health, use it in the question: "Hvad fejler du?" (What is wrong with you?)

sentence.da: Denne plan kan ikke **fejle**.
sentence.en: This plan cannot fail.

at fejre.explanation: "At fejre" means "to celebrate". To say which holiday you celebrate, put it after the verb: "Vi fejrer jul sammen" (We celebrate Christmas together).

sentence.da: Vi vil **fejre** min fødselsdag i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to celebrate my birthday on the weekend.

at feste.explanation: "At feste" means "to party". It is the verb for the noun "en fest" (a party). To say who you party with, add "med" (with): "Jeg fester med mine venner" (I party with my friends).

sentence.da: Vi vil **feste** hele natten i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to party all night this weekend.

at fikse.explanation: "At fikse" means "to fix". To promise someone you will fix a problem, say: "Jeg skal nok fikse det" (I will fix it, do not worry).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **fikse** den gamle cykel på en time.
sentence.en: My brother can fix the old bike in an hour.

at filme.explanation: "At filme" means "to film". It is the verb for the noun "en film" (a movie). To say who you film, put the person after the verb: "Jeg filmer min datter" (I film my daughter).

sentence.da: Må jeg **filme** dig med min telefon?
sentence.en: May I film you with my phone?

at finansiere.explanation: "At finansiere" means "to finance". To say who pays for something, put the payer first: "Staten finansierer broen" (The state finances the bridge).

sentence.da: Banken vil **finansiere** huset med et lån på tyve år.
sentence.en: The bank will finance the house with a twenty-year loan.

at finde.explanation: "At finde" means "to find". To give your opinion, use it as English does in "I find it difficult": "Jeg finder det svært" (I find it difficult).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **finde** mine nøgler.
sentence.en: I can't find my keys.

at finde på.explanation: "At finde på" means "to come up with". To say you invent a game or a plan, use it: "Vi fandt på en leg" (We came up with a game). Do not mix it up with "at finde" (to find), which is for something that already exists: "Jeg finder nøglen" (I find the key).

sentence.da: Vi skal **finde på** noget sjovt i weekenden.
sentence.en: We have to come up with something fun this weekend.

at finde ud af.explanation: "At finde ud af" means "to find out or figure out". To say you learn a fact, use it with a question word: "Jeg finder ud af, hvornår toget kører" (I find out when the train leaves). Do not mix it up with "at finde på" (to come up with), which is for ideas: "Vi finder på en løsning" (We come up with a solution).

forms.en: I have found out / figured out

sentence.da: Jeg vil **finde ud af**, hvad der er galt.
sentence.en: I want to find out what is wrong.

at finde vej.explanation: "At finde vej" means "to find one's way". The opposite is "at fare vild" (to get lost). To say you got lost, use its past tense: "Vi for vild i skoven" (We got lost in the forest).

sentence.da: Med et kort kan jeg let **finde vej**.
sentence.en: With a map, I can easily find my way.

at fjerne.explanation: "At fjerne" means "to remove". It is built from "fjern" (distant). The same word is in "en fjernbetjening" (a remote control).

sentence.da: Kan du **fjerne** skoene fra bordet?
sentence.en: Can you take the shoes off the table?

at flirte.explanation: "At flirte" means "to flirt". To say who you flirt with, add "med" (with): "Hun flirter med bartenderen" (She flirts with the bartender).

sentence.da: Han plejer at **flirte** med alle på kontoret.
sentence.en: He usually flirts with everyone at the office.

at flyde.explanation: "At flyde" means "to float or flow". When you talk about water moving along, it means "to flow": "Floden flyder ud i havet" (The river flows into the sea). When you talk about something that stays on top of a liquid, it means "to float": "Olie flyder ovenpå vand" (Oil floats on top of water).

sentence.da: Træ kan **flyde** på vand, men sten kan ikke.
sentence.en: Wood can float on water, but stone cannot.

at flygte.explanation: "At flygte" means "to flee". To say where someone flees to, add "til" (to): "De flygtede til Sverige" (They fled to Sweden).

sentence.da: De måtte **flygte** fra deres hjem.
sentence.en: They had to flee from their home.

at flytte.explanation: "At flytte" means "to move", as in moving house. To say you move a thing from one place to another, put the thing after the verb: "Kan du flytte bilen?" (Can you move the car?)

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte** til et nyt hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move to a new house.

at flytte ind.explanation: "At flytte ind" means "to move in". It is "at flytte" (to move) plus "ind" (in). To say you move a thing instead, leave out "ind": "Jeg flytter bordet" (I move the table).

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte ind** i vores nye hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move into our new house.

at flytte sammen.explanation: "At flytte sammen" means "to move in together". It is "at flytte" (to move) plus "sammen" (together). To say who you move in with, add "med" (with): "Jeg flytter sammen med min kæreste" (I am moving in with my boyfriend or girlfriend).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **flytte sammen** næste år.
sentence.en: We would like to move in together next year.

at flytte sig.explanation: "At flytte sig" means "to move (oneself)". To ask someone to step aside, say: "Kan du flytte dig?" (Can you move over?) To say you change homes, leave out "sig" (oneself): "Vi flytter til Aarhus" (We are moving to Aarhus).

sentence.da: Bilen står i vejen, og han vil ikke **flytte sig**.
sentence.en: The car is in the way, and he won't move.

at flytte ud.explanation: "At flytte ud" means "to move out". The opposite is "at flytte ind" (to move in). To say when you move in, say: "Vi flytter ind i morgen" (We are moving in tomorrow).

sentence.da: Min datter skal **flytte ud** og bo alene.
sentence.en: My daughter is going to move out and live alone.

at flyve.explanation: "At flyve" means "to fly". To say time passes quickly, use it for time: "Tiden flyver" (Time flies).

sentence.da: Fuglen kan **flyve** højt.
sentence.en: The bird can fly high.

at flå.explanation: "At flå" means "to rip or skin". When you tear a package open, use it: "Han flåede pakken op" (He ripped the package open). When you take the skin off an animal, use it: "Kokken flår kaninen" (The cook skins the rabbit). When a business charges far too much, use it: "Hotellet flår turisterne" (The hotel rips off the tourists).

sentence.da: Slagteren skal **flå** dyret og bruge kødet.
sentence.en: The butcher must skin the animal and use the meat.

at flække.explanation: "At flække" means "to split". To say what you split, put it after the verb: "Han flækker brænde" (He splits firewood).

sentence.da: Man kan **flække** et træstykke med en økse.
sentence.en: You can split a piece of wood with an ax.

at fnise.explanation: "At fnise" means "to giggle". To describe children giggling, say: "Børnene fnisede bag bogen" (The children giggled behind the book).

sentence.da: Eleverne kan ikke lade være med at **fnise** i timen.
sentence.en: The students cannot help giggling in class.

at fodre.explanation: "At fodre" means "to feed". It is the verb for the noun "et foder" (animal feed). To say what you feed an animal with, add "med" (with): "Jeg fodrer hestene med hø" (I feed the horses with hay).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **fodre** hundene klokken seks.
sentence.en: I have to feed the dogs at six o'clock.

at fokusere.explanation: "At fokusere" means "to focus". To say what you focus on, add "på" (on): "Jeg fokuserer på arbejdet" (I focus on the work).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **fokusere**, når der er så meget larm.
sentence.en: It is hard to focus when there is so much noise.

at folde.explanation: "At folde" means "to fold". To say you put your hands together, use it with the hands: "at folde hænderne" (to fold your hands). To say you fold a sheet of paper, say: "Hun folder papiret" (She folds the paper).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **folde** tøjet og lægge det i skabet.
sentence.en: I have to fold the clothes and put them in the closet.

at forandre.explanation: "At forandre" means "to change". To say you replace one thing with another, use "at skifte" (to switch) instead: "Jeg skifter job" (I am changing jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forandre** mit liv i år.
sentence.en: I want to change my life this year.

at forandre sig.explanation: "At forandre sig" means "to change". To say a place or a person has become different, use "sig" (oneself): "Byen har forandret sig" (The city has changed). To say you change something, leave out "sig": "Han forandrer planen" (He changes the plan).

sentence.da: Mange ting vil **forandre sig** i fremtiden.
sentence.en: Many things will change in the future.

at forankre.explanation: "At forankre" means "to anchor". It is built from "et anker" (an anchor). To say where an idea or decision is rooted, add "i" (in): "Beslutningen er forankret i ledelsen" (The decision is anchored in the management).

sentence.da: Vi vil **forankre** den nye plan i hele organisationen.
sentence.en: We want to anchor the new plan across the whole organization.

at forbedre.explanation: "At forbedre" means "to improve". It is built from "bedre" (better). To say something gets better without anyone working on it, use "at blive bedre" (to get better): "Vejret bliver bedre" (The weather is getting better).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **forbedre** mit danske ordforråd.
sentence.en: I would like to improve my Danish vocabulary.

at forbeholde.explanation: "At forbeholde" means "to reserve", as in keeping something for certain people only. To say who a seat is kept for, say: "Pladsen er forbeholdt gæster" (The seat is reserved for guests). To say you keep a right for yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Vi forbeholder os retten til at ændre prisen" (We reserve the right to change the price).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **forbeholde** den nye parkeringsplads beboerne.
sentence.en: The municipality will reserve the new parking lot for the residents.

at forberede.explanation: "At forberede" means "to prepare". To get yourself ready, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg forbereder mig til prøven" (I am getting ready for the test).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **forberede** et møde i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to prepare a meeting tomorrow.

at forberede sig.explanation: "At forberede sig" means "to prepare oneself". To say you prepare a thing instead of yourself, leave out "sig" (oneself): "Hun forbereder et møde" (She prepares a meeting).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **forberede sig** til prøven.
sentence.en: The students have to prepare for the test.

at forbinde.explanation: "At forbinde" means "to connect". To say what you connect something to, add "med" (with): "Jeg forbinder printeren med computeren" (I connect the printer to the computer). When you link one thing with another in your mind, it means "to associate": "Jeg forbinder sommer med is" (I associate summer with ice cream).

sentence.da: Du kan **forbinde** din telefon med højttaleren.
sentence.en: You can connect your phone to the speaker.

at forblive.explanation: "At forblive" means "to remain". To say what someone stays, put it after the verb: "Vi forbliver venner" (We remain friends). To say someone becomes something new, use "at blive" (to become) instead: "Hun bliver direktør" (She becomes director).

sentence.da: Hun vil **forblive** direktør, selvom firmaet bliver solgt.
sentence.en: She will remain director even though the company is sold.

at forbruge.explanation: "At forbruge" means "to consume". To say what a household uses up, use it with the supply: "Vi forbruger meget vand" (We consume a lot of water). To say you eat a meal, use "at spise" (to eat) instead: "Jeg spiser frokost" (I eat lunch).

sentence.da: Vi må **forbruge** mindre strøm, når prisen stiger.
sentence.en: We must consume less electricity when the price rises.

at forbyde.explanation: "At forbyde" means "to forbid or ban". To say a government bans something, put the thing after the verb: "Regeringen forbyder plastikposer" (The government bans plastic bags). To say something is not allowed, use "forbudt" (forbidden): "Det er forbudt at ryge her" (Smoking is forbidden here).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **forbyde** mobiler i timerne.
sentence.en: The school wants to ban phones in class.

at fordele.explanation: "At fordele" means "to distribute". To say who shares the money, use "mellem" (between): "Vi fordeler pengene mellem børnene" (We distribute the money between the children).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **fordele** eleverne i tre grupper.
sentence.en: The teacher wants to divide the students into three groups.

at fordoble.explanation: "At fordoble" means "to double". To say a number doubles by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Antallet fordobler sig hvert år" (The number doubles every year).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **fordoble** produktionen i løbet af to år.
sentence.en: The company wants to double production within two years.

at fordybe sig.explanation: "At fordybe sig" means "to immerse oneself". It is built from "dyb" (deep). To say what you are immersed in, add "i" (in): "Han fordyber sig i sin forskning" (He immerses himself in his research).

sentence.da: Hun kan **fordybe sig** i en bog i flere timer.
sentence.en: She can immerse herself in a book for hours.

at foregive.explanation: "At foregive" means "to pretend". To say someone pretends to be something, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Han foregav at være syg" (He pretended to be sick). To say the same with a full sentence, use "at lade som om" (to act as if): "Han lod som om, han var syg" (He pretended he was sick).

sentence.da: Han kan ikke **foregive**, at han ikke ved noget.
sentence.en: He cannot pretend that he knows nothing.

at foregå.explanation: "At foregå" means "to take place or happen". To say where an event takes place, name the place after the verb: "Mødet foregår i konferencelokalet" (The meeting takes place in the conference room). Its forms start with "det" (it), because the verb is used about events, not about people.

sentence.da: Hvor skal festen **foregå**?
sentence.en: Where will the party take place?

at forene.explanation: "At forene" means "to unite". To say you bring two countries together, say: "Vi vil forene de to lande" (We want to unite the two countries). When you combine two things in your life, it means "to combine": "Hun forener arbejde og familie" (She combines work and family).

sentence.da: Musikken kan **forene** mennesker fra hele verden.
sentence.en: Music can unite people from all over the world.

at forenkle.explanation: "At forenkle" means "to simplify". It is built from "enkel" (simple). To say you make rules simpler, use it with the rules: "Vi forenkler reglerne" (We simplify the rules).

sentence.da: Vi bør **forenkle** formularen, fordi den er for svær.
sentence.en: We should simplify the form because it is too hard.

at foreslå.explanation: "At foreslå" means "to suggest". To suggest a thing, put it straight after the verb: "Jeg foreslår en anden dag" (I suggest another day).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **foreslå**, at vi spiser ude.
sentence.en: I want to suggest that we eat out.

at forestille sig.explanation: "At forestille sig" means "to imagine". To say you cannot picture something, say: "Jeg kan ikke forestille mig det" (I cannot imagine that).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke **forestille sig** livet uden musik.
sentence.en: She cannot imagine life without music.

at forestå.explanation: "At forestå" means "to be in charge of or lie ahead". When someone runs a department or a project, it means "to be in charge of": "Hun forestår afdelingen" (She is in charge of the department). When something is coming, it means "to lie ahead": "Der forestår en svær tid" (A hard time lies ahead).

forms.en: to be in charge of / lie ahead
I have been in charge of

sentence.da: En erfaren leder skal **forestå** projektet og holde styr på pengene.
sentence.en: An experienced leader must be in charge of the project and keep track of the money.

at foretage.explanation: "At foretage" means "to make or carry out". To say you make a change, say: "Vi foretager en ændring" (We make a change). To say you make a call, say: "Jeg foretager et opkald" (I make a call). To say you make a cake, use "at lave" (to make) instead: "Jeg laver en kage" (I am making a cake).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **foretage** en lille undersøgelse i morgen.
sentence.en: The doctor will carry out a small examination tomorrow.

at foretrække.explanation: "At foretrække" means "to prefer". To say what someone prefers to do, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Hun foretrækker at gå" (She prefers to walk). To name the option you like less, add "frem for" (over): "Jeg foretrækker hunde frem for katte" (I prefer dogs to cats).

sentence.da: Jeg ville **foretrække** te frem for kaffe.
sentence.en: I would prefer tea to coffee.

at forfalde.explanation: "At forfalde" means "to fall due or decay". When a payment reaches its deadline, it means "to fall due": "Fakturaen forfalder om fjorten dage" (The invoice falls due in fourteen days). When a building falls into ruin, it means "to decay": "Huset forfalder" (The house is falling apart).

sentence.da: Uden vedligehold vil huset hurtigt **forfalde**.
sentence.en: Without upkeep the house will quickly decay.

at forfatte.explanation: "At forfatte" means "to compose", as in writing a text. It is the verb for "en forfatter" (a writer). To say you write a letter with care, say: "Hun forfattede et brev til ministeren" (She composed a letter to the minister).

sentence.da: Borgmesteren vil **forfatte** en tale til festen.
sentence.en: The mayor will compose a speech for the party.

at forfremme.explanation: "At forfremme" means "to promote", as in moving a person up to a better job: "Chefen forfremmede hende" (The boss promoted her). To promote a product, use "at markedsføre" (to market) instead: "Vi markedsfører den nye cykel" (We market the new bike).

sentence.da: Chefen vil **forfremme** hende, fordi hun arbejder så hårdt.
sentence.en: The boss wants to promote her because she works so hard.

at forfølge.explanation: "At forfølge" means "to pursue or persecute". When you follow a goal, it means "to pursue": "Hun forfølger sin drøm" (She pursues her dream). When a ruler treats people cruelly for their views, it means "to persecute": "Regimet forfølger sine kritikere" (The regime persecutes its critics).

sentence.da: Politiet kan ikke **forfølge** bilen længere, fordi den er for hurtig.
sentence.en: The police cannot pursue the car any longer because it is too fast.

at forføre.explanation: "At forføre" means "to seduce". It is built from "for" and "at føre" (to lead). To say someone tried to win a person over, say: "Han forsøgte at forføre hende" (He tried to seduce her).

sentence.da: Skurken vil **forføre** hende og få hendes penge.
sentence.en: The villain wants to seduce her and get her money.

at forhandle.explanation: "At forhandle" means "to negotiate". To name the topic, add "om" (about): "Vi forhandler om prisen" (We negotiate the price). Do not mix it up with "en forhandler" (a dealer), who sells goods: "Jeg køber bilen hos en forhandler" (I buy the car from a dealer).

sentence.da: Vi vil **forhandle** om prisen.
sentence.en: We want to negotiate the price.

at forhindre.explanation: "At forhindre" means "to prevent". To say what someone was stopped from doing, add "i at" (from) before the verb: "Regnen forhindrede os i at gå" (The rain stopped us from going).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forhindre** mange ulykker med bedre veje.
sentence.en: We can prevent many accidents with better roads.

at forhøre sig.explanation: "At forhøre sig" means "to inquire". To name the topic you ask about, add "om" (about): "Jeg forhører mig om åbningstiderne" (I am inquiring about the opening hours). Without "sig" (oneself), "at forhøre" means to interrogate: "Politiet forhører den mistænkte" (The police interrogate the suspect).

sentence.da: Han vil **forhøre sig** om prisen i butikken.
sentence.en: He wants to inquire about the price at the shop.

at forklare.explanation: "At forklare" means "to explain". To say who you explain something to, use "for" after the thing: "Kan du forklare det for mig?" (Can you explain it to me?)

sentence.da: Læreren vil **forklare** ordet.
sentence.en: The teacher will explain the word.

at forklæde sig.explanation: "At forklæde sig" means "to disguise oneself". To say what you disguise yourself as, add "som" (as): "Hun forklædte sig som tjener" (She disguised herself as a waiter).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **forklæde sig** som politibetjent og gå ind i banken.
sentence.en: The thief wants to disguise himself as a police officer and go into the bank.

at forkorte.explanation: "At forkorte" means "to shorten". To say you make a meeting shorter, say: "Vi forkorter mødet" (We shorten the meeting). When you shorten a word, it means "to abbreviate", and the result is "en forkortelse" (an abbreviation).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forkorte** turen ved at tage motorvejen.
sentence.en: We can shorten the trip by taking the highway.

at forkæle.explanation: "At forkæle" means "to spoil (pamper)". When you treat someone to nice things, say: "Jeg vil forkæle dig i dag" (I want to pamper you today). To say a child gets too much and expects it, use the form "forkælet": "Børnene er forkælede" (The children are spoiled).

sentence.da: Bedsteforældrene vil **forkæle** børnebørnene med is og slik.
sentence.en: The grandparents want to spoil the grandchildren with ice cream and candy.

at forlade.explanation: "At forlade" means "to leave". To say you leave a place, put the place after it: "Hun forlod huset klokken 8" (She left the house at 8). To say you leave a person, put the person after it: "Hun forlod ham" (She left him). To say you are simply going away, use "at gå" (to go): "Jeg går nu" (I am leaving now).

sentence.da: Han vil **forlade** landet i næste måned.
sentence.en: He will leave the country next month.

at forlange.explanation: "At forlange" means "to demand". To say what someone demands, put it after the verb: "Han forlangte sine penge tilbage" (He demanded his money back). To say someone asks for something politely, use "at bede om" (to ask for) instead: "Jeg beder om regningen" (I ask for the bill).

sentence.da: Du kan **forlange** en ny vare, hvis den er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: You can demand a new item if it has broken.

at forlove sig.explanation: "At forlove sig" means "to get engaged". To name the person you get engaged to, add "med" (with): "Hun forlovede sig med Peter i sommer" (She got engaged to Peter this summer).

sentence.da: Han har en ring og vil **forlove sig** med hende.
sentence.en: He has a ring and wants to get engaged to her.

at forlænge.explanation: "At forlænge" means "to extend". To say you make a permit last longer, say: "Jeg forlænger mit visum" (I extend my visa). To say you make a thing longer, put it after the verb: "Vi forlænger bordet" (We make the table longer).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **forlænge** vores ophold med to dage.
sentence.en: We would like to extend our stay by two days.

at forløbe.explanation: "At forløbe" means "to proceed or go". To say how an event went, add a word for how: "Festen forløb roligt" (The party went calmly). Its forms start with "det" (it), because the verb is used about events, not about people.

sentence.da: En operation som denne kan **forløbe** uden problemer.
sentence.en: An operation like this can go without problems.

at formidle.explanation: "At formidle" means "to convey or mediate". When you pass knowledge from one person to others, it means "to convey": "Læreren formidler viden til eleverne" (The teacher conveys knowledge to the students). When you arrange something between two sides, it means "to mediate": "Hun formidler en aftale mellem de to firmaer" (She mediates a deal between the two companies).

sentence.da: En god journalist kan **formidle** svære ting på en enkel måde.
sentence.en: A good journalist can convey difficult things in a simple way.

at formindske.explanation: "At formindske" means "to reduce". To say you cut costs, say: "Vi formindsker udgifterne" (We reduce the costs). Danish also has the shorter "at mindske" (to lessen): "Vi mindsker risikoen" (We lessen the risk).

sentence.da: Mere motion kan **formindske** risikoen for sygdom.
sentence.en: More exercise can reduce the risk of illness.

at formode.explanation: "At formode" means "to suppose or presume". To say what you assume, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg formoder, at han kommer snart" (I presume he is coming soon).

sentence.da: Vi kan **formode**, at toget er forsinket på grund af sneen.
sentence.en: We can presume that the train is late because of the snow.

at formulere.explanation: "At formulere" means "to formulate". To ask someone to word a question another way, say: "Kan du formulere spørgsmålet anderledes?" (Can you word the question differently?)

sentence.da: Det er svært at **formulere** sine tanker på et fremmedsprog.
sentence.en: It is hard to put your thoughts into words in a foreign language.

at fornemme.explanation: "At fornemme" means "to sense". To say you feel that something is wrong, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg fornemmer, at noget er galt" (I sense that something is wrong).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **fornemme**, når ejeren er ked af det.
sentence.en: The dog can sense when its owner is sad.

at forny.explanation: "At forny" means "to renew". It is built from "ny" (new). To say you make a document valid again, say: "Jeg skal forny mit pas" (I have to renew my passport).

sentence.da: Du skal **forny** dit pas, før du rejser.
sentence.en: You must renew your passport before you travel.

at fornægte.explanation: "At fornægte" means "to deny", as in refusing to accept that something is real. To say someone refuses to accept his feelings, say: "Han fornægter sine følelser" (He denies his feelings). To say you deny doing something, use "at nægte" (to deny) instead: "Jeg nægter at have taget pengene" (I deny taking the money).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **fornægte** din fortid.
sentence.en: You cannot deny your past.

at fornærme.explanation: "At fornærme" means "to offend". To say you did not mean to hurt someone, say: "Jeg ville ikke fornærme dig" (I did not mean to offend you).

sentence.da: Du kan **fornærme** folk, hvis du er for direkte.
sentence.en: You can offend people if you are too direct.

at forpligte.explanation: "At forpligte" means "to commit or oblige". When an agreement ties someone to something, it means "to oblige": "Kontrakten forpligter firmaet" (The contract obliges the company). When you promise to do something yourself, add "sig" (oneself) and it means "to commit": "Jeg forpligter mig til at komme" (I commit myself to coming).

sentence.da: En underskrift kan **forpligte** dig til at betale.
sentence.en: A signature can commit you to paying.

at forråde.explanation: "At forråde" means "to betray". To say someone turns on a friend, put the friend after the verb: "Han forrådte sin ven" (He betrayed his friend). When something gives a person away, it also fits: "Hans smil forrådte ham" (His smile gave him away).

sentence.da: Man må aldrig **forråde** en ven, der stoler på en.
sentence.en: You must never betray a friend who trusts you.

at forsikre.explanation: "At forsikre" means "to assure or insure". When you tell someone that something is certain, it means "to assure": "Jeg forsikrer dig om, at det er sikkert" (I assure you it is safe). When you buy cover against damage, it means "to insure": "Vi forsikrer bilen" (We insure the car). The cover itself is "en forsikring" (an insurance).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forsikre** huset mod brand og tyveri.
sentence.en: I want to insure the house against fire and theft.

at forsinke.explanation: "At forsinke" means "to delay". To say a train is late, use the form "forsinket" (delayed): "Toget er forsinket" (The train is delayed).

sentence.da: Trafikken kan **forsinke** os med en time.
sentence.en: The traffic can delay us by an hour.

at forske.explanation: "At forske" means "to research". To name the subject, add "i" (in): "Hun har forsket i kræft i ti år" (She has researched cancer for ten years).

sentence.da: Hun vil **forske** i, hvorfor bier forsvinder.
sentence.en: She wants to research why bees are disappearing.

at forskrække.explanation: "At forskrække" means "to frighten". To say you gave someone a sudden shock, say: "Du forskrækkede mig" (You frightened me). To say you got a fright, use "at blive forskrækket" (to get a fright): "Jeg blev forskrækket" (I got a fright).

sentence.da: Et højt knald kan **forskrække** børnene, fordi det kommer pludseligt.
sentence.en: A loud bang can frighten the children because it comes suddenly.

at forskyde.explanation: "At forskyde" means "to shift or displace". To say a time moves to a different point, use it for time: "Vi forskyder mødet en time" (We shift the meeting by an hour). In working life, "forskudt arbejdstid" means working hours that start at different times (staggered hours).

sentence.da: Et jordskælv kan **forskyde** jordlagene under byen.
sentence.en: An earthquake can shift the layers of earth under the city.

at forsone sig.explanation: "At forsone sig" means "to reconcile". To name who you make peace with, add "med" (with): "Jeg vil forsone mig med min bror" (I want to reconcile with my brother). To say you accept something hard, use it with the loss: "Han har forsonet sig med tabet" (He has come to terms with the loss).

sentence.da: Efter mange års skænderi vil brødrene gerne **forsone sig**.
sentence.en: After many years of quarreling the brothers want to reconcile.

at forstyrre.explanation: "At forstyrre" means "to disturb". To ask politely when you walk in on someone, say: "Må jeg forstyrre?" (May I interrupt?) To tell someone not to disturb you, say: "Forstyr mig ikke" (Do not disturb me).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **forstyrre** hende, når hun arbejder.
sentence.en: The children must not disturb her when she works.

at forstå.explanation: "At forstå" means "to understand". To say you do not understand, say: "Jeg forstår ikke" (I do not understand). To say you know a fact, use "at vide" (to know) instead: "Jeg ved, at han kommer" (I know that he is coming).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **forstå** ham.
sentence.en: I cannot understand him.

at forstærke.explanation: "At forstærke" means "to reinforce". It is built from "stærk" (strong). To say you make a wall stronger, say: "Vi forstærker muren" (We reinforce the wall). The device that makes sound louder is "en forstærker" (an amplifier).

sentence.da: Vi må **forstærke** broen, før tunge biler kører over den.
sentence.en: We must reinforce the bridge before heavy cars drive over it.

at forsvare.explanation: "At forsvare" means "to defend". To say who is defended, put it after the verb: "Soldaterne forsvarer landet" (The soldiers defend the country). In Denmark, the armed forces are called "Forsvaret" (the Defense).

sentence.da: Soldaterne skal **forsvare** grænsen mod fjenden.
sentence.en: The soldiers must defend the border against the enemy.

at forsvinde.explanation: "At forsvinde" means "to disappear". To say something that was here is now gone, use "er forsvundet": "Min taske er forsvundet" (My bag has disappeared).

sentence.da: Tyven kan **forsvinde** i mængden.
sentence.en: The thief can disappear in the crowd.

at forsyne.explanation: "At forsyne" means "to supply". To name what you supply, add "med" (with): "Vi forsyner byen med vand" (We supply the city with water). To tell guests at a meal to take food, say: "Forsyn dig!" (Help yourself!)

sentence.da: Vindmøllerne kan **forsyne** tusind hjem med strøm.
sentence.en: The wind turbines can supply a thousand homes with electricity.

at forsøge.explanation: "At forsøge" means "to attempt". To say you attempt to do something, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg forsøger at forstå" (I am trying to understand). To say you taste a cake, use "at prøve" (to try) instead: "Jeg prøver kagen" (I try the cake).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forsøge** at komme i morgen.
sentence.en: I will try to come tomorrow.

at forsømme.explanation: "At forsømme" means "to neglect". To say you let something go without care, put it after the verb: "Han forsømmer sin have" (He neglects his garden). When a student misses lessons, it also fits: "en elev, der forsømmer undervisningen" (a student who skips class).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **forsømme** sine tænder, hvis man vil beholde dem.
sentence.en: You must not neglect your teeth if you want to keep them.

at forsørge.explanation: "At forsørge" means "to support (financially)". To say who you earn money for, put them after the verb: "Hun forsørger tre børn" (She supports three children). To say you give help or encouragement, use "at støtte" (to support) instead: "Jeg støtter dig" (I support you).

related.en: to feed / provide a living for

sentence.da: Hun skal **forsørge** tre børn og arbejder to steder.
sentence.en: She has to support three children and works in two places.

at fortage sig.explanation: "At fortage sig" means "to wear off". To say a pain slowly goes away, say: "Smerten fortager sig langsomt" (The pain slowly wears off).

sentence.da: Smerten i foden vil **fortage sig** af sig selv.
sentence.en: The pain in the foot will wear off on its own.

at fortie.explanation: "At fortie" means "to conceal or keep quiet about". To say someone hid a mistake by not mentioning it, say: "Han fortiede fejlen" (He kept the mistake quiet).

forms.en: I have concealed / kept quiet about

sentence.da: Sælgeren må ikke **fortie**, at bilen har skader.
sentence.en: The seller must not conceal that the car has damage.

at fortjene.explanation: "At fortjene" means "to deserve". To say someone deserves something, put it after the verb: "Du fortjener en pause" (You deserve a break). It is built on "at tjene" (to earn). To say you earn money, use "at tjene" alone: "Jeg tjener penge" (I earn money).

sentence.da: Hun har trænet hårdt og kan **fortjene** prisen.
sentence.en: She has trained hard and may deserve the prize.

at fortolke.explanation: "At fortolke" means "to interpret". To say a text can be read in different ways, say: "Man kan fortolke et digt på mange måder" (A poem can be read in many ways).

sentence.da: Hvert land kan **fortolke** reglerne på sin egen måde.
sentence.en: Each country can interpret the rules in its own way.

at fortryde.explanation: "At fortryde" means "to regret". To name what you regret, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg fortryder, at jeg sagde det" (I regret that I said it).

sentence.da: Du kommer til at **fortryde** det senere.
sentence.en: You will regret it later.

at fortrænge.explanation: "At fortrænge" means "to repress or displace". When you push a painful memory out of your mind, it means "to repress": "Hun har fortrængt ulykken" (She has repressed the accident). When something takes the place of something else, it means "to displace": "Bilen har fortrængt hesten" (The car has displaced the horse).

sentence.da: Hjernen kan **fortrænge** minder, der gør for ondt.
sentence.en: The brain can repress memories that hurt too much.

at fortsætte.explanation: "At fortsætte" means "to continue". To name the activity you keep doing, add "med at" (with ...ing) before the verb: "Fortsæt med at læse!" (Keep reading!)

sentence.da: Efter pausen kan vi **fortsætte** timen.
sentence.en: After the break, we can continue the class.

at fortsætte med.explanation: "At fortsætte med" means "to continue with". To say you carry on with a job, name the job after "med": "Jeg fortsætter med arbejdet" (I continue with the work). To tell someone to keep going, say: "Fortsæt!" (Keep going!)

sentence.da: Vi kan **fortsætte med** øvelsen efter pausen.
sentence.en: We can continue with the exercise after the break.

at fortælle.explanation: "At fortælle" means "to tell". To say you tell someone a story, put the person first: "Jeg fortæller dig en historie" (I am telling you a story). To say someone says a few words aloud, use "at sige" (to say) instead: "Han siger hej" (He says hello).

sentence.da: Min mormor vil **fortælle** en historie til børnene.
sentence.en: My grandmother will tell the children a story.

at forudse.explanation: "At forudse" means "to foresee". It is built from "forud" (ahead) and "at se" (to see). To say you see a price rise coming: "Vi forudser en prisstigning" (We foresee a price increase).

sentence.da: Ingen kan **forudse** vejret om en måned.
sentence.en: No one can foresee the weather in a month.

at forudsige.explanation: "At forudsige" means "to predict". It is built from "forud" (ahead) and "at sige" (to say), so it is literally "to say ahead". To say someone predicts the weather: "Hun forudsiger regn i morgen" (She predicts rain tomorrow).

sentence.da: Ingen kan **forudsige**, hvordan vejret bliver i næste måned.
sentence.en: No one can predict what the weather will be next month.

at forurene.explanation: "At forurene" means "to pollute". To say what harms the sea: "Olie forurener havet" (Oil pollutes the sea).

sentence.da: Biler og fabrikker kan **forurene** luften i store byer.
sentence.en: Cars and factories can pollute the air in big cities.

at forvandle.explanation: "At forvandle" means "to transform". To say something turns into something else, add "til" (into): "Heksen forvandlede prinsen til en frø" (The witch turned the prince into a frog). To say something changes by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Larven forvandler sig til en sommerfugl" (The caterpillar turns into a butterfly).

sentence.da: Maling kan **forvandle** et gammelt værelse til et nyt.
sentence.en: Paint can transform an old room into a new one.

at forvente.explanation: "At forvente" means "to expect". To say you require something from someone: "Vi forventer, at du kommer til tiden" (We expect you to be on time).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forvente** regn i morgen.
sentence.en: We can expect rain tomorrow.

at forvirre.explanation: "At forvirre" means "to confuse". To say that you are the one who is confused, use "forvirret" (confused): "Jeg er helt forvirret" (I am completely confused).

sentence.da: Alle de nye regler kan **forvirre** gæsterne.
sentence.en: All the new rules can confuse the guests.

at forværre.explanation: "At forværre" means "to worsen". To say something becomes worse with nobody causing it, use "at blive værre" (to get worse): "Vejret bliver værre" (The weather gets worse).

sentence.da: Dårlig søvn kan **forværre** smerterne.
sentence.en: Poor sleep can worsen the pain.

at forårsage.explanation: "At forårsage" means "to cause". It comes from "en årsag" (a reason). To say what led to a result: "Ulykken forårsagede store forsinkelser" (The accident caused big delays).

sentence.da: Is på vejene kan **forårsage** mange ulykker om vinteren.
sentence.en: Ice on the roads can cause many accidents in the winter.

at forære.explanation: "At forære" means "to give (as a gift)". To name the person receiving the gift, put the person right after the verb and leave out "til" (to): "Han forærede hende en ring" (He gave her a ring).

sentence.da: Farfar vil **forære** mig sit gamle ur.
sentence.en: Grandpa wants to give me his old watch as a gift.

at fotografere.explanation: "At fotografere" means "to photograph". To say you take a picture of something, use "at tage et billede af" (to take a picture of): "Jeg tager et billede af huset" (I take a picture of the house).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **fotografere** solnedgangen med min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to photograph the sunset with my phone.

at fremføre.explanation: "At fremføre" means "to present or put forward". To say you put forward a view: "Hun fremførte sine synspunkter" (She put forward her views). To say someone performs music before an audience: "Koret fremførte en salme" (The choir performed a hymn).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **fremføre** et teaterstykke for forældrene.
sentence.en: The students are going to perform a play for the parents.

at fremhæve.explanation: "At fremhæve" means "to emphasize". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at hæve" (to raise), so it is literally "to raise forward". To say you point out what matters most: "Læreren fremhævede de vigtigste punkter" (The teacher emphasized the most important points).

sentence.da: Den røde farve kan **fremhæve** dine øjne.
sentence.en: The red color can make your eyes stand out.

at fremkalde.explanation: "At fremkalde" means "to cause or develop (film)". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at kalde" (to call). To say something brings on an effect: "Medicinen fremkaldte kvalme" (The medicine caused nausea). To say you develop photos from film: "Jeg fremkalder billederne i aften" (I am developing the pictures tonight).

sentence.da: Stærk sol kan **fremkalde** hovedpine hos nogle mennesker.
sentence.en: Strong sun can cause headaches in some people.

at fremkomme.explanation: "At fremkomme" means "to emerge or appear". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at komme" (to come). To say someone comes up with a claim, add "med" (with): "Han fremkom med en ny teori" (He came up with a new theory).

sentence.da: Nye fakta kan **fremkomme** under retssagen.
sentence.en: New facts can emerge during the trial.

at fremlægge.explanation: "At fremlægge" means "to present". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at lægge" (to put). To say a group puts a report before others: "Udvalget fremlagde en rapport om skolerne" (The committee presented a report about the schools).

sentence.da: Direktøren skal **fremlægge** årsregnskabet på mødet.
sentence.en: The director is going to present the annual accounts at the meeting.

at fremme.explanation: "At fremme" means "to promote or further". It comes from "frem" (forward). To say something helps health grow: "at fremme sundhed" (to promote health). To say something holds growth back, use the opposite, "at hæmme" (to hinder): "Kulden hæmmer væksten" (The cold hinders growth).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **fremme** cykling med flere cykelstier.
sentence.en: The town wants to promote cycling with more bike lanes.

at fremskynde.explanation: "At fremskynde" means "to speed up". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at skynde" (to hurry). To say you make a decision happen sooner: "Vi vil fremskynde beslutningen" (We want to speed up the decision). To say a car goes faster, use "at accelerere" (to accelerate) instead: "Bilen accelererer hurtigt" (The car accelerates quickly).

sentence.da: Flere hænder kan **fremskynde** arbejdet og spare os tid.
sentence.en: More hands can speed up the work and save us time.

at fremstille.explanation: "At fremstille" means "to produce or portray". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at stille" (to place). To say a text or picture shows someone in a certain way: "Avisen fremstiller ham som en helt" (The newspaper portrays him as a hero).

sentence.da: Fabrikken kan **fremstille** tusind cykler om dagen.
sentence.en: The factory can produce a thousand bikes per day.

at fremvise.explanation: "At fremvise" means "to display or show". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at vise" (to show). To ask someone to show you a picture, use "at vise" instead: "Vis mig billedet" (Show me the picture).

sentence.da: Du skal **fremvise** din billet, når kontrolløren spørger.
sentence.en: You must show your ticket when the inspector asks.

at fri.explanation: "At fri" means "to propose". To name the person you ask to marry you, add "til" (to): "Han friede til hende" (He proposed to her). The same spelling "fri" is also an adjective meaning "off work": "Jeg har fri i dag" (I am off today).

sentence.da: Han vil **fri** til hende i aften.
sentence.en: He is going to propose to her tonight.

at frifinde.explanation: "At frifinde" means "to acquit". It is built from "fri" (free) and "at finde" (to find). To say a court finds someone guilty, use the opposite, "at dømme" (to convict): "Retten dømte ham for tyveri" (The court convicted him of theft).

sentence.da: Retten vil **frifinde** ham, fordi der ikke er nogen beviser.
sentence.en: The court will acquit him because there is no evidence.

at frigive.explanation: "At frigive" means "to release". It is built from "fri" (free) and "at give" (to give). To say a publisher puts out a book, use "at udgive" (to publish) instead: "Forlaget udgiver bogen i maj" (The publisher publishes the book in May).

sentence.da: Retten vil **frigive** fangen, fordi der ikke er beviser.
sentence.en: The court will release the prisoner because there is no evidence.

at fritage.explanation: "At fritage" means "to exempt". It is built from "fri" (free) and "at tage" (to take). To name what someone is freed from, add "for" (from): "Han blev fritaget for gymnastik" (He was exempted from gym).

sentence.da: Lægen kan **fritage** dig fra arbejde, når du er syg.
sentence.en: The doctor can exempt you from work when you are sick.

at frygte.explanation: "At frygte" means "to fear". To say you are afraid of something in everyday talk, use "at være bange for" (to be afraid of) instead: "Jeg er bange for hunde" (I am afraid of dogs).

sentence.da: Vi må ikke **frygte** fremtiden.
sentence.en: We must not fear the future.

at fryse.explanation: "At fryse" means "to freeze". To say you feel cold: "Jeg fryser" (I am cold; literally, "I freeze"). To say water turns to ice: "Vandet fryser" (The water freezes). Do not mix it up with "en fryser" (a freezer): "Maden ligger i fryseren" (The food is in the freezer).

sentence.da: Uden jakke vil du **fryse**.
sentence.en: Without a jacket you will freeze.

at fuldende.explanation: "At fuldende" means "to complete". It comes from "fuld" (full). To say someone completes a work of art: "Hun fuldendte maleriet" (She completed the painting). To say a meeting simply ends, use "at afslutte" (to end) instead: "Vi afslutter mødet" (We end the meeting).

sentence.da: Han vil **fuldende** romanen, før han bliver halvfjerds.
sentence.en: He wants to complete the novel before he turns seventy.

at fuldføre.explanation: "At fuldføre" means "to complete". It is built from "fuld" (full) and "at føre" (to lead). To say you complete a long race: "Han fuldførte maratonløbet" (He completed the marathon).

sentence.da: Han vil **fuldføre** sin uddannelse og blive lærer.
sentence.en: He wants to complete his education and become a teacher.

at fungere.explanation: "At fungere" means "to work or function". To say a machine does what it should: "Opvaskemaskinen fungerer ikke" (The dishwasher does not work). To say a person has a job, use "at arbejde" (to work) instead: "Jeg arbejder på et hospital" (I work at a hospital).

sentence.da: Tror du, at planen kan **fungere**?
sentence.en: Do you think the plan can work?

at fylde.explanation: "At fylde" means "to fill or take up space". To say you fill a container: "Jeg fylder glasset med vand" (I fill the glass with water). To say a thing takes up space: "Sofaen fylder meget" (The sofa takes up a lot of space). To say how old you turn on your birthday: "Jeg fylder 30 i dag" (I turn 30 today).

forms.en: I have filled / taken up space

sentence.da: Børnene må **fylde** posen med slik.
sentence.en: The children may fill the bag with candy.

at fylde op.explanation: "At fylde op" means "to fill up". The "op" (up) adds that you fill something all the way to the top. To say you fill the fuel tank: "Jeg fylder tanken op" (I fill up the tank).

sentence.da: Vi skal **fylde op** med benzin i morgen.
sentence.en: We have to fill up with gas tomorrow.

at fylde år.explanation: "At fylde år" means "to have a birthday". To say how old you turn, add the age: "Jeg fylder tredive år" (I am turning thirty). To say it is your birthday without naming an age, use "at have fødselsdag" (to have a birthday): "Jeg har fødselsdag i dag" (It is my birthday today).

sentence.da: Min far skal **fylde år** i morgen.
sentence.en: My dad has a birthday tomorrow.

at fyre.explanation: "At fyre" means "to fire (dismiss)". To say a boss dismisses an employee: "Chefen fyrede ham" (The boss fired him). To say you make a fire in a stove: "Vi fyrer i brændeovnen" (We light the wood stove).

sentence.da: Firmaet må **fyre** ti medarbejdere.
sentence.en: The company has to fire ten employees.

at få.explanation: "At få" means "to get". To say you are allowed to do something, use it in "få lov" (to be allowed): "Jeg fik lov" (I was allowed). To go and fetch something, use "at hente" (to fetch) instead: "Jeg henter brød" (I am fetching bread).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få** en gave til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I am going to get a present for my birthday.

at få besked.explanation: "At få besked" means "to be notified". To say you will tell someone, use "at give besked" (to let someone know): "Jeg giver dig besked" (I will let you know).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få besked**, når pakken kommer.
sentence.en: I will be notified when the package arrives.

at få besøg.explanation: "At få besøg" means "to have visitors". To say you go to see someone yourself, use "at være på besøg" (to be visiting): "Jeg er på besøg hos min mor" (I am visiting my mother).

sentence.da: Jeg rydder op, fordi jeg skal **få besøg**.
sentence.en: I am tidying up because I am having visitors.

at få det bedre.explanation: "At få det bedre" means "to feel better". To wish a sick person well, say "God bedring!" (Get well soon!).

sentence.da: Med lidt hvile vil du **få det bedre**.
sentence.en: With some rest, you will feel better.

at få et barn.explanation: "At få et barn" means "to have a baby", literally "to get a child". To say you and your partner are going to have a baby: "Vi får et barn" (We are having a baby).

sentence.da: Min søster er gravid og skal **få et barn**.
sentence.en: My sister is pregnant and is going to have a baby.

at få fat i.explanation: "At få fat i" means "to get hold of". To say you grabbed an object: "Jeg fik fat i rebet" (I grabbed the rope). To say you could not reach a person: "Jeg kunne ikke få fat i ham" (I could not get hold of him).

sentence.da: Barnet kan ikke **få fat i** kagen på hylden.
sentence.en: The child cannot get hold of the cake on the shelf.

at få fri.explanation: "At få fri" means "to get off (work or school)". To say when you were allowed to leave: "Jeg fik fri klokken tre" (I got off at three o'clock). To say you decide to take a day yourself, use "at tage fri" (to take time off): "Jeg tager fri på fredag" (I am taking Friday off).

forms.en: I have gotten off (work or school)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **få fri** tidligt i dag.
sentence.en: I would like to get off early today.

at få hjælp.explanation: "At få hjælp" means "to get help". Danish uses "hjælp" without an article after "brug for" (need): "Jeg har brug for hjælp" (I need help).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og vil **få hjælp**.
sentence.en: I am sick and want to get help.

at få kolde fødder.explanation: "At få kolde fødder" means "to get cold feet". To say your feet are really cold, use "at have kolde fødder" (to have cold feet): "Jeg har kolde fødder" (My feet are cold).

sentence.da: Mange kan **få kolde fødder**, når bryllupsdagen nærmer sig.
sentence.en: Many people can get cold feet when the wedding day gets close.

at få lov til.explanation: "At få lov til" means "to be allowed to". To name what you are allowed to do, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg fik lov til at gå hjem" (I was allowed to go home).

sentence.da: Børnene vil gerne **få lov til** at blive længe.
sentence.en: The children would like to be allowed to stay longer.

at få lyst til.explanation: "At få lyst til" means "to feel like". To name what you feel like doing, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg fik lyst til at gå en tur" (I felt like going for a walk). To ask what someone feels like having, use "have lyst til" instead: "Har du lyst til en kop kaffe?" (Do you feel like a cup of coffee?)

sentence.da: Når solen skinner, kan man **få lyst til** is.
sentence.en: When the sun shines, you can feel like having ice cream.

at få nok.explanation: "At få nok" means "to have had enough". To say you cannot stand something any more: "Nu har jeg fået nok!" (Now I have had enough!) To ask whether someone has eaten enough: "Har du fået nok at spise?" (Have you had enough to eat?)

forms.en: I get fed up (have had enough)

sentence.da: Jeg begynder at **få nok** af støjen.
sentence.en: I am starting to get fed up with the noise.

at få ondt af.explanation: "At få ondt af" means "to feel sorry for". To say you pity someone: "Jeg får ondt af hende" (I feel sorry for her). Do not mix it up with "at have ondt i" (to have pain in): "Jeg har ondt i maven" (My stomach hurts).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke andet end **få ondt af** ham.
sentence.en: You cannot help feeling sorry for him.

at få ret.explanation: "At få ret" means "to be proven right". To say events showed that someone was correct: "Hun fik ret" (She was proven right). To say someone is right at this moment, use "at have ret" (to be right): "Du har ret" (You are right).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, hun vil **få ret** til sidst.
sentence.en: I think she will be proven right in the end.

at få styr på.explanation: "At få styr på" means "to get control of or sort out". To say something is already under control, use "at have styr på" (to have under control): "Nu har jeg styr på regnskabet" (Now I have the accounts under control).

forms.en: to get control of / sort out
I get control of / sort out
I got control of / sorted out
I have gotten control of / sorted out

sentence.da: Vi skal **få styr på** rodet i garagen.
sentence.en: We have to sort out the mess in the garage.

at få tid.explanation: "At få tid" means "to find time": "Jeg fik tid til at læse" (I found time to read). To say you got an appointment, for example at the hairdresser: "Jeg fik tid hos frisøren" (I got an appointment at the hairdresser). To ask whether someone is free right now, use "at have tid" (to have time): "Har du tid nu?" (Do you have time now?)

related.en: to have time to / make it

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **få tid** hos lægen før mandag.
sentence.en: I cannot get an appointment with the doctor before Monday.

at få travlt.explanation: "At få travlt" means "to get busy". To say you are busy right now, use "at have travlt" (to be busy): "Jeg har travlt" (I am busy).

sentence.da: Vi vil **få travlt**, når gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We will get busy when the guests arrive.

at få øje på.explanation: "At få øje på" means "to catch sight of", literally "to get an eye on". To say you noticed an animal: "Jeg fik øje på en ræv" (I caught sight of a fox).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **få øje på** bussen endnu.
sentence.en: I can't spot the bus yet.

at føde.explanation: "At føde" means "to give birth". To say a woman has a baby: "Hun føder en datter" (She gives birth to a daughter). To say where you were born, use "at blive født" (to be born): "Jeg blev født i Aarhus" (I was born in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Kvinden skal **føde** barnet på hospitalet.
sentence.en: The woman is going to give birth to the baby at the hospital.

at fødes.explanation: "At fødes" means "to be born". It comes from "at føde" (to give birth). To say when you were born, use "at blive født" (to be born): "Jeg blev født i 1990" (I was born in 1990).

sentence.da: Vores barn skal **fødes** i maj.
sentence.en: Our child is due to be born in May.

at føle.explanation: "At føle" means "to feel", as in sensing something with your body. To describe your mood, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg føler mig glad" (I feel happy).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **føle** vinden på min hud.
sentence.en: I can feel the wind on my skin.

at føle sig.explanation: "At føle sig" means "to feel (a certain way)". To say how you feel: "Jeg føler mig glad" (I feel happy). To say who is feeling, change "sig" to match the person: "du føler dig" (you feel), "han føler sig" (he feels).

sentence.da: Man kan **føle sig** ensom i en ny by.
sentence.en: You can feel lonely in a new city.

at føles.explanation: "At føles" means "to feel (seem)". To say how a thing seems to you: "Vandet føles koldt" (The water feels cold). To say how a person feels, use "at føle sig" (to feel (a certain way)) instead: "Jeg føler mig træt" (I feel tired).

sentence.da: Det kan **føles** underligt at flytte.
sentence.en: It can feel strange to move.

at følge.explanation: "At følge" means "to follow". To say someone walks behind you: "Hunden følger mig" (The dog follows me). To say you go along with someone to take them somewhere: "Jeg følger dig hjem" (I will walk you home).

sentence.da: Alle skal **følge** reglerne i skolen.
sentence.en: Everyone has to follow the rules at school.

at følge med.explanation: "At følge med" means "to keep up or come along". To ask whether someone can keep the pace: "Kan du følge med?" (Can you keep up?) To say you are joining someone: "Jeg følger med" (I will come along). Without "med" (along), "at følge" means "to follow": "Hunden følger mig" (The dog follows me).

forms.en: I have kept up / come along

sentence.da: Hun går hurtigt, og jeg kan ikke **følge med**.
sentence.en: She walks fast, and I can't keep up.

at føre.explanation: "At føre" means "to lead or conduct". To say someone runs a conversation: "Han fører samtalen" (He is leading the conversation). To say you keep accounts or records: "Vi fører regnskab" (We keep the accounts).

sentence.da: Vejen kan **føre** dig til stranden.
sentence.en: The road can lead you to the beach.

en fabel.explanation: "En fabel" means "a fable". The word "fabelagtig" (fabulous) comes from it: "en fabelagtig rejse" (a fabulous trip).

sentence.da: I en **fabel** taler dyrene som mennesker og lærer os noget.
sentence.en: In a fable the animals talk like people and teach us something.

en fabrik.explanation: "En fabrik" means "a factory". When "fabrik" is joined to another word, it gets an "s": "en fabriksarbejder" (a factory worker).

sentence.da: Min bror arbejder på en **fabrik** og laver møbler.
sentence.en: My brother works at a factory and makes furniture.

en fabriksarbejder.explanation: "En fabriksarbejder" means "a factory worker". It joins "fabrik" (factory) and "arbejder" (worker) with an "s". The ending "-arbejder" is also in "en havnearbejder" (a dock worker).

sentence.da: En **fabriksarbejder** står ved et samlebånd og pakker varer.
sentence.en: A factory worker stands at an assembly line and packs goods.

en facade.explanation: "En facade" means "a facade". It also means an appearance that hides what is behind it: "en facade af venlighed" (a facade of friendliness).

sentence.da: Husets **facade** er gul og vender ud mod gaden.
sentence.en: The house's facade is yellow and faces the street.

en fagbog.explanation: "En fagbog" means "a nonfiction book". It is built from "fag" (subject or trade) and "bog" (book).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **fagbog** om økonomi, fordi jeg skal til eksamen.
sentence.en: I am reading a nonfiction book about economics because I have an exam.

en fagforening.explanation: "En fagforening" means "a trade union". It is built from "fag" (trade) and "forening" (association).

sentence.da: Min **fagforening** hjælper mig, hvis jeg får problemer på arbejdet.
sentence.en: My union helps me if I have problems at work.

en faktor.explanation: "En faktor" means "a factor". To say something influences a result: "Pris er en vigtig faktor" (Price is an important factor). In math, a factor is a number that is multiplied: "2 og 3 er faktorer i 6" (2 and 3 are factors of 6).

sentence.da: Vejret er en **faktor**, som man ikke selv kan styre.
sentence.en: The weather is a factor that you cannot control yourself.

en faktura.explanation: "En faktura" means "an invoice". To ask for the bill after a meal, use "en regning" (a bill) instead: "Kan vi få regningen?" (Can we have the bill?)

sentence.da: Vi sender en **faktura**, og du betaler inden fjorten dage.
sentence.en: We send an invoice, and you pay within fourteen days.

en familie.explanation: "En familie" means "a family". To say a couple starts having children, use "at stifte familie" (to start a family): "De vil stifte familie" (They want to start a family).

sentence.da: Min **familie** er mor, far og søster.
sentence.en: My family is my mom, my dad and my sister.

en familiefest.explanation: "En familiefest" means "a family party". It is built from "familie" (family) and "fest" (party). The word "fest" is also in "en julefest" (a Christmas party).

sentence.da: Vi holder en **familiefest** for farmor.
sentence.en: We are having a family party for grandma.

en fan.explanation: "En fan" means "a fan", as in a supporter of a team or singer. For a fan that cools a room, use "en ventilator" (a fan) instead: "Tænd ventilatoren, det er varmt" (Turn on the fan, it is hot).

sentence.da: Min bror er **fan** af det danske landshold.
sentence.en: My brother is a fan of the Danish national team.

en fange.explanation: "En fange" means "a prisoner". It comes from the verb "at fange" (to catch): a prisoner is a person who has been caught.

sentence.da: Den **fange**, der flygtede, blev fanget igen næste dag.
sentence.en: The prisoner who escaped was caught again the next day.

en fanklub.explanation: "En fanklub" means "a fan club". It is built from "fan" (fan) and "klub" (club).

sentence.da: Hun er medlem af en **fanklub** for sit yndlingsband.
sentence.en: She is a member of a fan club for her favorite band.

en fantasi.explanation: "En fantasi" means "a fantasy". To say something is not real: "Det er bare en fantasi" (It is just a fantasy). It also means the ability to imagine things. To say someone has that ability: "Hun har en rig fantasi" (She has a rich imagination).

sentence.da: Børn har ofte meget **fantasi**.
sentence.en: Children often have a lot of imagination.

en far.explanation: "En far" means "a father". To speak to your own father, say "Hej, far!" (Hi, Dad!). The word "far" is also in "farfar" (father's father) and "farbror" (father's brother).

sentence.da: Min mor og min **far** har to børn.
sentence.en: My mother and my father have two children.

en farbror.explanation: "En farbror" means "an uncle (father's brother)". It is built from "far" (father) and "bror" (brother). To say your mother's brother, use "en morbror" (an uncle on your mother's side): "Min morbror bor i Odense" (My mother's brother lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **farbror** er min fars bror og bor i Aarhus.
sentence.en: My uncle is my father's brother and lives in Aarhus.

en fare.explanation: "En fare" means "a danger". To say what may happen, add "for" (of): "Der er fare for brand" (There is a danger of fire). To say something is in danger, use "i fare" (in danger), without "en": "Dyret er i fare" (The animal is in danger).

sentence.da: Børnene er i **fare** på den tynde is.
sentence.en: The children are in danger on the thin ice.

en farfar.explanation: "En farfar" means "a grandfather (father's father)". It is built from "far" (father) and "far" (father). To say your mother's father, use "en morfar" (a grandfather on your mother's side): "Min morfar bor i Odense" (My mother's father lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **farfar** er min fars far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my father's father.

en farmaceut.explanation: "En farmaceut" means "a pharmacist". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Min søster er farmaceut" (My sister is a pharmacist).

sentence.da: En **farmaceut** kan forklare, hvordan man tager sin medicin.
sentence.en: A pharmacist can explain how to take your medicine.

en farmor.explanation: "En farmor" means "a grandmother (father's mother)". It is built from "far" (father) and "mor" (mother). To talk to her or about her like a name, leave out "en": "Farmor kommer i dag" (Grandma is coming today).

sentence.da: Min **farmor** er min fars mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en fart.explanation: "En fart" means "speed". To say things are moving fast and full of energy: "Der er fart på" (Things are really moving).

sentence.da: Bilen kørte i høj **fart** gennem byen.
sentence.en: The car drove at high speed through the town.

en fartbøde.explanation: "En fartbøde" means "a speeding ticket". It is built from "fart" (speed) and "bøde" (fine). To say you got a fine for something else, use "en bøde" (a fine): "Jeg fik en bøde" (I got a fine).

sentence.da: Han fik en **fartbøde** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: He got a speeding ticket on the highway.

en fartgrænse.explanation: "En fartgrænse" means "a speed limit". It is built from "fart" (speed) and "grænse" (limit). To say someone goes over the limit: "at overskride fartgrænsen" (to exceed the speed limit).

sentence.da: Der er en **fartgrænse** på 50 i byen.
sentence.en: There is a speed limit of 50 in town.

en farve.explanation: "En farve" means "a color". The same spelling is also a verb, "at farve" (to dye): "Hun farver sit hår" (She is dyeing her hair).

sentence.da: Hvilken **farve** har din bil? Den er rød.
sentence.en: What color is your car? It is red.

en fase.explanation: "En fase" means "a phase". To talk about the moon, use the plural: "månens faser" (the phases of the moon).

sentence.da: Barnet er i en svær **fase** lige nu.
sentence.en: The child is in a hard phase right now.

en fastelavnsbolle.explanation: "En fastelavnsbolle" means "a Shrovetide bun". It is built from "fastelavn" (Shrovetide) and "bolle" (bun). Danes eat it around Fastelavn, a holiday in February or March when children dress up in costumes.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **fastelavnsbolle** med fløde.
sentence.en: I am eating a Shrovetide bun with cream.

en faster.explanation: "En faster" means "an aunt (father's sister)". To say your mother's sister, use "en moster" (an aunt on your mother's side): "Min moster bor i Esbjerg" (My mother's sister lives in Esbjerg).

sentence.da: Min **faster** er min fars søster og bor i Aalborg.
sentence.en: My aunt is my father's sister and lives in Aalborg.

en favorit.explanation: "En favorit" means "a favorite". To make a word with it, put "favorit" in front of another word: "favoritsang" (favorite song).

sentence.da: Pizza er min **favorit** blandt alle retter.
sentence.en: Pizza is my favorite of all dishes.

en feber.explanation: "En feber" means "a fever". To say you have a fever, leave out "en": "Jeg har feber" (I have a fever).

sentence.da: Hun har **feber** og bliver i sengen.
sentence.en: She has a fever and stays in bed.

en fejebakke.explanation: "En fejebakke" means "a dustpan". It is built from "feje" (to sweep) and "bakke" (tray). The word "bakke" also means "a hill": "en stor bakke" (a big hill).

sentence.da: Jeg samler støvet op med en **fejebakke**.
sentence.en: I pick up the dust with a dustpan.

en fejl.explanation: "En fejl" means "an error or bug". To say a program has a fault: "Der er en fejl i programmet" (There is an error in the program). To say a person did something wrong: "Jeg lavede en fejl" (I made a mistake).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en **fejl** i din tekst.
sentence.en: I found a mistake in your text.

en fejltagelse.explanation: "En fejltagelse" means "a mistake". It comes from "at tage fejl" (to be wrong). For a fault in a machine or a text, use "en fejl" (an error): "Der er en fejl i teksten" (There is an error in the text).

sentence.da: Det var en **fejltagelse**, at jeg sendte mailen til dig.
sentence.en: It was a mistake that I sent the email to you.

en fejring.explanation: "En fejring" means "a celebration". It comes from "at fejre" (to celebrate). To name what is celebrated, add "af" (of): "fejringen af jul" (the celebration of Christmas). To talk about the party itself, use "en fest" (a party): "Festen starter klokken otte" (The party starts at eight o'clock).

sentence.da: Familien holder en lille **fejring** af hendes fødselsdag.
sentence.en: The family holds a small celebration of her birthday.

en ferie.explanation: "En ferie" means "a vacation". To say you are going away, use "på" (on): "Jeg tager på ferie" (I am going on vacation). To say when something happens, use "i ferien" (during the vacation): "I ferien læser jeg meget" (During the vacation I read a lot).

sentence.da: Jeg har fri og tager på **ferie**.
sentence.en: I have time off and am going on vacation.

en fersken.explanation: "En fersken" means "a peach". To talk about more than one peach, add "-er": "tre ferskener" (three peaches).

sentence.da: En **fersken** er sød og saftig, og den har en sten.
sentence.en: A peach is sweet and juicy, and it has a pit.

en fest.explanation: "En fest" means "a party". To say you throw a party: "Vi holder fest i weekenden" (We are having a party this weekend). To wish someone a good time at a party, say "God fest!" (Have a good party!).

sentence.da: Vi holder **fest** med musik og kage.
sentence.en: We are having a party with music and cake.

en festdag.explanation: "En festdag" means "a festive day". It is built from "fest" (party) and "dag" (day). To talk about a public holiday, use "en helligdag" (a public holiday): "Juledag er en helligdag" (Christmas Day is a public holiday).

sentence.da: Bryllupsdagen er en stor **festdag** for hele familien.
sentence.en: The wedding day is a big festive day for the whole family.

sentence.da: Vi skal på **festival** i sommer og sove i telt.
sentence.en: We are going to a festival this summer and sleeping in a tent.

en festsal.explanation: "En festsal" means "a banquet hall". It is built from "fest" (party) and "sal" (hall).

sentence.da: Bryllupsgæsterne spiser og danser i den store **festsal**.
sentence.en: The wedding guests eat and dance in the big banquet hall.

en festtale.explanation: "En festtale" means "a celebratory speech". It is built from "fest" (party) and "tale" (speech). To say someone gives a speech, use "at holde" (to hold): "at holde en tale" (to give a speech).

sentence.da: Hun holdt en kort **festtale** for sin bedste ven.
sentence.en: She gave a short speech for her best friend.

en fiasko.explanation: "En fiasko" means "a failure". Danish spells it with a "k" where English "fiasco" has a "c".

sentence.da: Festen blev en **fiasko**, fordi maden slet ikke kom.
sentence.en: The party became a fiasco because the food never came.

en figur.explanation: "En figur" means "a figure". To say a character in a story: "en figur i bogen" (a character in the book). To describe someone's body shape: "Hun har en flot figur" (She has a nice figure).

sentence.da: Børnene tegner en sjov **figur** på papiret.
sentence.en: The children draw a funny figure on the paper.

en fil.explanation: "En fil" means "a file" on a computer. It is also a metal tool for smoothing things, like "en neglefil" (a nail file).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne den **fil**, du sendte mig.
sentence.en: I cannot open the file you sent me.

en filial.explanation: "En filial" means "a branch", as in a branch of a company. To say a company opens one in another town: "Vi åbner en filial i Odense" (We are opening a branch in Odense). Do not mix it up with "en afdeling" (a department): "Jeg arbejder i salgsafdelingen" (I work in the sales department).

sentence.da: Banken har en **filial** i hver større by.
sentence.en: The bank has a branch in every larger town.

en film.explanation: "En film" means "a film". To say more than one, add no ending: "Vi har set to film" (We have seen two films). To ask if someone has seen a film, use "set" (seen): "Har du set filmen?" (Have you seen the film?)

sentence.da: Vi ser en **film** i biografen.
sentence.en: We watch a movie at the movie theater.

en filmaften.explanation: "En filmaften" means "a movie night". It is built from "film" (movie) and "aften" (evening). To suggest one, ask: "Skal vi have filmaften i aften?" (Shall we have movie night tonight?)

sentence.da: Vi har **filmaften** hver fredag med popcorn og venner.
sentence.en: We have a movie night every Friday with popcorn and friends.

en filmstjerne.explanation: "En filmstjerne" means "a film star". It is built from "film" (movie) and "stjerne" (star). To talk about stars in the sky, use the same word "stjerne": "Der er mange stjerner i aften" (There are many stars tonight).

sentence.da: Hun er blevet en kendt **filmstjerne** i USA.
