sentence.en: She has become a famous film star in the USA.

en filosof.explanation: "En filosof" means "a philosopher". To say what a person studies, use "filosofi" (philosophy): "Hun læser filosofi" (She studies philosophy).

sentence.da: En **filosof** tænker over, hvad der er rigtigt og forkert.
sentence.en: A philosopher thinks about what is right and wrong.

en finale.explanation: "En finale" means "a final", as in the last match of a competition. To say a team gets that far, say: "De nåede finalen" (They reached the final). To talk about the big last part of a concert, use the same word: "Koncertens finale var flot" (The finale of the concert was beautiful).

sentence.da: Kampen søndag er en **finale**, og alle vil se den.
sentence.en: The match on Sunday is a final, and everyone wants to watch it.

en finanslov.explanation: "En finanslov" means "a national budget". It is built from "finans" (finance) and "lov" (law). In Denmark, the parliament "Folketinget" passes it each year.

sentence.da: Folketinget skal vedtage en **finanslov**, før det nye år begynder.
sentence.en: Parliament must pass a finance act before the new year begins.

en finger.explanation: "En finger" means "a finger". To say your finger hurts, Danish says "the finger" where English says "my finger": "Jeg har ondt i fingeren" (My finger hurts), literally "I have a pain in the finger".

sentence.da: Hun har en ring på sin **finger**.
sentence.en: She has a ring on her finger.

en finne.explanation: "En finne" means "a fin". Another meaning is a person from Finland. To say someone is one, say: "Min ven er finne" (My friend is a Finn).

sentence.da: Fisken bruger sin **finne** til at dreje i vandet.
sentence.en: The fish uses its fin to turn in the water.

en firewall.explanation: "En firewall" means "a firewall". The word comes from English. To say you switch it off, use "at slå fra" (to switch off): "Slå firewallen fra" (Turn the firewall off).

sentence.da: Min **firewall** stopper farlige programmer.
sentence.en: My firewall stops dangerous programs.

en firkant.explanation: "En firkant" means "a four-sided shape". It is built from "fire" (four) and "kant" (edge). The part "kant" also appears in "en bordkant" (a table edge).

sentence.da: Bordet er en **firkant**, ikke en cirkel.
sentence.en: The table is a four-sided shape, not a circle.

en fisk.explanation: "En fisk" means "a fish". In the plural, "fisk" has no ending: "tre fisk" (three fish). To say what you eat, use "at spise" (to eat): "Vi spiser fisk til middag" (We eat fish for dinner).

sentence.da: En **fisk** svømmer i vandet.
sentence.en: A fish swims in the water.

en fiskefrikadelle.explanation: "En fiskefrikadelle" means "a fish cake". It is built from "fisk" (fish) and "frikadelle" (a Danish meatball). A classic Danish dish is "fiskefrikadeller med remoulade" (fish cakes with remoulade, a cold sauce).

sentence.da: En **fiskefrikadelle** er lavet af hakket fisk og stegt på panden.
sentence.en: A fish cake is made of minced fish and fried in a pan.

en fiskehandler.explanation: "En fiskehandler" means "a fishmonger". It is built from "fisk" (fish) and "handler" (a dealer). The word also means the shop itself. To say you go to the shop: "Jeg skal ned til fiskehandleren" (I am going down to the fish shop).

sentence.da: Jeg køber frisk laks hos en **fiskehandler**.
sentence.en: I buy fresh salmon from a fishmonger.

en fisker.explanation: "En fisker" means "a fisherman". To say what a fisherman does, use "at fange" (to catch): "Fiskeren fanger torsk" (The fisherman catches cod). Do not mix it up with "en fiskehandler" (a fishmonger): "Fiskehandleren sælger frisk laks" (The fishmonger sells fresh salmon).

sentence.da: Vores nabo er **fisker** og sejler hver morgen.
sentence.en: Our neighbor is a fisherman and sails every morning.

en fiskerby.explanation: "En fiskerby" means "a fishing village". It is built from "fisker" (fisherman) and "by" (town). The part "by" also appears in "en storby" (a big city).

sentence.da: Jeg bor i en lille **fiskerby** ved havet.
sentence.en: I live in a small fishing village by the sea.

en fiskestang.explanation: "En fiskestang" means "a fishing rod". The last part "stang" (pole) also appears in "en flagstang" (a flagpole). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to fiskestænger" (two fishing rods).

sentence.da: Han fanger fisk med en **fiskestang** og en lille krog.
sentence.en: He catches fish with a fishing rod and a small hook.

en fjende.explanation: "En fjende" means "an enemy". To talk about an enemy that two sides share, say: "en fælles fjende" (a common enemy).

sentence.da: Kongen sendte soldater mod sin **fjende**.
sentence.en: The king sent soldiers against his enemy.

en fjer.explanation: "En fjer" means "a feather". In the plural, "fjer" has no ending: "tre fjer" (three feathers). To say a pillow is filled with feathers: "en pude med fjer" (a pillow with feathers).

sentence.da: Fuglen har en lang **fjer** på vingen.
sentence.en: The bird has a long feather on its wing.

en fjerdedel.explanation: "En fjerdedel" means "a quarter", one of four equal parts. It is built from fjerde (fourth) and del (part), the same way as "en femtedel" (a fifth).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler en **fjerdedel** af huslejen.
sentence.en: I pay a quarter of the rent.

en fjernbetjening.explanation: "En fjernbetjening" means "a remote control". It is built from "fjern" (far) and "betjening" (operation). "Betjening" also means "service", as in "god betjening" (good service).

sentence.da: Man bruger en **fjernbetjening** til at skifte kanal.
sentence.en: You use a remote control to change channels.

sentence.da: Skibet sejler ind i en **fjord**, ikke ud på havet.
sentence.en: The ship sails into a fjord, not out to sea.

en flagermus.explanation: "En flagermus" means "a bat", as in the animal. Literally, it is "flutter mouse", from "flagre" (to flutter) and "mus" (mouse). To say more than one, add no ending: "to flagermus" (two bats).

sentence.da: Om natten jager en **flagermus** insekter i mørket.
sentence.en: At night, a bat hunts insects in the dark.

en flagstang.explanation: "En flagstang" means "a flagpole". The last part "stang" (pole) also appears in "en fiskestang" (a fishing rod). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to flagstænger" (two flagpoles).

sentence.da: Flaget sidder øverst på en høj **flagstang**.
sentence.en: The flag is at the top of a tall flagpole.

en flamme.explanation: "En flamme" means "a flame". To talk about a former love, say: "en gammel flamme" (an old flame).

sentence.da: Når du tænder et lys, kommer der en lille **flamme**.
sentence.en: When you light a candle, a small flame appears.

en flaske.explanation: "En flaske" means "a bottle". To say what is in it, put the drink right after it, with no word for "of": "en flaske vand" (a bottle of water).

sentence.da: Han hælder mælk fra en **flaske** i glasset.
sentence.en: He pours milk from a bottle into the glass.

en flaskeåbner.explanation: "En flaskeåbner" means "a bottle opener". It is built from "flaske" (bottle) and "åbner" (opener). The last part "åbner" also appears in "en dåseåbner" (a can opener).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne flasken uden en **flaskeåbner**.
sentence.en: I cannot open the bottle without a bottle opener.

et fleksjob.explanation: "Et fleksjob" means "a flex job", a job in Denmark for a person who can only work part of a normal week because of illness or injury. The municipality helps pay the wage.

sentence.da: Hun har et **fleksjob**, fordi hun ikke kan arbejde fuld tid.
sentence.en: She has a flex job because she cannot work full time.

en fletning.explanation: "En fletning" means "a braid". The matching verb is "at flette" (to braid): "Hun fletter sit hår" (She braids her hair).

sentence.da: Hun satte sit lange hår i en **fletning**.
sentence.en: She put her long hair in a braid.

en flirt.explanation: "En flirt" means "a flirt". The matching verb is "at flirte" (to flirt): "De flirter hele aftenen" (They flirt all evening).

sentence.da: Det var bare en **flirt**, ikke et rigtigt forhold.
sentence.en: It was just a flirt, not a real relationship.

en flise.explanation: "En flise" means "a tile". To say where it goes, put the place before it: "en gulvflise" (a floor tile) and "en vægflise" (a wall tile).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en ny **flise** på badeværelsets gulv.
sentence.en: I am laying a new tile on the bathroom floor.

en flod.explanation: "En flod" means "a river". To name one, say: "Rhinen er en flod" (The Rhine is a river). Do not mix it up with "en å" (a stream), which is smaller: "Der er en å bag huset" (There is a stream behind the house).

sentence.da: Der ligger en gammel by ved en bred **flod**.
sentence.en: An old town lies by a wide river.

en flok.explanation: "En flok" means "a flock". It also means "a crowd" of people. To talk about animals together, say: "en flok får" (a flock of sheep). To talk about people together, say: "en flok børn" (a bunch of children).

sentence.da: En **flok** fugle sidder på taget.
sentence.en: A flock of birds is sitting on the roof.

en flok fugle.explanation: "En flok fugle" means "a flock of birds". After "flok", the birds are plural: "fugle" (birds), from "en fugl" (a bird). The first part "flok" (flock) also works for other groups: "en flok får" (a flock of sheep) and "en flok børn" (a bunch of children).

forms.en: a flock of birds in the field

sentence.da: På marken sidder en **flok fugle** og spiser korn.
sentence.en: On the field sits a flock of birds eating grain.

en flue.explanation: "En flue" means "a fly". The word also appears in "en fluesmækker" (a fly swatter).

sentence.da: Der er en **flue** i min suppe.
sentence.en: There is a fly in my soup.

en flybillet.explanation: "En flybillet" means "a plane ticket". It is built from "fly" (plane) and "billet" (ticket). The part "billet" also appears in "en koncertbillet" (a concert ticket).

sentence.da: Uden en **flybillet** kan du ikke flyve.
sentence.en: Without a plane ticket you cannot fly.

en flygtning.explanation: "En flygtning" means "a refugee". The word comes from the verb "at flygte" (to flee). To say people fled, use it in the past: "De flygtede fra krigen" (They fled from the war).

sentence.da: Hun kom til Danmark som **flygtning** i 2015.
sentence.en: She came to Denmark as a refugee in 2015.

en flygtningestrøm.explanation: "En flygtningestrøm" means "a flow of refugees". It is built from "en flygtning" (a refugee) and "en strøm" (a stream). "Strøm" also means electric current: "Strømmen er gået" (The power has gone out).

sentence.da: Krigen førte til en **flygtningestrøm** mod nabolandene.
sentence.en: The war led to a flow of refugees toward the neighboring countries.

en flyrejse.explanation: "En flyrejse" means "a flight". Do not mix it up with "et fly" (a plane): "Flyet er forsinket" (The plane is delayed). A "flyrejse" is the trip: "Flyrejsen var forsinket" (The flight was delayed).

sentence.da: En **flyrejse** til Spanien tager tre timer.
sentence.en: A flight to Spain takes three hours.

en flytning.explanation: "En flytning" means "a move", as in moving to a new home. It comes from "at flytte" (to move). To say you are moving, use the verb: "Vi flytter i næste uge" (We are moving next week).

sentence.da: Ved en **flytning** pakker man alle sine ting i kasser.
sentence.en: In a move you pack all your things in boxes.

en flyttekasse.explanation: "En flyttekasse" means "a moving box". It is built from "at flytte" (to move) and "en kasse" (a box). "Kasse" also means "checkout" in a shop: "Betal ved kassen" (Pay at the checkout).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker alle bøgerne i en **flyttekasse**.
sentence.en: I pack all the books in a moving box.

en flyverdragt.explanation: "En flyverdragt" means "a snowsuit". The word is "flyver" (a pilot) plus "dragt" (a suit). To talk about the suit a pilot wears, use the same word: "Piloten har en flyverdragt på" (The pilot is wearing a flight suit).

sentence.da: Når det er koldt, får barnet en varm **flyverdragt** på.
sentence.en: When it is cold, the child puts on a warm snowsuit.

en flyvetid.explanation: "En flyvetid" means "a flight time". It is built from "at flyve" (to fly) and "en tid" (a time). "En tid" also means "an appointment", as in "en tid hos lægen" (an appointment with the doctor).

sentence.da: Til London er der kun to timers **flyvetid**.
sentence.en: To London there are only two hours of flight time.

en flåde.explanation: "En flåde" means "a fleet". To talk about the vehicles of a company, say: "en flåde af lastbiler" (a fleet of trucks).

sentence.da: Landets **flåde** består af krigsskibe og ubåde.
sentence.en: The country's navy consists of warships and submarines.

en flåt.explanation: "En flåt" means "a tick", as in the biting animal. In Denmark, ticks can spread an illness called "borreliose" (Lyme disease).

sentence.da: Efter skovturen fandt jeg en **flåt** på min mave.
sentence.en: After the forest trip, I found a tick on my stomach.

en flødebolle.explanation: "En flødebolle" means "a chocolate-covered marshmallow treat". It is a classic Danish sweet. The name is built from "fløde" (cream) and "bolle" (a bun).

sentence.da: En **flødebolle** har et blødt fyld og et lag chokolade udenpå.
sentence.en: A flødebolle has a soft filling and a layer of chocolate on the outside.

en fløjte.explanation: "En fløjte" means "a flute". It also means "a whistle". To talk about a referee, say: "Dommeren blæser i fløjten" (The referee blows the whistle).

sentence.da: Hun spiller **fløjte** i skolens orkester.
sentence.en: She plays the flute in the school orchestra.

en fod.explanation: "En fod" means "a foot", as in the body part. To say your feet hurt, Danish says "the feet" where English says "my feet": "Jeg har ondt i fødderne" (My feet hurt), literally "I have pain in the feet". To say you go on foot, use "til fods": "Han kom til fods" (He came on foot).

sentence.da: Skoen er for lille til min **fod**.
sentence.en: The shoe is too small for my foot.

en fodboldkamp.explanation: "En fodboldkamp" means "a soccer match". It is built from "fodbold" (soccer) and "kamp" (match). The part "kamp" also appears in other sports: "en tenniskamp" (a tennis match).

sentence.da: Vi ser en **fodboldkamp** på tv i aften.
sentence.en: We are watching a soccer match on TV tonight.

en fodboldspiller.explanation: "En fodboldspiller" means "a soccer player". It is built from "fodbold" (soccer) and "spiller" (player). The part "spiller" also appears in "en skakspiller" (a chess player).

sentence.da: En **fodboldspiller** løber efter bolden og scorer mål.
sentence.en: A soccer player runs after the ball and scores goals.

en fodgænger.explanation: "En fodgænger" means "a pedestrian", literally a foot-goer, from "fod" (foot). The first part "fod" also appears in "en fodtur" (a walk on foot).

sentence.da: En **fodgænger** skal vente, når lyset er rødt.
sentence.en: A pedestrian has to wait when the light is red.

en fodgængerzone.explanation: "En fodgængerzone" means "a pedestrian zone". It is built from "en fodgænger" (a pedestrian) and "en zone" (a zone).

sentence.da: Der må ikke køre biler i en **fodgængerzone**.
sentence.en: Cars may not drive in a pedestrian zone.

en fodnote.explanation: "En fodnote" means "a footnote". The name is built from "fod" (a foot) and "note" (a note), because it sits at the foot of the page. To point to one, write: "se fodnote 3" (see footnote 3).

sentence.da: Forklaringen står i en **fodnote** nederst på siden.
sentence.en: The explanation is in a footnote at the bottom of the page.

en fodring.explanation: "En fodring" means "a feeding". It comes from "at fodre" (to feed an animal): "Jeg fodrer hestene" (I feed the horses).

sentence.da: Dyrene får mad ved hver **fodring**.
sentence.en: The animals get food at each feeding.

en fold.explanation: "En fold" means "a fold". The matching verb is "at folde" (to fold): "Jeg folder papiret" (I fold the paper).

sentence.da: Der er en **fold** i papiret, fordi jeg har lagt det sammen.
sentence.en: There is a fold in the paper because I have folded it.

en folkeafstemning.explanation: "En folkeafstemning" means "a referendum". Do not mix it up with "et valg" (an election): "Der er valg i november" (There is an election in November).

sentence.da: Ved en **folkeafstemning** kan alle stemme ja eller nej til et forslag.
sentence.en: In a referendum, everyone can vote yes or no on a proposal.

en folkepension.explanation: "En folkepension" means "a state pension", literally a "people's pension". In Denmark, the amount depends on how many years you have lived in the country.

sentence.da: Man kan få **folkepension**, når man bliver gammel nok.
sentence.en: You can get a state pension when you get old enough.

en folkeskole.explanation: "En folkeskole" means "a primary school". In Denmark, it is the public school for children from about age 6 to 16.

sentence.da: Min søn går i **folkeskole** og har mange venner.
sentence.en: My son goes to primary school and has many friends.

en forandring.explanation: "En forandring" means "a change". The matching verb is "at forandre" (to change): "Jeg vil forandre mit liv" (I want to change my life).

sentence.da: Efter ti år på kontoret vil jeg have en **forandring**.
sentence.en: After ten years at the office I want a change.

en forbandelse.explanation: "En forbandelse" means "a curse". To swear when something goes wrong, use the same word: "Forbandelse!" (Damn!)

sentence.da: Ifølge sagnet hviler der en **forbandelse** over slottet.
sentence.en: According to the legend, a curse rests on the castle.

en forbedring.explanation: "En forbedring" means "an improvement". It comes from "at forbedre" (to improve): "Vi vil forbedre servicen" (We want to improve the service).

sentence.da: Det nye skema er en stor **forbedring**, fordi det er nemmere at læse.
sentence.en: The new schedule is a big improvement because it is easier to read.

en forbindelse.explanation: "En forbindelse" means "a connection". To say a phone or internet connection is bad: "Forbindelsen er dårlig" (The connection is bad). It also means a tie between two things: "Der er en forbindelse mellem søvn og humør" (There is a connection between sleep and mood).

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen **forbindelse** til internettet lige nu.
sentence.en: I have no connection to the internet right now.

en forbinding.explanation: "En forbinding" means "a dressing", as in a bandage for a wound. To ask for one, say: "Jeg har brug for en forbinding" (I need a dressing). Do not mix it up with "et plaster" (a Band-Aid): "Har du et plaster?" (Do you have a Band-Aid?)

sentence.da: Han fik en **forbinding** på armen.
sentence.en: He got a dressing on his arm.

en forbruger.explanation: "En forbruger" means "a consumer". It comes from "at forbruge" (to use up): "Vi forbruger meget strøm" (We use a lot of electricity).

sentence.da: Som **forbruger** kan du klage, hvis varen er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: As a consumer, you can complain if the product has broken.

en forbrydelse.explanation: "En forbrydelse" means "a crime". To say someone commits one, use "at begå" (to commit): "Han begik en forbrydelse" (He committed a crime).

sentence.da: Det er en **forbrydelse** at stjæle fra andre.
sentence.en: It is a crime to steal from others.

en forbryder.explanation: "En forbryder" means "a criminal". It comes from "en forbrydelse" (a crime). To describe an act, use the adjective "kriminel" (criminal): "en kriminel handling" (a criminal act).

sentence.da: Politiet har fanget en farlig **forbryder**.
sentence.en: The police have caught a dangerous criminal.

en fordel.explanation: "En fordel" means "an advantage". To weigh two sides, say: "fordele og ulemper" (advantages and disadvantages).

sentence.da: Det er en **fordel** at bo tæt på arbejde.
sentence.en: It is an advantage to live close to work.

en fordeling.explanation: "En fordeling" means "a distribution". It comes from "at fordele" (to share out): "Vi fordeler arbejdet" (We share out the work).

sentence.da: Der er en skæv **fordeling** af arbejdet i gruppen.
sentence.en: There is an uneven distribution of the work in the group.

en fordom.explanation: "En fordom" means "a prejudice". It is built from "for" (before) and "dom" (judgment). "Dom" also means a court verdict: "Dommen faldt i går" (The verdict came yesterday).

sentence.da: Han har en **fordom** om folk, han aldrig har mødt.
sentence.en: He has a prejudice about people he has never met.

en forelæsning.explanation: "En forelæsning" means "a lecture". To say you are going to one, use: "Jeg skal til forelæsning" (I am going to a lecture).

sentence.da: Studerende lytter og tager noter til en **forelæsning**.
sentence.en: Students listen and take notes at a lecture.

en forening.explanation: "En forening" means "an association". To say you belong to one, say: "Jeg er medlem af en forening" (I am a member of an association).

sentence.da: I en **forening** mødes folk med samme interesse.
sentence.en: In an association, people with the same interest meet.

en forespørgsel.explanation: "En forespørgsel" means "an inquiry". The matching verb is "at forespørge" (to inquire): "Jeg vil gerne forespørge om prisen" (I would like to inquire about the price). To talk about a search in a database, use the same noun: "en forespørgsel" (a query).

sentence.da: Vi har sendt en **forespørgsel** til hotellet om priser.
sentence.en: We sent an inquiry to the hotel about prices.

en forestilling.explanation: "En forestilling" means "a performance". To say you have no idea about something, use the same word: "Jeg har ingen forestilling om det" (I have no idea).

sentence.da: Børnene så en sjov **forestilling** i går.
sentence.en: The children saw a funny show yesterday.

en forfader.explanation: "En forfader" means "an ancestor". It is built from "for" (before) and "fader" (father). In the plural, the vowel changes: "mine forfædre" (my ancestors).

sentence.da: Min **forfader** boede her for længe siden.
sentence.en: My ancestor lived here long ago.

en forfatter.explanation: "En forfatter" means "an author". To say who wrote a book, use "skrevet af" (written by): "Bogen er skrevet af en dansk forfatter" (The book is written by a Danish author).

sentence.da: Hun er **forfatter** og har skrevet tre bøger.
sentence.en: She is an author and has written three books.

en forfremmelse.explanation: "En forfremmelse" means "a promotion", as in a move to a higher job. The matching verb is "at forfremme" (to promote): "Chefen vil forfremme hende" (The boss wants to promote her).

sentence.da: Efter ti år fik hun en **forfremmelse** til afdelingsleder.
sentence.en: After ten years she got a promotion to department head.

en forgænger.explanation: "En forgænger" means "a predecessor". To talk about an earlier version of a thing, use the same word: "Bilen er forgængeren til den nye model" (The car is the predecessor of the new model).

sentence.da: Den nye direktør er mere åben end sin **forgænger**.
sentence.en: The new director is more open than her predecessor.

en forhandler.explanation: "En forhandler" means "a dealer". To say what a dealer sells, put it before the word: "en bilforhandler" (a car dealer). Do not mix it up with "en forhandling" (a negotiation): "Forhandlingen tager lang tid" (The negotiation takes a long time).

sentence.da: En **forhandler** sælger varer fra flere fabrikker til kunderne.
sentence.en: A dealer sells goods from several factories to the customers.

en forhandling.explanation: "En forhandling" means "a negotiation". To say two sides are negotiating, use "i forhandlinger" (in negotiations): "De er i forhandlinger om en ny kontrakt" (They are in negotiations about a new contract).

sentence.da: Efter en lang **forhandling** blev parterne enige om en pris.
sentence.en: After a long negotiation, the parties agreed on a price.

en forhindring.explanation: "En forhindring" means "a hurdle", as in an obstacle. The matching verb is "at forhindre" (to prevent): "Regnen forhindrer os i at spille" (The rain prevents us from playing).

sentence.da: Den største **forhindring** er, at vi mangler tid.
sentence.en: The biggest hurdle is that we are short of time.

en forhøjelse.explanation: "En forhøjelse" means "an increase". To say what rises, put it before the word: "en skatteforhøjelse" (a tax increase).

sentence.da: Efter en **forhøjelse** af huslejen kunne vi ikke blive boende.
sentence.en: After an increase in the rent, we could not stay.

en forklaring.explanation: "En forklaring" means "an explanation". The verb is "at forklare" (to explain): "Kan du forklare opgaven?" (Can you explain the assignment?)

sentence.da: Læreren gav en god **forklaring** på reglen.
sentence.en: The teacher gave a good explanation of the rule.

en forkortelse.explanation: "En forkortelse" means "an abbreviation". Danish examples are "osv." for "og så videre" (and so on) and "FN" for "Forenede Nationer" (the United Nations).

sentence.da: Kl. er en **forkortelse** for klokken.
sentence.en: Kl. is an abbreviation for klokken (the clock).

en forkærlighed.explanation: "En forkærlighed" means "a fondness". The last part "kærlighed" means "love": "Kærlighed gør blind" (Love is blind).

sentence.da: Han har en **forkærlighed** for gamle biler.
sentence.en: He has a fondness for old cars.

en forkølelse.explanation: "En forkølelse" means "a cold", as in the illness. To say you have one, you can also use the adjective "forkølet": "Jeg er forkølet" (I have a cold).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **forkølelse** og ondt i halsen.
sentence.en: I have a cold and a sore throat.

en forlovelse.explanation: "En forlovelse" means "an engagement", as in a promise to marry. To talk about the person you are engaged to, say "min forlovede" (my fiancé or fiancée), the same word for both.

sentence.da: De fejrede deres **forlovelse** med en middag for familien.
sentence.en: They celebrated their engagement with a dinner for the family.

en forlovelsesring.explanation: "En forlovelsesring" means "an engagement ring". It is built from "forlovelse" (engagement) and "ring" (ring). To say someone proposed, use "at fri" (to propose): "Han friede til hende" (He proposed to her).

sentence.da: Han gav hende en **forlovelsesring**, og hun sagde ja.
sentence.en: He gave her an engagement ring, and she said yes.

en forlover.explanation: "En forlover" means "a best man". The same word is used for a woman, as in "a maid of honor": "Hun er min forlover" (She is my maid of honor). Do not mix it up with "en forlovelse" (an engagement): "De fejrer deres forlovelse" (They are celebrating their engagement).

forms.en: a best man / maid of honor
the best men / maids of honor

sentence.da: Min bror skal være **forlover** ved mit bryllup.
sentence.en: My brother will be best man at my wedding.

en forlygte.explanation: "En forlygte" means "a headlight". It is built from "for" (front) and "lygte" (lamp). The part "for" also means "front" in "et forsæde" (a front seat).

sentence.da: Bilens **forlygte** lyser op på vejen.
sentence.en: The car's headlight lights up the road.

en forlystelsespark.explanation: "En forlystelsespark" means "an amusement park". It is built from "en forlystelse" (an amusement) and "en park" (a park).

sentence.da: I en **forlystelsespark** kan man køre i rutsjebane.
sentence.en: In an amusement park you can ride a roller coaster.

en forlængelse.explanation: "En forlængelse" means "an extension", as in more time. To talk about a contract, say: "en forlængelse af kontrakten" (an extension of the contract). Do not mix it up with "en forlængerledning" (an extension cord): "Jeg har brug for en forlængerledning" (I need an extension cord).

sentence.da: Jeg bad om en **forlængelse** af fristen, fordi jeg var syg.
sentence.en: I asked for an extension of the deadline because I was sick.

en forlængerledning.explanation: "En forlængerledning" means "an extension cord". It is built from "forlænge" (to extend) and "ledning" (cord). "Forlænge" also works for time: "at forlænge en aftale" (to extend an agreement).

sentence.da: Der er langt til stikkontakten, men jeg har en **forlængerledning**.
sentence.en: It is a long way to the outlet, but I have an extension cord.

en form.explanation: "En form" means "a shape". To talk about a baking pan, use the same word: "Kagen bages i en form" (The cake is baked in a pan). To say someone is fit, use "i form" (in shape): "Han er i god form" (He is in good shape). Do not mix it up with "en blanket" (a paper form): "Udfyld blanketten" (Fill in the form).

sentence.da: Kagen har en sjov **form**.
sentence.en: The cake has a funny shape.

en formand.explanation: "En formand" means "a chairman". It is built from "for" (in front) and "mand" (man). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to formænd" (two chairmen).

sentence.da: Hun blev valgt til **formand** for foreningen.
sentence.en: She was elected chair of the association.

en formel.explanation: "En formel" means "a formula". To name what it works out, add "for": "formlen for arealet af en cirkel" (the formula for the area of a circle). The "e" disappears when you add an ending: "formlen" (the formula).

sentence.da: I fysik bruger man en **formel** til at regne farten ud.
sentence.en: In physics you use a formula to calculate the speed.

en formidler.explanation: "En formidler" means "a communicator". It also means "an intermediary". To talk about someone who passes things between two sides, say: "Han er formidler mellem kunden og firmaet" (He is the go-between for the customer and the company).

sentence.da: En god **formidler** kan forklare svære ting på en enkel måde.
sentence.en: A good communicator can explain difficult things in a simple way.

en formidling.explanation: "En formidling" means "a communication". It also means "mediation", as in helping two sides find each other. To talk about helping people find a home, use "boligformidling" (housing placement).

sentence.da: Museets **formidling** gør historie levende for børn.
sentence.en: The museum's communication makes history come alive for children.

en formue.explanation: "En formue" means "a fortune". To say something costs a lot, say: "Det koster en formue" (It costs a fortune).

sentence.da: Han tjente en **formue** på at sælge huse.
sentence.en: He earned a fortune by selling houses.

en formular.explanation: "En formular" means "a form". To tell someone to complete one, say: "Udfyld formularen" (Fill in the form). Do not mix it up with "en form" (a shape): "Cirklen har en rund form" (The circle has a round shape).

sentence.da: Du skal udfylde en **formular** med navn og adresse.
sentence.en: You must fill in a form with name and address.

en fornemmelse.explanation: "En fornemmelse" means "a feeling or sense". It comes from the verb "at fornemme" (to sense). To describe a bodily sensation, add "af" (of) and what you feel: "en fornemmelse af kulde" (a sense of cold).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **fornemmelse** af, at han kommer i dag.
sentence.en: I have a feeling he is coming today.

en fornyelse.explanation: "En fornyelse" means "a renewal". It comes from the verb "at fornye" (to renew). To say what is being renewed, add "af" (of): "fornyelse af kontrakten" (renewal of the contract).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have en **fornyelse** af mit pas.
sentence.en: I need a renewal of my passport.

en fornærmelse.explanation: "En fornærmelse" means "an insult". It comes from the verb "at fornærme" (to insult). To say you feel insulted by something, use this phrase: "at tage det som en fornærmelse" (to take it as an insult).

sentence.da: Han kaldte mig dum, og det var en **fornærmelse**.
sentence.en: He called me stupid, and it was an insult.

en fornøjelse.explanation: "En fornøjelse" means "a pleasure". To say you enjoyed meeting someone, say: "Det var en fornøjelse at møde dig" (It was a pleasure to meet you). To answer thanks politely, say: "Tak for hjælpen." "Fornøjelsen er min." (Thanks for the help. The pleasure is mine.)

sentence.da: Det var en **fornøjelse** at arbejde med dig.
sentence.en: It was a pleasure to work with you.

en forpligtelse.explanation: "En forpligtelse" means "an obligation". To say someone does what they have promised or must do, use "at opfylde" (to fulfil): "Firmaet opfylder sine forpligtelser" (The company meets its obligations).

sentence.da: En lejer har en **forpligtelse** til at betale husleje hver måned.
sentence.en: A tenant has an obligation to pay rent every month.

en forret.explanation: "En forret" means "a starter". It is built from "for" (before) and "en ret" (a dish). Do not mix it up with "en forretning" (a business). "En forret" is food: "Forretten er en suppe" (The starter is a soup). "En forretning" is a business: "Han driver en forretning" (He runs a business).

sentence.da: Jeg tager suppe til **forret**.
sentence.en: I will have soup as a starter.

en forretning.explanation: "En forretning" means "a business or shop". To say someone owns or runs one, use "at drive" (to run): "Hun driver en forretning" (She runs a business). When you mean a place where you buy things, it means "a shop": "Der er mange forretninger på gaden" (There are many shops on the street).

sentence.da: Min far har en lille **forretning** i byen.
sentence.en: My father has a small business in town.

en forretningsrejse.explanation: "En forretningsrejse" means "a business trip". It is built from "en forretning" (a business) and "en rejse" (a trip). To say you are away for work, use "på" (on): "Han er på forretningsrejse i Tyskland" (He is on a business trip in Germany).

sentence.da: På en **forretningsrejse** betaler firmaet ofte for hotellet.
sentence.en: On a business trip, the company often pays for the hotel.

en forrude.explanation: "En forrude" means "a windshield". It is built from "for" (front) and "en rude" (a pane of glass). The back window of a car is "en bagrude" (a rear window): "Bagruden er dugget" (The rear window is fogged up).

sentence.da: Der er en lille revne i min **forrude**.
sentence.en: There is a small crack in my windshield.

en forræder.explanation: "En forræder" means "a traitor". It comes from the verb "at forråde" (to betray). To accuse someone of it, use "at kalde" (to call): "Han kaldte hende en forræder" (He called her a traitor).

sentence.da: Den, der sviger sit eget land, er en **forræder**.
sentence.en: Whoever betrays their own country is a traitor.

en forside.explanation: "En forside" means "a front page or front". To say where a story was printed in a newspaper, use "på" (on): "Nyheden var på forsiden" (The news was on the front page). To talk about the front side of a flat object, use it for that side: "forsiden af kortet" (the front of the card).

sentence.da: Der er et billede af et fyrtårn på bogens **forside**.
sentence.en: There is a picture of a lighthouse on the front of the book.

en forsikring.explanation: "En forsikring" means "insurance". To say you take out insurance, use "at tegne" (to take out): "Jeg vil gerne tegne en forsikring" (I would like to take out insurance).

sentence.da: Vi har en **forsikring** på vores hus.
sentence.en: We have insurance on our house.

en forsinkelse.explanation: "En forsinkelse" means "a delay". It comes from the verb "at forsinke" (to delay). To say something is late, use "forsinket" (late): "Bussen er forsinket" (The bus is late).

sentence.da: Toget har en **forsinkelse** på en time.
sentence.en: The train has a delay of one hour.

en forskel.explanation: "En forskel" means "a difference". To say the difference between two things, Danish uses "på" (on) where English says "between": "Der er en stor forskel på kaffe og te" (There is a big difference between coffee and tea). To say something does not matter, use "at gøre" (to make): "Det gør ingen forskel" (It makes no difference).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke se nogen **forskel** på dem.
sentence.en: I can't see any difference between them.

en forsker.explanation: "En forsker" means "a researcher". It comes from the verb "at forske" (to do research). To say which field someone works in, use "i" (in): "Hun er forsker i kræft" (She is a cancer researcher).

sentence.da: En **forsker** undersøger, hvorfor bierne forsvinder.
sentence.en: A researcher investigates why the bees are disappearing.

en forskudsopgørelse.explanation: "En forskudsopgørelse" means "a preliminary income assessment". It is built from "et forskud" (an advance) and "en opgørelse" (a statement). In Denmark, it is the tax authority's estimate of what you will earn this year, and it decides how much tax is taken from your pay each month. To change it, use "at rette" (to correct): "Jeg har rettet min forskudsopgørelse" (I have corrected my preliminary income assessment).

sentence.da: I en **forskudsopgørelse** skriver man, hvor meget man tror, man tjener.
sentence.en: In a preliminary income assessment you write how much you think you will earn.

en forsoning.explanation: "En forsoning" means "a reconciliation". It comes from the verb "at forsone" (to reconcile). To say someone makes peace with another person, add "sig" (oneself): "Hun har forsonet sig med sin far" (She has made peace with her father).

sentence.da: Efter krigen kom der en **forsoning** mellem de to lande.
sentence.en: After the war there was a reconciliation between the two countries.

en forstad.explanation: "En forstad" means "a suburb". It is built from "for" (in front of) and "en stad" (a town). The plural changes the vowel: "forstæder" (suburbs).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **forstad** uden for København.
sentence.en: We live in a suburb outside Copenhagen.

en forstand.explanation: "En forstand" means "a mind or sense". To say "in a way", use "i en vis forstand": "I en vis forstand har du ret" (In a way, you are right). To say someone has lost their mind, use "at miste" (to lose): "Han har mistet forstanden" (He has lost his mind).

forms.en: in the true meaning of the word

sentence.da: Hun har **forstand** på biler og kan hurtigt finde fejlen.
sentence.en: She knows a lot about cars and can quickly find the fault.

en forstuvning.explanation: "En forstuvning" means "a sprain". It comes from the verb "at forstuve" (to sprain). To say you sprained a joint, use that verb: "Jeg har forstuvet min ankel" (I have sprained my ankle).

sentence.da: Hun fik en **forstuvning** og kan ikke gå.
sentence.en: She got a sprain and cannot walk.

en forståelse.explanation: "En forståelse" means "an understanding". To say you know a subject well, add "af" (of): "Jeg har en god forståelse af reglerne" (I have a good understanding of the rules). To say two sides understand each other, use "gensidig" (mutual): "Der er en gensidig forståelse mellem dem" (There is a mutual understanding between them).

sentence.da: Tak for din **forståelse**, mens vi løser problemet.
sentence.en: Thanks for your understanding while we solve the problem.

en forsvarsspiller.explanation: "En forsvarsspiller" means "a defender". It is built from "forsvar" (defense) and "en spiller" (a player). To name the player who tries to score, use "en angriber" (an attacker): "Angriberen scorede to mål" (The attacker scored two goals).

sentence.da: En **forsvarsspiller** skal passe på, at modstanderen ikke scorer.
sentence.en: A defender must make sure the opponent does not score.

en forsyning.explanation: "En forsyning" means "a supply". It comes from the verb "at forsyne" (to supply). To talk about stored goods such as food and fuel, use the plural: "Vi har forsyninger til en uge" (We have supplies for a week).

sentence.da: Byen får en stabil **forsyning** af rent vand fra værket.
sentence.en: The town gets a stable supply of clean water from the plant.

en fortaler.explanation: "En fortaler" means "an advocate". It is built from "for" (for) and "en taler" (a speaker). To name the cause someone supports, add "for": "en fortaler for gratis skolemad" (an advocate for free school meals).

sentence.da: Hun er en stærk **fortaler** for flere cykelstier i byen.
sentence.en: She is a strong advocate for more bike lanes in the city.

en fortid.explanation: "En fortid" means "a past". It is built from "for" (before) and "en tid" (a time). To say how things were earlier, use "i fortiden" (in the past): "I fortiden boede man anderledes" (In the past people lived differently).

sentence.da: Han taler ikke om sin **fortid**.
sentence.en: He does not talk about his past.

en fortjeneste.explanation: "En fortjeneste" means "a profit or merit". It comes from the verb "at fortjene" (to deserve). To say a shop makes money, use "give" (to give): "Butikken giver en god fortjeneste" (The shop makes a good profit). When you give someone credit for a good result, it means "merit": "Det er hendes fortjeneste, at vi vandt" (We won thanks to her).

sentence.da: Efter udgifterne er der en **fortjeneste** på tusind kroner.
sentence.en: After the costs there is a profit of a thousand kroner.

en fortolkning.explanation: "En fortolkning" means "an interpretation". It comes from the verb "at fortolke" (to interpret). To say people understand the same thing in different ways, use the plural: "Der er flere fortolkninger af loven" (There are several interpretations of the law).

sentence.da: Hver elev har sin egen **fortolkning** af digtet.
sentence.en: Each student has their own interpretation of the poem.

en fortsættelse.explanation: "En fortsættelse" means "a continuation". It comes from the verb "at fortsætte" (to continue). At the end of a story told in parts, you read "Fortsættelse følger" (To be continued).

sentence.da: Filmen er en **fortsættelse** af den, vi så sidste år.
sentence.en: The film is a continuation of the one we saw last year.

en fortælling.explanation: "En fortælling" means "a story or narrative". It comes from the verb "at fortælle" (to tell). To say what a story is about, use "om" (about): "en fortælling om krigen" (a story about the war). Do not mix it up with "historie" (history), the school subject: "Jeg har historie i dag" (I have history today).

sentence.da: En **fortælling** kan være sand eller opfundet.
sentence.en: A story can be true or invented.

en forudsigelse.explanation: "En forudsigelse" means "a prediction". It comes from the verb "at forudsige" (to predict). To say you predict something, use the verb: "Ingen kan forudsige fremtiden" (No one can predict the future).

sentence.da: Hans **forudsigelse** viste sig at være rigtig.
sentence.en: His prediction turned out to be right.

en forudsætning.explanation: "En forudsætning" means "a precondition". To say "on the condition that", use "på den forudsætning, at": "Vi kommer på den forudsætning, at det er gratis" (We will come on the condition that it is free). When you talk about what someone brings to a task, use the plural: "Hun har gode forudsætninger for at blive læge" (She has what it takes to become a doctor).

sentence.da: Tillid er en **forudsætning** for et godt samarbejde.
sentence.en: Trust is a precondition for good cooperation.

en forvaltning.explanation: "En forvaltning" means "an administration". It comes from the verb "at forvalte" (to manage). To say someone looks after money or property for another person, use "forvaltning af" (management of): "forvaltning af en arv" (management of an inheritance).

sentence.da: Byens **forvaltning** styrer skoler, veje og biblioteker.
sentence.en: The city's administration runs schools, roads and libraries.

en forventning.explanation: "En forventning" means "an expectation". It comes from the verb "at forvente" (to expect). To say something was as good as people hoped, use this phrase: "Filmen levede op til forventningerne" (The film lived up to expectations).

sentence.da: Min **forventning** er, at det bliver en god dag.
sentence.en: My expectation is that it will be a good day.

en forværring.explanation: "En forværring" means "a worsening". It comes from the verb "at forværre" (to make worse). To say an illness has got worse, use the verb: "Hans sygdom er blevet forværret" (His illness has got worse).

sentence.da: Lægen frygter en **forværring**, hvis patienten ikke tager medicinen.
sentence.en: The doctor fears a worsening if the patient does not take the medicine.

en forårsdag.explanation: "En forårsdag" means "a spring day". It is built from "forår" (spring) and "dag" (day). To say something happens in spring, use "i foråret" (in the spring): "Blomsterne springer ud i foråret" (The flowers open in the spring).

sentence.da: Det er en dejlig **forårsdag**, og solen skinner.
sentence.en: It is a lovely spring day, and the sun is shining.

en forælder.explanation: "En forælder" means "a parent". The plural "forældre" is also part of "et forældremøde" (a parents' meeting at school) and "bedsteforældre" (grandparents): "Der er forældremøde i morgen" (There is a parents' meeting tomorrow).

sentence.da: Som **forælder** vil man det bedste for sit barn.
sentence.en: As a parent you want the best for your child.

en fotobog.explanation: "En fotobog" means "a photo book". It is built from "foto" (photo) and "en bog" (a book). To say you made one, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg har lavet en fotobog fra ferien" (I have made a photo book from the holiday).

sentence.da: I en **fotobog** samler man sine egne billeder fra en rejse.
sentence.en: In a photo book you collect your own pictures from a trip.

en fotograf.explanation: "En fotograf" means "a photographer". It comes from the verb "at fotografere" (to photograph). To show how the two words fit together: "Fotografen fotograferede brudeparret" (The photographer photographed the bride and groom).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **fotograf** til brylluppet.
sentence.en: We need a photographer for the wedding.

en frakke.explanation: "En frakke" means "a coat". To say you hang up your coat, use "at hænge op" (to hang up): "Hæng din frakke i garderoben" (Hang your coat in the cloakroom).

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **frakke** på i kulden.
sentence.en: I put my coat on in the cold.

en franskmand.explanation: "En franskmand" means "a Frenchman". It is built from "fransk" (French) and "en mand" (a man). To say where he comes from, use the country, "Frankrig" (France): "Han kommer fra Frankrig" (He comes from France).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **franskmand**, og han bager godt brød.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a Frenchman, and he bakes good bread.

en fredagsbar.explanation: "En fredagsbar" means "a Friday bar". It is built from "fredag" (Friday) and "en bar" (a bar). In Denmark, it is a weekly get-together on Friday afternoon at a workplace or a university. To ask someone to come, use "med til" (along to): "Skal du med til fredagsbar?" (Are you coming to Friday bar?)

sentence.da: Hver fredag mødes kollegerne til **fredagsbar** på kontoret.
sentence.en: Every Friday the coworkers meet for Friday bar at the office.

en fredsaftale.explanation: "En fredsaftale" means "a peace agreement". It is built from "fred" (peace) and "en aftale" (an agreement). To say both sides signed it, use "at underskrive" (to sign): "De to lande underskrev en fredsaftale" (The two countries signed a peace agreement).

sentence.da: En **fredsaftale** afslutter en krig mellem to lande.
sentence.en: A peace agreement ends a war between two countries.

en fregne.explanation: "En fregne" means "a freckle". To say someone has freckles, use the plural: "Hun har fregner i ansigtet" (She has freckles on her face). The adjective is "fregnet" (freckled): "en fregnet dreng" (a freckled boy).

sentence.da: En **fregne** er en lille brun prik på huden.
sentence.en: A freckle is a small brown dot on the skin.

en frekvens.explanation: "En frekvens" means "a frequency". To describe a high or low sound or signal, use "høj" (high) or "lav" (low): "en lav frekvens" (a low frequency).

sentence.da: Radioen sender på en bestemt **frekvens**.
sentence.en: The radio broadcasts on a certain frequency.

en frelser.explanation: "En frelser" means "a savior". It comes from the verb "at frelse" (to save).

sentence.da: Folket kaldte ham deres **frelser**, fordi han reddede byen.
sentence.en: The people called him their savior because he saved the town.

en fremgangsmåde.explanation: "En fremgangsmåde" means "a procedure". It is built from "fremgang" (progress) and "en måde" (a way). To say you follow the steps, use "at følge" (to follow): "Følg den rigtige fremgangsmåde" (Follow the correct procedure).

sentence.da: Manualen forklarer trin for trin, hvad den rigtige **fremgangsmåde** er.
sentence.en: The manual explains step by step what the right procedure is.

en fremlæggelse.explanation: "En fremlæggelse" means "a presentation (of results)". It is built from the verb "at fremlægge" (to put forward). To say you have one scheduled, use "have" (to have): "Vi har fremlæggelse i morgen" (We have a presentation tomorrow).

sentence.da: Efter gruppearbejdet har hver gruppe en kort **fremlæggelse** for klassen.
sentence.en: After the group work, each group gives a short presentation for the class.

en fremmed.explanation: "En fremmed" means "a stranger". To warn a child, say: "Tal ikke med fremmede" (Do not talk to strangers). When "fremmed" describes a noun, it means "foreign": "et fremmed land" (a foreign country).

sentence.da: En **fremmed** bankede på døren i aftes.
sentence.en: A stranger knocked on the door last night.

en fremstilling.explanation: "En fremstilling" means "a production or portrayal". It comes from the verb "at fremstille" (to make). When you talk about making goods, it means "production": "Fremstilling af ost tager tid" (Making cheese takes time). When you talk about how something is shown, it means "portrayal": "Avisens fremstilling af sagen var forkert" (The newspaper's portrayal of the case was wrong).

sentence.da: Bogens **fremstilling** af krigen er meget levende og detaljeret.
sentence.en: The book's portrayal of the war is very vivid and detailed.

en fremtid.explanation: "En fremtid" means "a future". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "en tid" (a time). To say something will happen later in life, use "i fremtiden" (in the future): "I fremtiden vil jeg bo i udlandet" (In the future I want to live abroad).

sentence.da: Børnene skal have en god **fremtid**.
sentence.en: The children should have a good future.

en fremvisning.explanation: "En fremvisning" means "a showing or display". It comes from the verb "at fremvise" (to show). To say a home is shown to buyers, use "en visning" (a viewing) instead: "Vi har visning på lørdag" (We have a viewing on Saturday).

sentence.da: Museet holder en **fremvisning** af de nye malerier i morgen.
sentence.en: The museum is holding a showing of the new paintings tomorrow.

en fridag.explanation: "En fridag" means "a day off". It is built from "fri" (free) and "en dag" (a day). To say you are off today, use "fri" alone: "Jeg har fri i dag" (I am off today).

sentence.da: Min mand har **fridag** på onsdag.
sentence.en: My husband has a day off on Wednesday.

en frihed.explanation: "En frihed" means "a freedom". The word is the last part of "ytringsfrihed" (freedom of speech): "Der er ytringsfrihed i Danmark" (There is freedom of speech in Denmark).

sentence.da: Børn har brug for **frihed** til at lege.
sentence.en: Children need freedom to play.

en frikadelle.explanation: "En frikadelle" means "a meatball". In Denmark, it is a flat fried patty, eaten hot with potatoes or cold on rye bread.

sentence.da: Han steger en **frikadelle** af svinekød i panden.
sentence.en: He fries a pork meatball in the pan.

en frist.explanation: "En frist" means "a deadline". To talk about meeting or extending a deadline, use these verbs: "at overholde en frist" (to meet a deadline) and "at forlænge en frist" (to extend a deadline).

sentence.da: Sidste **frist** for at aflevere opgaven er fredag.
sentence.en: The final deadline for handing in the assignment is Friday.

en frisure.explanation: "En frisure" means "a hairstyle". Use it for the cut and the styling together. A haircut, "en klipning", is only the cutting: "Jeg har tid til en klipning" (I have an appointment for a haircut).

sentence.da: En kort **frisure** er nemmere at passe end langt hår.
sentence.en: A short hairstyle is easier to take care of than long hair.

en frisør.explanation: "En frisør" means "a hairdresser". It also means the place where you get a haircut: "Jeg har tid hos frisøren" (I have an appointment at the hairdresser's).

sentence.da: Jeg skal til **frisør** i morgen.
sentence.en: I am going to the hairdresser tomorrow.

en frisørsalon.explanation: "En frisørsalon" means "a hair salon". It is built from "frisør" (hairdresser) and "en salon" (a salon). To book a visit, use "at bestille tid" (to book an appointment): "Jeg har bestilt tid til torsdag" (I have booked an appointment for Thursday).

sentence.da: Hun får klippet håret i en **frisørsalon**.
sentence.en: She gets her hair cut at a hair salon.

en fritidsaktivitet.explanation: "En fritidsaktivitet" means "a leisure activity". It is built from "fritid" (free time) and "en aktivitet" (an activity). To ask what someone does in their free time, say: "Hvad laver du i din fritid?" (What do you do in your free time?)

sentence.da: Fodbold er en populær **fritidsaktivitet** for børn efter skole.
sentence.en: Soccer is a popular leisure activity for children after school.

en fritidsordning.explanation: "En fritidsordning" means "an after-school program". It is built from "fritid" (free time) and "en ordning" (an arrangement). In Denmark, the best-known kind is "SFO" (short for "skolefritidsordning"), for the youngest school children: "Min søn er i SFO" (My son is in SFO).

sentence.da: Efter skole går han i **fritidsordning**, til hans far har fri.
sentence.en: After school he goes to an after-school program until his father is off work.

en frivillig.explanation: "En frivillig" means "a volunteer". To say something is not required, use the adjective: "Det er frivilligt" (It is voluntary).

sentence.da: En **frivillig** arbejder uden løn for en god sag.
sentence.en: A volunteer works without pay for a good cause.

en frokostpause.explanation: "En frokostpause" means "a lunch break". It is built from "frokost" (lunch) and "en pause" (a break). To say someone is on their lunch break, use "i" (in): "Hun er i frokostpause" (She is on her lunch break).

sentence.da: Vi holder **frokostpause** klokken tolv.
sentence.en: We take our lunch break at twelve.

en front.explanation: "En front" means "a front". When you talk about war, it means the line where two armies fight: "Soldaterne er ved fronten" (The soldiers are at the front).

sentence.da: Når en kold **front** kommer, falder temperaturen hurtigt.
sentence.en: When a cold front arrives, the temperature drops quickly.

en frugt.explanation: "En frugt" means "a fruit". When you talk about fruit as food in general, say "frugt" without an article: "Jeg spiser meget frugt" (I eat a lot of fruit). To count single pieces, use "et stykke frugt" (a piece of fruit): "Jeg tager et stykke frugt" (I will take a piece of fruit).

sentence.da: Æbler og bananer er **frugt**.
sentence.en: Apples and bananas are fruit.

en frugthave.explanation: "En frugthave" means "an orchard". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en have" (a garden). Do not mix up the verb "at have" (to have) and "en have" (a garden): "Vi har en have" (We have a garden).

sentence.da: Der vokser mange æbler i vores **frugthave**.
sentence.en: Many apples grow in our orchard.

en frugtplantage.explanation: "En frugtplantage" means "an orchard". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en plantage" (a plantation). To say you pick fruit there, use "at plukke" (to pick): "Vi plukker kirsebær i frugtplantagen" (We pick cherries in the orchard).

sentence.da: I en **frugtplantage** dyrker man æbler og kirsebær til salg.
sentence.en: In an orchard you grow apples and cherries for sale.

en frugtsalat.explanation: "En frugtsalat" means "a fruit salad". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en salat" (a salad). To say you have it as the last course, use "til dessert" (for dessert): "Vi får frugtsalat til dessert" (We are having fruit salad for dessert).

sentence.da: Hun laver en **frugtsalat** med æbler og bananer.
sentence.en: She makes a fruit salad with apples and bananas.

en frugtskål.explanation: "En frugtskål" means "a fruit bowl". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en skål" (a bowl). The word "skål" is also what you say when you raise a glass: "Skål!" (Cheers!)

sentence.da: Der ligger tre æbler i en **frugtskål**.
sentence.en: There are three apples in a fruit bowl.

en frustration.explanation: "En frustration" means "a frustration". It is related to the adjective "frustreret" (frustrated): "Jeg er frustreret over trafikken" (I am frustrated about the traffic).

sentence.da: Det er en stor **frustration**, når bussen er forsinket.
sentence.en: It is a big frustration when the bus is late.

en frysepose.explanation: "En frysepose" means "a freezer bag". It is built from "at fryse" (to freeze) and "en pose" (a bag). To describe food that is in the freezer, use "frossen" (frozen): "frossen fisk" (frozen fish).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger brødet i en **frysepose** og fryser det.
sentence.en: I put the bread in a freezer bag and freeze it.

en fryser.explanation: "En fryser" means "a freezer". Do not mix it up with the verb "at fryse" (to be cold): "Jeg fryser" (I am cold). "En fryser" is the appliance: "Der er is i fryseren" (There is ice cream in the freezer).

sentence.da: Maden holder sig længe i en **fryser**.
sentence.en: Food keeps for a long time in a freezer.

en frø.explanation: "En frø" means "a frog". It takes "en", as the form "frøen" shows. Do not mix it up with "et frø" (a seed): "Jeg lægger et frø i jorden" (I put a seed in the soil).

sentence.da: En **frø** hopper rundt ved søen og kvækker.
sentence.en: A frog hops around by the lake and croaks.

en frøken.explanation: "En frøken" means "a miss or young lady". To use it as a title before a last name, write: "frøken Hansen" (Miss Hansen).

sentence.da: Hun er ugift og hedder derfor **frøken** Larsen i den gamle bog.
sentence.en: She is unmarried and is therefore called Miss Larsen in the old book.

en frøpose.explanation: "En frøpose" means "a seed packet". It is built from "et frø" (a seed) and "en pose" (a bag). Do not mix up "et frø" (a seed) with "en frø" (a frog). "Et frø": "Jeg lægger et frø i jorden" (I put a seed in the soil). "En frø": "En frø sidder ved søen" (A frog sits by the lake).

sentence.da: Jeg købte en **frøpose** til haven i dag.
sentence.en: I bought a seed packet for the garden today.

en fugl.explanation: "En fugl" means "a bird". The word "fugl" is also part of "en fuglekasse" (a birdhouse): "Vi har sat en fuglekasse op" (We have put up a birdhouse).

sentence.da: Der sidder en **fugl** i træet og synger.
sentence.en: A bird is sitting in the tree and singing.

en fuglekasse.explanation: "En fuglekasse" means "a birdhouse". It is built from "en fugl" (a bird) and "en kasse" (a box). To say birds live in one, use "bo i" (live in): "Fuglene bor i fuglekassen" (The birds live in the birdhouse).

sentence.da: Vi hængte en **fuglekasse** op i et træ i haven.
sentence.en: We hung a birdhouse up in a tree in the garden.

en fugletur.explanation: "En fugletur" means "a birdwatching trip". It is built from "fugl" (bird) and "en tur" (a trip). To say you go for a walk, use "tur" alone: "at gå en tur" (to go for a walk).

sentence.da: Vi tog på **fugletur** med kikkert tidligt om morgenen.
sentence.en: We went on a birdwatching trip with binoculars early in the morning.

en fugleunge.explanation: "En fugleunge" means "a baby bird". It is built from "en fugl" (a bird) and "en unge" (a young one). The last part is also used for the young of other animals: "en andeunge" (a duckling).

sentence.da: Den lille **fugleunge** sidder i reden og piber.
sentence.en: The little baby bird sits in the nest and chirps.

en fuldmåne.explanation: "En fuldmåne" means "a full moon". It is built from "fuld" (full) and "en måne" (a moon). To say tonight has one, leave out "en": "I nat er det fuldmåne" (Tonight there is a full moon).

sentence.da: Natten er lys, når der er **fuldmåne**.
sentence.en: The night is bright when there is a full moon.

en funktion.explanation: "En funktion" means "a function". To say a machine does not work, use "ude af funktion" (out of order): "Elevatoren er ude af funktion" (The lift is out of order).

sentence.da: Knappen har en vigtig **funktion**.
sentence.en: The button has an important function.

en fusion.explanation: "En fusion" means "a merger". It is related to the verb "at fusionere" (to merge): "De to banker fusionerer" (The two banks are merging). When you talk about physics, it means "fusion": "kernefusion" (nuclear fusion).

sentence.da: Bankerne har fået ét navn efter en **fusion**.
sentence.en: The banks have been given one name after a merger.

en fyldning.explanation: "En fyldning" means "a filling". It comes from the verb "at fylde" (to fill). When you talk about food, it means the soft part inside a cake or chocolate: "en fyldning af flødeskum" (a filling of whipped cream).

sentence.da: Jeg har fået en **fyldning**, fordi tanden havde et hul.
sentence.en: I got a filling because the tooth had a hole.

en fynbo.explanation: "En fynbo" means "a person from Funen". It is built from "Fyn" (Funen) and "-bo" (a resident). The island is called "Fyn" in Danish: "Jeg bor på Fyn" (I live on Funen).

sentence.da: Hun er **fynbo** og bor i Odense.
sentence.en: She is from Funen and lives in Odense.

en fyr.explanation: "En fyr" means "a guy". It is a casual word: "Han er en flink fyr" (He is a nice guy). The neutral word is "en mand" (a man): "Der står en mand ved døren" (A man is standing at the door). Do not mix it up with "et fyr" (a lighthouse): "Fyret lyser om natten" (The lighthouse shines at night).

sentence.da: Min bror er en rigtig sjov **fyr**.
sentence.en: My brother is a really funny guy.

en fyring.explanation: "En fyring" means "a dismissal". It comes from the verb "at fyre" (to fire someone). When you talk about heating a house, "fyring" means "heating": "olie til fyring" (oil for heating).

sentence.da: Efter en **fyring** har man ikke længere et job.
sentence.en: After a dismissal you no longer have a job.

en fysiker.explanation: "En fysiker" means "a physicist". It comes from "fysik" (physics). To say what someone studies, use "at læse" (to study): "Hun læser fysik" (She studies physics).

sentence.da: En **fysiker** undersøger, hvordan lys og lyd bevæger sig.
sentence.en: A physicist studies how light and sound move.

en fysioterapeut.explanation: "En fysioterapeut" means "a physiotherapist". To say you go for treatment, use "gå til" (go to): "Jeg går til fysioterapeut hver torsdag" (I go to the physiotherapist every Thursday).

sentence.da: En **fysioterapeut** viser dig øvelser, som gør din ryg stærkere.
sentence.en: A physiotherapist shows you exercises that make your back stronger.

en fåreflok.explanation: "En fåreflok" means "a flock of sheep". It is built from "får" (sheep) and "en flok" (a flock). To talk about a group of people, use "flok" alone: "en flok børn" (a group of children).

sentence.da: Der går en stor **fåreflok** på marken.
sentence.en: A big flock of sheep is walking on the field.

en fælde.explanation: "En fælde" means "a trap". When you mean a trap for animals, put the animal first: "en musefælde" (a mousetrap). When you mean a trick set for a person, use "at gå i fælden" (to fall into the trap): "Han gik i fælden" (He fell into the trap).

sentence.da: Han stillede en **fælde** op for musen.
sentence.en: He set up a trap for the mouse.

en fællesspisning.explanation: "En fællesspisning" means "a communal dinner". It is built from "fælles" (shared) and "at spise" (to eat). To invite someone, use "til" (to): "Kom til fællesspisning i aften" (Come to the communal dinner tonight).

sentence.da: Hver torsdag laver vi mad sammen til en **fællesspisning**.
sentence.en: Every Thursday we cook together for a communal dinner.

en færd.explanation: "En færd" means "a journey or conduct". To say you are in the middle of doing something, use "i færd med at" (in the middle of doing): "Jeg er i færd med at lave mad" (I am in the middle of cooking). To say people are out and about, use "på færde" (about): "Der er tyve på færde" (There are thieves about).

sentence.da: Hun er i **færd** med at pakke, fordi toget kører om en time.
sentence.en: She is in the middle of packing because the train leaves in an hour.

en færdighed.explanation: "En færdighed" means "a skill". It is built from "færdig" (finished, ready). To say what someone is good at, use "færdigheder i" (skills in): "Hun har gode færdigheder i matematik" (She has good skills in maths).

sentence.da: Det er en vigtig **færdighed** at kunne svømme.
sentence.en: It is an important skill to be able to swim.

en færdselsregel.explanation: "En færdselsregel" means "a traffic rule". It is built from "færdsel" (traffic) and "en regel" (a rule). To say someone breaks the rules, use "at overtræde" (to break): "Han overtrådte færdselsreglerne" (He broke the traffic rules).

sentence.da: At stoppe ved rødt lys er en **færdselsregel**.
sentence.en: Stopping at a red light is a traffic rule.

en færge.explanation: "En færge" means "a ferry". To say you travel by ferry, use "med" (by): "Vi sejler med færgen til Bornholm" (We sail by ferry to Bornholm).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **færge** over til øen.
sentence.en: We take a ferry over to the island.

en fætter.explanation: "En fætter" means "a male cousin". Danish has a separate word for a female cousin, "en kusine": "Min kusine bor i Odense" (My female cousin lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **fætter** er søn af min mors bror.
sentence.en: My cousin is the son of my mother's brother.

en fødegang.explanation: "En fødegang" means "a maternity ward". It comes from the verb "at føde" (to give birth). To say where a woman is, use "på" (in): "Hun er på fødegangen" (She is in the maternity ward).

sentence.da: Barnet kommer til verden på sygehusets **fødegang**.
sentence.en: The child comes into the world in the hospital's maternity ward.

en fødevare.explanation: "En fødevare" means "a food item". It is built from "føde" (food) and "en vare" (a product). The Danish food authority is called "Fødevarestyrelsen" (the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration).

sentence.da: En **fødevare** er noget, man kan spise eller drikke.
sentence.en: A food item is something you can eat or drink.

en fødsel.explanation: "En fødsel" means "a birth". It comes from the verb "at føde" (to give birth). It is also the first part of "fødselsdag" (birthday): "Min fødselsdag er i maj" (My birthday is in May).

sentence.da: Ved en **fødsel** kommer et barn til verden.
sentence.en: At a birth, a child comes into the world.

en fødselsdag.explanation: "En fødselsdag" means "a birthday". It is built from "en fødsel" (a birth) and "en dag" (a day). To say it is your birthday, use "have" (to have): "Jeg har fødselsdag" (literally, "I have birthday"). To congratulate someone, say: "Tillykke med fødselsdagen!" (Happy birthday!)

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fødselsdag** og får kage.
sentence.en: Today is my birthday, and I get cake.

en fødselsdagsfest.explanation: "En fødselsdagsfest" means "a birthday party". It is built from "fødselsdag" (birthday) and "en fest" (a party). To invite someone, use "at invitere til" (to invite to): "Jeg inviterer dig til fødselsdagsfest" (I invite you to a birthday party).

sentence.da: Vi har **fødselsdagsfest** med kage og gaver.
sentence.en: We have a birthday party with cake and presents.

en fødselsdagsgave.explanation: "En fødselsdagsgave" means "a birthday present". It is built from "en fødselsdag" (a birthday) and "en gave" (a gift). To name a gift for a wedding, use the same ending: "en bryllupsgave" (a wedding gift).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **fødselsdagsgave** til min mor.
sentence.en: I am buying a birthday present for my mother.

en fødselsdagskage.explanation: "En fødselsdagskage" means "a birthday cake". It is built from "en fødselsdag" (a birthday) and "en kage" (a cake). The word "kage" also appears in "en småkage" (a cookie).

sentence.da: En **fødselsdagskage** har ofte lys på.
sentence.en: A birthday cake often has candles on it.

en fødselsdato.explanation: "En fødselsdato" means "a date of birth". It is easy to mix up with "en fødselsdag" (a birthday). To give the date you were born on a form, use "fødselsdato": "Skriv din fødselsdato her" (Write your date of birth here). To talk about the yearly celebration, use "fødselsdag": "I dag har jeg fødselsdag" (Today is my birthday).

sentence.da: Min **fødselsdato** er 12. marts 1990.
sentence.en: My date of birth is March 12, 1990.

en følelse.explanation: "En følelse" means "a feeling", as in an emotion. When you have a hunch about something, use it with "af" (of): "Jeg har en følelse af, at det går godt" (I have a feeling that it will go well).

sentence.da: Kærlighed er en stærk **følelse**.
sentence.en: Love is a strong feeling.

en følelse af lettelse.explanation: "En følelse af lettelse" means "a sense of relief". It is built from "en følelse" (a feeling), "af" (of) and "lettelse" (relief). To name another feeling the same way, put it after "af": "en følelse af sikkerhed" (a feeling of safety).

sentence.da: Der kom en **følelse af lettelse**, da prøven var slut.
sentence.en: A sense of relief came when the test was over.

en følger.explanation: "En følger" means "a follower", as in a person who follows your account online. It comes from the verb "at følge" (to follow). To say someone has many followers: "Hun har mange følgere" (She has many followers).

sentence.da: En **følger** kan se alle dine opslag.
sentence.en: A follower can see all your posts.

en føljeton.explanation: "En føljeton" means "a serial", as in a story published in parts. It is also used for a matter that keeps dragging on. To say a case has dragged on like that: "Sagen er blevet en rigtig føljeton" (The case has become a real saga).

sentence.da: En **føljeton** i avisen kommer i små dele, én hver dag.
sentence.en: A serial in the newspaper comes in small parts, one each day.

en føntørrer.explanation: "En føntørrer" means "a hairdryer". To say you blow-dry your hair, use the verb "at føne" (to blow-dry): "Jeg føner mit hår" (I blow-dry my hair).

sentence.da: Mit hår er vådt, og jeg bruger en **føntørrer**.
sentence.en: My hair is wet, and I am using a hairdryer.

et fad.explanation: "Et fad" means "a dish", as in a serving dish for the table. To say what is on the table, use it for the serving dish: "Der står et fad med kartofler på bordet" (There is a dish of potatoes on the table). Do not mix it up with "en tallerken" (a plate), which you eat from: "Jeg lægger maden på tallerkenen" (I put the food on the plate).

sentence.da: Hun lægger kødet på et **fad**.
sentence.en: She puts the meat on a dish.

et fadøl.explanation: "Et fadøl" means "a draft beer". It is built from "fad" (a barrel) and "øl" (beer).

sentence.da: Vi tager hver et **fadøl** i baren.
sentence.en: We each have a draft beer at the bar.

et fag.explanation: "Et fag" means "a subject", as in a subject you study at school. To say which one you like best, put "yndlings-" (favorite) in front: "Mit yndlingsfag er historie" (My favorite subject is history).

sentence.da: Matematik er et svært **fag**, men jeg kan lide det.
sentence.en: Math is a hard subject, but I like it.

et fagområde.explanation: "Et fagområde" means "a field of study". It is built from "et fag" (a subject) and "et område" (an area). To say something is outside what you know, use it after "uden for" (outside): "Det ligger uden for mit fagområde" (That is outside my field).

sentence.da: Hun ved meget om sit **fagområde**, som er historie.
sentence.en: She knows a lot about her field, which is history.

et faktum.explanation: "Et faktum" means "a fact". A very common phrase is "Faktum er, at" (The fact is that). To make a strong point, start with it: "Faktum er, at vi ikke har penge nok" (The fact is that we do not have enough money).

sentence.da: Det er et **faktum**, at vand koger ved hundrede grader.
sentence.en: It is a fact that water boils at a hundred degrees.

et fald.explanation: "Et fald" means "a fall or drop". It comes from the verb "at falde" (to fall). When someone falls down, say "et fald fra stigen" (a fall from the ladder). When a number goes down, say "et fald i priserne" (a drop in prices).

sentence.da: Der har været et stort **fald** i temperaturen.
sentence.en: There has been a big drop in temperature.

et familiebillede.explanation: "Et familiebillede" means "a family photo". It is built from "en familie" (a family) and "et billede" (a picture). To say who is in a picture, use "af" (of): "Jeg har et billede af min søster" (I have a picture of my sister).

sentence.da: Der hænger et **familiebillede** over sofaen.
sentence.en: A family photo hangs over the sofa.

et familiemedlem.explanation: "Et familiemedlem" means "a family member". "Et medlem" is also used for a member of a club: "et medlem af klubben" (a member of the club).

sentence.da: Hvert **familiemedlem** fik en gave.
sentence.en: Every family member got a gift.

et fartkamera.explanation: "Et fartkamera" means "a speed camera". It is built from "fart" (speed) and "et kamera" (a camera). The word "fart" also appears in "høj fart" (high speed): "Han kørte i høj fart" (He drove at high speed).

sentence.da: Jeg bremser, fordi der er et **fartkamera** ved vejen.
sentence.en: I brake because there is a speed camera by the road.

et fartøj.explanation: "Et fartøj" means "a vessel", as in a ship or aircraft. The word is also the last part of "et luftfartøj" (an aircraft) and "et rumfartøj" (a spacecraft).

sentence.da: Et **fartøj** kan være et skib, et fly eller en rumraket.
sentence.en: A vessel can be a ship, a plane or a space rocket.

et felt.explanation: "Et felt" means "a field", as in a box on a form or an area of work. When you fill in a form, use it for the box: "Skriv navnet i feltet" (Write the name in the field). When you talk about the area someone works in, use it for that area: "Hun arbejder inden for dette felt" (She works in this field). For farm land, use "en mark" (a field): "Koen står på marken" (The cow stands in the field).

sentence.da: Du skal udfylde hvert **felt** på siden.
sentence.en: You have to fill in every field on the page.

et feriested.explanation: "Et feriested" means "a vacation spot". It is built from "en ferie" (a vacation) and "et sted" (a place). The word "sted" also appears in "et mødested" (a meeting place).

sentence.da: Vi tager til et **feriested** ved havet i sommer.
sentence.en: We are going to a vacation spot by the sea this summer.

et fingeraftryk.explanation: "Et fingeraftryk" means "a fingerprint". It is built from "en finger" (a finger) and "et aftryk" (an imprint). The common phrase for recording them is "at tage fingeraftryk" (to take fingerprints): "De tog hans fingeraftryk" (They took his fingerprints).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt et **fingeraftryk** på vinduet og kunne identificere tyven.
sentence.en: The police found a fingerprint on the window and could identify the thief.

et firben.explanation: "Et firben" means "a lizard". It is built from "fir" (four) and "et ben" (a leg), so it is literally "four-leg".

sentence.da: Et **firben** ligger på den varme sten og soler sig.
sentence.en: A lizard lies on the warm rock and sunbathes.

et firma.explanation: "Et firma" means "a company". To say someone sets one up, use "at starte" (to start): "Hun vil starte et firma" (She wants to start a company).

sentence.da: Han har sit eget **firma** i Aarhus.
sentence.en: He has his own company in Aarhus.

et fitnessabonnement.explanation: "Et fitnessabonnement" means "a gym membership". It is built from "fitness" (fitness) and "et abonnement" (a subscription). "Abonnement" also works for other things you subscribe to: "et abonnement på en avis" (a subscription to a newspaper).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler hver måned for mit **fitnessabonnement**, men jeg går sjældent.
sentence.en: I pay every month for my gym membership, but I rarely go.

et fitnesscenter.explanation: "Et fitnesscenter" means "a gym". It is built from "fitness" (fitness) and "et center" (a center). The word "center" also appears in "et indkøbscenter" (a shopping center).

sentence.da: Mange mennesker træner i et **fitnesscenter** efter arbejde.
sentence.en: Many people work out at a gym after work.

et fjernsyn.explanation: "Et fjernsyn" means "a television". It is built from "fjern" (far) and "syn" (sight), literally "far sight". To say you watch TV, use "at se" (to see): "Jeg ser fjernsyn" (I watch TV).

sentence.da: Vi ser film på vores store **fjernsyn**.
sentence.en: We watch movies on our big TV.

et fjols.explanation: "Et fjols" means "a fool". It is a mild insult. To tell someone to stop being silly, say: "Hold nu op, dit fjols!" (Stop it, you fool!)

sentence.da: Jeg følte mig som et **fjols**, da jeg glemte hans navn.
sentence.en: I felt like a fool when I forgot his name.

et flag.explanation: "Et flag" means "a flag". The Danish flag has its own name, "Dannebrog". To raise a flag, use "at hejse" (to hoist): "Vi hejser flaget" (We raise the flag).

sentence.da: Det danske **flag** er rødt med et hvidt kors.
sentence.en: The Danish flag is red with a white cross.

et flertal.explanation: "Et flertal" means "a majority". In grammar, "flertal" also means "plural", and its opposite is "ental" (singular). To say a word is in the plural: "Ordet børn står i flertal" (The word børn is in the plural).

sentence.da: Et **flertal** i Folketinget stemte for den nye lov.
sentence.en: A majority in Parliament voted for the new law.

et fly.explanation: "Et fly" means "a plane". To say you travel by plane, use "med" (by) and leave out the article: "Vi rejser med fly til Spanien" (We travel by plane to Spain). A longer word with the same meaning is "en flyvemaskine" (an airplane).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i et **fly** over skyerne.
sentence.en: We are sitting in a plane above the clouds.

et flyselskab.explanation: "Et flyselskab" means "an airline". It is built from "et fly" (a plane) and "et selskab" (a company). "Selskab" also means a party: "Der er selskab hos naboerne i aften" (There is a party at the neighbors' tonight).

sentence.da: Hvilket **flyselskab** flyver du med?
sentence.en: Which airline are you flying with?

et foder.explanation: "Et foder" means "feed", as in food for farm animals. To say what you buy it for, use "til" (for): "Jeg køber foder til min hest" (I buy feed for my horse). It also means the lining inside a coat: "Jakken har et varmt foder" (The jacket has a warm lining).

sentence.da: Køerne får **foder** i stalden om vinteren.
sentence.en: The cows get feed in the barn in winter.

et foderbræt.explanation: "Et foderbræt" means "a bird feeder". It is built from "et foder" (feed) and "et bræt" (a board). To say you put out food for birds: "Jeg lægger frø på foderbrættet" (I put seeds on the bird feeder).

sentence.da: Småfuglene spiser solsikkekerner fra et **foderbræt** i haven.
sentence.en: The small birds eat sunflower seeds from a bird feeder in the garden.

et fodgængerfelt.explanation: "Et fodgængerfelt" means "a crosswalk". It is built from "en fodgænger" (a pedestrian) and "et felt" (a marked area). A longer word with the same meaning is "en fodgængerovergang" (a pedestrian crossing).

sentence.da: Børnene går over vejen ved et **fodgængerfelt**.
sentence.en: The children cross the road at a crosswalk.
