et fodspor.explanation: "Et fodspor" means "a footprint". It is built from "en fod" (a foot) and "et spor" (a track). "Spor" also means a clue. To say the police look for clues: "Politiet leder efter spor" (The police look for clues).

sentence.da: Der er et **fodspor** i sneen foran døren.
sentence.en: There is a footprint in the snow in front of the door.

et fokus.explanation: "Et fokus" means "a focus". To say you put attention on a subject, use the phrase "at sætte fokus på" (to put focus on): "Skolen sætter fokus på sundhed" (The school puts the focus on health).

forms.en: The focus is on the children.

sentence.da: Vi har **fokus** på vores kunder.
sentence.en: We focus on our customers.

et folk.explanation: "Et folk" means "a people or nation". To talk about the whole nation, say "det danske folk" (the Danish people). To talk about people in general, "folk" is used without an article: "Der er mange folk her" (There are lots of people here).

sentence.da: Det danske **folk** elsker at cykle.
sentence.en: The Danish people love to cycle.

et folketingsvalg.explanation: "Et folketingsvalg" means "a general election". It is built from "Folketinget" (the Danish parliament) and "et valg" (an election). In Denmark, one must be held at least every four years.

sentence.da: Efter et **folketingsvalg** danner partierne en ny regering.
sentence.en: After a general election, the parties form a new government.

et forbud.explanation: "Et forbud" means "a ban". It comes from the verb "at forbyde" (to forbid). To name what is banned, use "mod" (against) after it: "et forbud mod mobiltelefoner" (a ban on cell phones).

sentence.da: Der er et **forbud** mod at ryge på stationen.
sentence.en: There is a ban on smoking at the station.

et foredrag.explanation: "Et foredrag" means "a talk". Do not mix it up with "en tale" (a speech). To say you listen to someone teaching about a subject, use "foredrag": "Vi hører et foredrag om kunst" (We are listening to a talk about art). To say someone thanks the guests, use "tale": "Han sagde tak i sin tale" (He said thank you in his speech).

sentence.da: Forfatteren holder et **foredrag** om sin nye bog på biblioteket.
sentence.en: The author gives a talk about his new book at the library.

et forhold.explanation: "Et forhold" means "a relationship", as in a relationship between people. It also means how two things relate: "Forholdet mellem pris og kvalitet er godt" (The relation between price and quality is good).

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **forhold** til min chef.
sentence.en: I have a good relationship with my boss.

et forholdsord.explanation: "Et forholdsord" means "a preposition". It is built from "et forhold" (a relation) and "et ord" (a word). The ending "ord" also appears in other grammar words, such as "et navneord" (a noun).

sentence.da: På er et **forholdsord**, som viser, hvor noget er.
sentence.en: På is a preposition that shows where something is.

et forhør.explanation: "Et forhør" means "an interrogation". It comes from the verb "at forhøre" (to interrogate). To say the police question a man: "Politiet forhører manden" (The police are interrogating the man).

sentence.da: Politiet holdt et **forhør** med manden i flere timer.
sentence.en: The police held an interrogation with the man for several hours.

et forlag.explanation: "Et forlag" means "a publisher". To say which publisher a book comes out with, use "hos" (at): "Bogen udkommer hos Gyldendal" (The book comes out with Gyldendal).

sentence.da: Hun sender sit manuskript til et **forlag**, fordi hun vil udgive bogen.
sentence.en: She sends her manuscript to a publisher because she wants to publish the book.

et forlig.explanation: "Et forlig" means "a settlement", as in an agreement that ends a dispute. In Danish politics it is also the word for a deal between parties in parliament: "et politisk forlig" (a political deal).

sentence.da: Fagforeningen og arbejdsgiverne nåede et **forlig** efter lange forhandlinger.
sentence.en: The union and the employers reached a settlement after long negotiations.

et formål.explanation: "Et formål" means "a purpose". To say what something is for, use "med" (with) after it, where English says "of": "formålet med mødet" (the purpose of the meeting).

sentence.da: Hvad er dit **formål** med at rejse til Danmark?
sentence.en: What is your purpose in traveling to Denmark?

et fornavn.explanation: "Et fornavn" means "a first name". It is built from "for" (before) and "et navn" (a name). To ask someone for it: "Hvad er dit fornavn?" (What is your first name?)

sentence.da: Mit **fornavn** er Anna.
sentence.en: My first name is Anna.

et forord.explanation: "Et forord" means "a preface". It is built from "for" (before) and "et ord" (a word). For a text at the end of a book, use "efter" (after) instead: "Efterordet står bagest i bogen" (The afterword is at the back of the book).

sentence.da: I et **forord** forklarer forfatteren, hvorfor hun skrev bogen.
sentence.en: In a preface the author explains why she wrote the book.

et forræderi.explanation: "Et forræderi" means "a betrayal". It comes from "en forræder" (a traitor). To name betraying your own country, put "land" (country) in front: "landsforræderi" (treason).

sentence.da: At sælge hemmeligheder til fjenden er et **forræderi** mod landet.
sentence.en: Selling secrets to the enemy is a betrayal of the country.

et forsikringsselskab.explanation: "Et forsikringsselskab" means "an insurance company". It is built from "en forsikring" (insurance) and "et selskab" (a company). To say where you have your insurance, use "hos" (with): "Jeg har min forsikring hos et dansk selskab" (I have my insurance with a Danish company).

sentence.da: Mit **forsikringsselskab** betaler for skaden, hvis bilen bliver stjålet.
sentence.en: My insurance company pays for the damage if the car is stolen.

et forskud.explanation: "Et forskud" means "an advance", as in money paid early. A common phrase is "på forskud" (in advance): "at betale på forskud" (to pay in advance).

sentence.da: Jeg bad chefen om et **forskud** på min løn.
sentence.en: I asked the boss for an advance on my salary.

et forslag.explanation: "Et forslag" means "a suggestion". To say you make one, use "at komme med" (to come with): "Må jeg komme med et forslag?" (May I make a suggestion?)

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **forslag** til middag.
sentence.en: I have a good suggestion for dinner.

et forspring.explanation: "Et forspring" means "a head start". When someone is ahead in something other than a race, the word still fits: "Hun har et forspring i viden" (She has a head start in knowledge).

sentence.da: Hun fik ti sekunders **forspring**, fordi hun var yngst.
sentence.en: She got a ten-second head start because she was the youngest.

et forsvar.explanation: "Et forsvar" means "a defense". When you talk about a country, it means its military: "Danmarks forsvar" (Denmark's defense). When you talk about a sports team, it means the players who stop the other team from scoring: "Holdet har et stærkt forsvar" (The team has a strong defense). The name "Forsvaret" (with a capital F) means the Danish armed forces.

sentence.da: Landets **forsvar** beskytter os mod angreb udefra.
sentence.en: The country's defense protects us against attacks from outside.

et forsøg.explanation: "Et forsøg" means "an experiment". When you talk about trying to do something, it also means "an attempt": "Det var et godt forsøg" (That was a good attempt).

sentence.da: Vi laver et **forsøg** med vand og salt.
sentence.en: We do an experiment with water and salt.

et fortov.explanation: "Et fortov" means "a sidewalk". To say a car is parked on it: "Bilen holder på fortovet" (The car is parked on the sidewalk). Do not mix it up with "en cykelsti" (a bike path), where bikes ride: "Cyklerne kører på cykelstien" (The bikes ride on the bike path).

sentence.da: Jeg går på et smalt **fortov** langs vejen.
sentence.en: I walk on a narrow sidewalk along the road.

et forår.explanation: "Et forår" means "a spring", as in the season. To say what happens in that season, use "i foråret" (in the spring): "I foråret kommer fuglene tilbage" (In the spring the birds come back).

sentence.da: Det er **forår** med mange blomster.
sentence.en: It is spring with many flowers.

et forældremøde.explanation: "Et forældremøde" means "a parent-teacher meeting". It is built from "forældre" (parents) and "et møde" (a meeting). It is for the whole class: "Der er forældremøde i aften" (There is a parent-teacher meeting tonight). A talk about one child is "en skole-hjem-samtale" (a school-home talk): "Vi har en skole-hjem-samtale om Mia" (We have a school-home talk about Mia).

sentence.da: Til et **forældremøde** hører forældrene, hvad børnene laver i skolen.
sentence.en: At a parent-teacher meeting the parents hear what the children do at school.

et foto.explanation: "Et foto" means "a photo". It is short for "et fotografi" (a photograph). To say you take one, use "at tage" (to take): "Må jeg tage et foto?" (May I take a photo?)

sentence.da: Jeg sendte hende et **foto** af hunden.
sentence.en: I sent her a photo of the dog.

et fotografi.explanation: "Et fotografi" means "a photograph". It is the long form of "et foto" (a photo): "Jeg tog et foto af broen" (I took a photo of the bridge).

sentence.da: Fotografen tager et **fotografi** med sit kamera.
sentence.en: The photographer takes a photograph with his camera.

et fradrag.explanation: "Et fradrag" means "a deduction", as in tax. In Danish tax, one deduction is for long trips to work: "et befordringsfradrag" (a commuting deduction).

sentence.da: Et **fradrag** trækker man fra, før skatten beregnes.
sentence.en: You subtract a deduction before the tax is calculated.

et fredet område.explanation: "Et fredet område" means "a protected area". "Fredet" comes from the verb "at frede" (to protect). The word is also used for old buildings: "en fredet bygning" (a listed building).

sentence.da: I et **fredet område** må man ikke fælde træer eller samle blomster.
sentence.en: In a protected area you may not cut down trees or pick flowers.

et fremmedord.explanation: "Et fremmedord" means "a foreign word". It is built from "fremmed" (foreign) and "et ord" (a word). A dictionary of such words is "en fremmedordbog" (a foreign-word dictionary).

sentence.da: Computer er et **fremmedord**, som vi bruger hver dag.
sentence.en: Computer is a foreign word that we use every day.

et fremskridt.explanation: "Et fremskridt" means "an advance", as in progress made. It is built from "frem" (forward) and "et skridt" (a step).

sentence.da: Jeg gør store **fremskridt** i dansk, fordi jeg øver hver dag.
sentence.en: I am making great progress in Danish because I practice every day.

et frikvarter.explanation: "Et frikvarter" means "a recess or break". It is built from "fri" (free) and "et kvarter" (a quarter of an hour). The word "fri" also begins "en fridag" (a day off).

sentence.da: Efter to timer har vi et **frikvarter**, og så leger vi.
sentence.en: After two lessons we have a recess, and then we play.

et frimærke.explanation: "Et frimærke" means "a stamp", as in a postage stamp: "Jeg køber et frimærke" (I buy a stamp). Do not mix it up with "et stempel" (a rubber stamp): "Der er et stempel på papiret" (There is a stamp on the paper).

sentence.da: Du skal sætte et **frimærke** på brevet.
sentence.en: You have to put a stamp on the letter.

et frispark.explanation: "Et frispark" means "a free kick". It is built from "fri" (free) and "et spark" (a kick). The word "spark" also appears in "et hjørnespark" (a corner kick).

sentence.da: Dommeren fløjter og giver os et **frispark** efter en hård tackling.
sentence.en: The referee blows the whistle and gives us a free kick after a hard tackle.

et frø.explanation: "Et frø" means "a seed": "Jeg lægger et frø i jorden" (I put a seed in the soil). Do not mix it up with "en frø" (a frog), which takes "en" instead of "et": "Frøen hopper" (The frog jumps).

sentence.da: Fra et lille **frø** vokser et stort træ.
sentence.en: A big tree grows from a small seed.

et fuglekvidder.explanation: "Et fuglekvidder" means "birdsong". It is built from "en fugl" (a bird) and "kvidder" (twittering). The matching verb is "at kvidre" (to chirp): "Fuglene kvidrer i træerne" (The birds chirp in the trees).

sentence.da: Om foråret er haven fuld af **fuglekvidder**.
sentence.en: In the spring the garden is full of birdsong.

et fund.explanation: "Et fund" means "a find". It comes from the verb "at finde" (to find). Do not read it as the English word "fund" (money): "et fund af mønter" (a find of coins).

sentence.da: Arkæologerne gjorde et vigtigt **fund**: en gammel guldring i jorden.
sentence.en: The archaeologists made an important find: an old gold ring in the ground.

et fundament.explanation: "Et fundament" means "a foundation", as in the base of a building. When you talk about what an idea or a relationship rests on, you use it too: "Tillid er fundamentet for et venskab" (Trust is the foundation of a friendship).

sentence.da: Huset står på et stærkt **fundament** af beton.
sentence.en: The house stands on a strong foundation of concrete.

et fyrretræ.explanation: "Et fyrretræ" means "a pine tree". To name the group of trees it belongs to, use "et nåletræ" (a conifer): "Et fyrretræ er et nåletræ" (A pine tree is a conifer).

sentence.da: Et **fyrretræ** har nåle i stedet for blade og er grønt hele året.
sentence.en: A pine tree has needles instead of leaves and is green all year.

et fyrtårn.explanation: "Et fyrtårn" means "a lighthouse". It is built from "et fyr" (a light for ships) and "et tårn" (a tower). The word "fyr" also means a guy, and then it takes "en": "Han er en flot fyr" (He is a handsome guy).

sentence.da: Om natten viser et **fyrtårn** skibene vej.
sentence.en: At night, a lighthouse shows the ships the way.

et får.explanation: "Et får" means "a sheep": "Der står et får på marken" (There is a sheep in the field). Do not mix it up with "får" (gets) from "at få" (to get): "Han får en gave" (He gets a gift).

sentence.da: Et **får** har uld og siger mæh.
sentence.en: A sheep has wool and says baa.

et fællesskab.explanation: "Et fællesskab" means "a community". It is built from "fælles" (shared) and the ending "-skab", which also appears in "et venskab" (a friendship). For the people living in one local area, use "et lokalsamfund" (a local community): "Hele lokalsamfundet kom til festen" (The whole local community came to the party).

sentence.da: I vores **fællesskab** hjælper alle hinanden, når nogen har brug for det.
sentence.en: In our community everyone helps each other when someone needs it.

et fællesvaskeri.explanation: "Et fællesvaskeri" means "a shared laundry room". It is built from "fælles" (shared) and "et vaskeri" (a laundry). The word "fælles" also appears in "et fællesskab" (a community).

sentence.da: Der er et **fællesvaskeri** i huset, som alle bruger.
sentence.en: There is a shared laundry room in the building that everyone uses.

et fængsel.explanation: "Et fængsel" means "a prison". It comes from the verb "at fængsle" (to imprison): "Politiet fængsler tyven" (The police imprison the thief).

sentence.da: Han kom i **fængsel** i to år.
sentence.en: He went to prison for two years.

et fænomen.explanation: "Et fænomen" means "a phenomenon". With "natur" (nature) in front, "et naturfænomen" is a natural phenomenon: "Regnbuen er et naturfænomen" (The rainbow is a natural phenomenon).

sentence.da: Nordlys er et smukt **fænomen**, men man ser det sjældent i Danmark.
sentence.en: The northern lights are a beautiful phenomenon, but you rarely see them in Denmark.

et fødested.explanation: "Et fødested" means "a birthplace". It is built from "at føde" (to give birth) and "et sted" (a place). To ask someone where they were born: "Hvad er dit fødested?" (What is your place of birth?)

sentence.da: Mit **fødested** er Odense.
sentence.en: My birthplace is Odense.

et føl.explanation: "Et føl" means "a foal". To say a horse gave birth, use "at få" (to get): "Hesten har fået et føl i nat" (The horse had a foal tonight).

sentence.da: Hoppen står i engen med sit lille **føl**.
sentence.en: The mare stands in the meadow with her little foal.

faglig.explanation: "Faglig" means "professional". It comes from the noun "et fag" (a subject or trade). To talk about what someone knows in their field: "faglig viden" (knowledge of the field).

sentence.da: Rapporten er meget **faglig** og bygger på forskning.
sentence.en: The report is very academic and builds on research.

faktisk.explanation: "Faktisk" means "actually". It comes from "et faktum" (a fact). To add a surprising fact about yourself: "Jeg har faktisk boet i Danmark i ti år" (I have actually lived in Denmark for ten years).

sentence.da: Nej, han er **faktisk** dansk.
sentence.en: No, he is actually Danish.

falsk.explanation: "Falsk" means "fake". When you talk about a person who only pretends to be nice, it means "false": "en falsk ven" (a false friend). When you talk about singing, it means "out of tune": "Han synger falsk" (He sings out of tune).

sentence.da: Sedlen er **falsk**, og banken tager ikke imod den.
sentence.en: The bill is fake, and the bank will not accept it.

fantasifuld.explanation: "Fantasifuld" means "imaginative". It is built from "fantasi" (imagination) and "-fuld" (full of), which also appears in "smertefuld" (painful).

sentence.da: Hun er så **fantasifuld**, at hun finder på nye eventyr hver dag.
sentence.en: She is so imaginative that she makes up new adventures every day.

fantastisk.explanation: "Fantastisk" means "fantastic". To answer how something was, say: "Hvordan var ferien?" "Den var fantastisk." (How was the vacation? It was fantastic.)

sentence.da: Maden var **fantastisk**!
sentence.en: The food was fantastic!

farlig.explanation: "Farlig" means "dangerous". It comes from "en fare" (a danger). With "liv" (life) in front, "livsfarlig" means "life-threatening": "Det er livsfarligt at svømme her" (It is life-threatening to swim here).

sentence.da: Vejen er meget **farlig**.
sentence.en: The road is very dangerous.

farvel.explanation: "Farvel" means "goodbye". Literally, it is "fare well". For a casual goodbye to someone you will see again, use "vi ses" (see you): "Vi ses i morgen" (See you tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg siger **farvel** til min ven.
sentence.en: I say goodbye to my friend.

farverig.explanation: "Farverig" means "colorful". It is built from "farve" (color) and "-rig" (rich in), which also appears in "fantasirig" (rich in imagination). When you describe a lively person who stands out, use it too: "en farverig person" (a colorful person).

sentence.da: Gaden er **farverig**, fordi husene er malet gule, røde og blå.
sentence.en: The street is colorful because the houses are painted yellow, red and blue.

fascinerende.explanation: "Fascinerende" means "fascinating". It describes the thing that fascinates you: "Museet er fascinerende" (The museum is fascinating). To say how you feel, use "fascineret" (fascinated): "Jeg er fascineret" (I am fascinated).

sentence.da: Fuglenes liv er **fascinerende**, og jeg læser om dem.
sentence.en: The life of birds is fascinating, and I read about them.

fast.explanation: "Fast" means "fixed", as in a price that does not change: "en fast pris" (a fixed price). When you describe a job that lasts, it also means "steady": "et fast job" (a steady job).

sentence.da: Vi har en **fast** tid hver uge.
sentence.en: We have a set time every week.

fastelavn.explanation: "Fastelavn" means "Shrovetide", a holiday in late winter, in the days before Lent, when a barrel full of sweets is hit open.

forms.en: hit the cat out of the barrel

sentence.da: Børnene klæder sig ud til **fastelavn** og får slik.
sentence.en: The children dress up for Shrovetide and get candy.

fattig.explanation: "Fattig" means "poor", as in having little money: "Familien er fattig" (The family is poor). Do not mix it up with "stakkels" (poor in the sense of unlucky): "stakkels dig" (poor you).

sentence.da: Han er **fattig** og har næsten ingen penge.
sentence.en: He is poor and has almost no money.

fattigdom.explanation: "Fattigdom" means "poverty". It is built from "fattig" (poor) and the ending "-dom", which also makes "en sygdom" (an illness) from "syg" (sick).

sentence.da: Mange børn lever i **fattigdom**.
sentence.en: Many children live in poverty.

februar.explanation: "Februar" means "February". Month names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish: "Vi rejser i februar" (We are traveling in February).

sentence.da: Efter januar kommer **februar**.
sentence.en: After January comes February.

fed.explanation: "Fed" means "cool". It is casual slang. When you see something good, you can say "Det er fedt!" (That is cool!), with a t at the end because it goes with "det". It also means "fatty" in "fed mad" (fatty food).

sentence.da: Wow, du har en **fed** cykel!
sentence.en: Wow, you have a cool bike!

fedt.explanation: "Fedt" means "fat", the kind in food. In casual talk it also means "cool": "Det er fedt!" (That is cool!)

sentence.da: Der er meget **fedt** i pommes frites.
sentence.en: There is a lot of fat in french fries.

fej.explanation: "Fej" means "cowardly": "Det var fejt ikke at sige noget" (It was cowardly not to say anything). Do not mix it up with "bange" (afraid), which is only a feeling: "Jeg er bange, men jeg er ikke fej" (I am afraid, but I am not cowardly).

sentence.da: Han er **fej**, fordi han altid løber væk.
sentence.en: He is cowardly because he always runs away.

fejhed.explanation: "En fejhed" means "cowardice". It is built from "fej" (cowardly) and the ending "-hed", which also makes "en frihed" (freedom) from "fri" (free).

sentence.da: Det var **fejhed** at lade andre tage skylden.
sentence.en: It was cowardice to let others take the blame.

fejlfri.explanation: "Fejlfri" means "flawless". It is built from "en fejl" (a mistake) and "fri" (free). The same "fri" appears in "sukkerfri" (sugar-free).

sentence.da: Teksten er **fejlfri**, og der er ingen stavefejl.
sentence.en: The text is flawless, and there are no spelling mistakes.

fem.explanation: "Fem" means "five". In numbers such as 25, the five comes before the tens: "femogtyve" (twenty-five).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fem** fingre på hver hånd.
sentence.en: I have five fingers on each hand.

femogtredive.explanation: "Femogtredive" means "thirty-five". It is built from "fem" (five), "og" (and) and "tredive" (thirty), so it is literally "five-and-thirty".

sentence.da: Min bror er **femogtredive** år.
sentence.en: My brother is thirty-five years old.

femte.explanation: "Femte" means "fifth". To say a date, use it after "den": "den femte juni" (the fifth of June). To count things, use "fem" (five) instead: "fem dage" (five days).

sentence.da: Min fødselsdag er den **femte** marts.
sentence.en: My birthday is the fifth of March.

femten.explanation: "Femten" means "fifteen". To say fifteen minutes in another way, use "et kvarter" (a quarter of an hour): "Der er et kvarter til bussen" (The bus comes in a quarter of an hour).

sentence.da: Der er **femten** elever i klassen.
sentence.en: There are fifteen students in the class.

festlig.explanation: "Festlig" means "festive". It is built from "en fest" (a party) and the ending "-lig". When you describe a funny person, it can also mean "amusing": "Han er en festlig fyr" (He is an amusing guy).

sentence.da: Julen er **festlig**, fordi vi spiser og synger sammen.
sentence.en: Christmas is festive because we eat and sing together.

feta.explanation: "Feta" means "feta". To name the cheese in full, add "ost" (cheese) to make "fetaost": "Jeg køber fetaost" (I buy feta cheese).

sentence.da: Salaten smager godt med salt **feta** og agurk.
sentence.en: The salad tastes good with salty feta and cucumber.

fibre.explanation: "Fibre" means "fiber". To talk about the fiber in food, use "kostfibre" (dietary fiber): "Havregryn indeholder kostfibre" (Oats contain dietary fiber).

sentence.da: Fuldkornsbrød indeholder mange **fibre**, som er gode for maven.
sentence.en: Whole-grain bread contains many fibers that are good for the stomach.

fiktiv.explanation: "Fiktiv" means "fictional". It comes from "en fiktion" (a fiction). When something is made up to look real, it means "fake": "en fiktiv adresse" (a fake address).

sentence.da: Romanens hovedperson er **fiktiv**, men byen findes i virkeligheden.
sentence.en: The main character of the novel is fictional, but the city exists in reality.

filosofi.explanation: "Filosofi" means "philosophy". When you talk about your own approach to life or work, use it after "min" (my): "Min filosofi er at tage én dag ad gangen" (My philosophy is to take one day at a time).

sentence.da: Hun studerer **filosofi** og spørger, hvorfor vi findes.
sentence.en: She studies philosophy and asks why we exist.

fin.explanation: "Fin" means "nice". When you describe a place that is elegant or expensive, it means "fancy": "en fin restaurant" (a fancy restaurant).

sentence.da: Det er en **fin** dag til en tur.
sentence.en: It is a nice day for a walk.

finland.explanation: "Finland" means "Finland". It is built from "finne" (Finn) and "land" (country).

sentence.da: **Finland** ligger øst for Sverige.
sentence.en: Finland lies east of Sweden.

finsk.explanation: "Finsk" means "Finnish". It is written with a lowercase f, unlike "Finland" (Finland), which starts with a capital F: "Hun er finsk" (She is Finnish).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Finland og taler **finsk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Finland and speaks Finnish.

fint.explanation: "Fint" means "fine". When you agree to a plan, you can answer with just "Fint!": "Skal vi mødes klokken tre?" "Fint!" (Shall we meet at three? Fine!) Before a word that takes "en", use "fin" (nice): "en fin dag" (a nice day).

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? Det går **fint**.
sentence.en: How is it going? It is going fine.

fire.explanation: "Fire" means "four". Do not mix it up with "fyrre" (forty). To say a price, use "fire kroner" (four kroner) for four and "fyrre kroner" (forty kroner) for forty.

sentence.da: Hunden har **fire** ben.
sentence.en: The dog has four legs.

fireogtyve.explanation: "Fireogtyve" means "twenty-four". It is built from "fire" (four), "og" (and) and "tyve" (twenty), so it is literally "four-and-twenty".

sentence.da: Der er **fireogtyve** timer i et døgn.
sentence.en: There are twenty-four hours in a day.

firkantet.explanation: "Firkantet" means "square". It is built from "fire" (four) and "kantet" (edged). When you describe a person, it also means "rigid": "Han er meget firkantet" (He is very rigid).

sentence.da: Skakbrættet er **firkantet** og har 64 felter.
sentence.en: The chessboard is square-shaped and has 64 squares.

firs.explanation: "Firs" means "eighty". It is short for "firsindstyve", which is literally "four times twenty".

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er **firs** år gammel.
sentence.en: My grandfather is eighty years old.

fiskeri.explanation: "Fiskeri" means "fishing", as in the trade or industry. For fishing as a hobby, use "lystfiskeri" (angling): "Min far elsker lystfiskeri" (My father loves angling).

sentence.da: Mange familier i den lille havneby lever af **fiskeri**.
sentence.en: Many families in the small port town make a living from fishing.

fitness.explanation: "Fitness" means "gym". To name the place, add "center": "Vi mødes i fitnesscenteret" (We meet at the gym). To say you are in good shape, use "i form" (in shape): "Jeg er i form" (I am in shape).

sentence.da: Jeg dyrker **fitness** hver morgen før arbejde.
sentence.en: I do fitness every morning before work.

fjendtlig.explanation: "Fjendtlig" means "hostile". It is built from "en fjende" (an enemy) and the ending "-lig". When you talk about the enemy in a war, it means "belonging to the enemy": "et fjendtligt fly" (an enemy plane).

sentence.da: Hunden var **fjendtlig** og knurrede af os.
sentence.en: The dog was hostile and growled at us.

fjerde.explanation: "Fjerde" means "fourth". To say a date, use it after "den": "den fjerde maj" (the fourth of May). To count things, use "fire" (four) instead: "fire dage" (four days).

sentence.da: Han sad i **fjerde** række.
sentence.en: He sat in the fourth row.

fjerkræ.explanation: "Fjerkræ" means "poultry". It is built from "en fjer" (a feather) and "kræ" (an old word for a creature).

sentence.da: Man holder **fjerkræ** på gården for kød og æg.
sentence.en: You keep poultry on the farm for meat and eggs.

fjern.explanation: "Fjern" means "distant". In "fjernsyn" (television), "fjern" means "far away", so it is literally "far-away sight". Do not mix it up with the verb "at fjerne" (to remove): "Jeg fjerner pletten" (I remove the stain).

sentence.da: Han er en **fjern** fætter til mig.
sentence.en: He is a distant cousin of mine.

fjernvarme.explanation: "Fjernvarme" means "district heating". It is built from "fjern" (far) and "varme" (heat), so it is literally "far heat". Many homes in Denmark are heated this way.

sentence.da: Med **fjernvarme** kommer varmen i rør fra et stort værk.
sentence.en: With district heating, the warmth comes in pipes from a big plant.

fjollet.explanation: "Fjollet" means "silly". It comes from the noun "en fjolle" (a fool). To tell someone to stop acting silly, say: "Vær ikke så fjollet!" (Do not be so silly!)

sentence.da: Hun er **fjollet** og laver sjove grimasser.
sentence.en: She is silly and makes funny faces.

fjorten.explanation: "Fjorten" means "fourteen". To say "in two weeks", Danes use "fjorten dage" (literally "fourteen days"): "Vi ses om fjorten dage" (See you in two weeks).

sentence.da: Vi tager på ferie i **fjorten** dage.
sentence.en: We are going on vacation for fourteen days.

flad.explanation: "Flad" means "flat", as in a level surface. When you say a tire has no air, use it too: "Mit dæk er fladt" (My tire is flat).

sentence.da: Stenen er **flad** og glat som en tallerken.
sentence.en: The stone is flat and smooth like a plate.

fleksibel.explanation: "Fleksibel" means "flexible". To describe working hours that can change, say "fleksibel arbejdstid" (flexible working hours).

sentence.da: Min chef er **fleksibel** og lader mig arbejde hjemme.
sentence.en: My boss is flexible and lets me work from home.

fleksibilitet.explanation: "Fleksibilitet" means "flexibility". It comes from the adjective "fleksibel" (flexible). When you talk about the body, it means how well you can bend: "Yoga giver bedre fleksibilitet" (Yoga gives better flexibility).

sentence.da: Hjemmearbejde giver mig **fleksibilitet**, fordi jeg selv bestemmer min tid.
sentence.en: Working from home gives me flexibility because I decide my own time.

flere.explanation: "Flere" means "more". Use it with things you can count: "Jeg vil have flere kager" (I want more cakes). With something you cannot count, use "mere" (more): "Jeg vil have mere vand" (I want more water). When no number is given, "flere" also means "several": "Flere gæster kom for sent" (Several guests came too late).

sentence.da: Der er **flere** æbler end pærer i kurven.
sentence.en: There are more apples than pears in the basket.

flink.explanation: "Flink" means "nice". To say someone is good at something, add "til" (at): "Hun er flink til matematik" (She is good at math).

sentence.da: Naboen er **flink**, og han hjælper os ofte.
sentence.en: The neighbor is nice, and he often helps us.

flittig.explanation: "Flittig" means "diligent". To say someone does not work hard, use the opposite, "doven" (lazy): "Min bror er doven" (My brother is lazy).

sentence.da: Hun er **flittig** og læser lektier hver dag.
sentence.en: She is diligent and does homework every day.

flormelis.explanation: "Flormelis" means "powdered sugar". It is built from "flor" (a thin veil) and "melis" (a kind of sugar).

sentence.da: Drys kagen med **flormelis**, så den ligner sne.
sentence.en: Dust the cake with powdered sugar so that it looks like snow.

flot.explanation: "Flot" means "handsome". When you describe things, it means "nice-looking": "flotte sko" (nice-looking shoes). To praise someone after good work, say "Flot!" (Well done!)

sentence.da: Hun er smuk og har en **flot** kjole.
sentence.en: She is beautiful and has a nice-looking dress.

flov.explanation: "Flov" means "embarrassed". To say how a person feels, use "flov": "Hun følte sig flov" (She felt embarrassed). To say a situation is embarrassing, use "pinlig" (embarrassing): "Det var pinligt" (That was embarrassing).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **flov**, da jeg glemte hans navn.
sentence.en: I got embarrassed when I forgot his name.

flovhed.explanation: "Flovhed" means "embarrassment". It is built from the adjective "flov" (embarrassed) and the ending "-hed". To say why someone reacts, use "af" (out of): "Han tav af flovhed" (He fell silent out of embarrassment).

sentence.da: Hun rødmede af **flovhed** foran hele klassen.
sentence.en: She blushed with embarrassment in front of the whole class.

flydende.explanation: "Flydende" means "fluent". To say how well someone speaks a language, put it before the language: "Han taler flydende engelsk" (He speaks fluent English). When you describe something you can pour, it means "liquid": "flydende sæbe" (liquid soap).

sentence.da: Efter to år taler hun **flydende** dansk.
sentence.en: After two years she speaks fluent Danish.

flæsk.explanation: "Flæsk" means "pork belly". A dish that is specific to Denmark is "stegt flæsk med persillesovs" (fried pork belly with parsley sauce).

sentence.da: Fede skiver **flæsk** bliver sprøde, når man steger dem.
sentence.en: Fatty slices of pork belly become crisp when you fry them.

flæskesteg.explanation: "Flæskesteg" means "roast pork". It is built from "flæsk" (pork) and "en steg" (a roast), the same "steg" as in "en oksesteg" (a beef roast). In Denmark, it is a traditional dish at Christmas dinner.

sentence.da: Vi spiser **flæskesteg** med kartofler og sovs.
sentence.en: We eat roast pork with potatoes and gravy.

fløde.explanation: "Fløde" means "cream". "Piskefløde" (whipping cream) is built from "piske" (to whip) and "fløde". To buy cream for whipping, ask for it by that name: "Jeg køber piskefløde" (I buy whipping cream).

sentence.da: Vil du have **fløde** i kaffen?
sentence.en: Do you want cream in your coffee?

flødeost.explanation: "Flødeost" means "cream cheese". It is built from "fløde" (cream) and "ost" (cheese).

sentence.da: Vi spiser brød med **flødeost** og laks.
sentence.en: We eat bread with cream cheese and salmon.

fn.explanation: "FN" means "the UN", short for "De Forenede Nationer" (the United Nations). It is said letter by letter: "ef-en".

sentence.da: **FN** arbejder for fred og hjælper mennesker i krigsramte lande.
sentence.en: The UN works for peace and helps people in war-torn countries.

fodbold.explanation: "Fodbold" means "soccer ball". When you talk about the game, it means "soccer", and you leave out "en": "Jeg spiller fodbold" (I play soccer). It is built from "en fod" (a foot) and "en bold" (a ball).

sentence.da: Børnene spiller **fodbold** og sparker til bolden.
sentence.en: The children play soccer and kick the ball.

folketinget.explanation: "Folketinget" means "the Parliament". It is the name of Denmark's parliament, which meets at Christiansborg in Copenhagen. It is built from "folk" (people) and "ting" (an assembly). To talk about another country's parliament, use "parlament": "Det britiske parlament" (the British Parliament).

sentence.da: **Folketinget** stemmer om den nye lov i dag.
sentence.en: The Parliament votes on the new law today.

for.explanation: "For" means "for". When you thank someone for something, use it before the thing: "Tak for hjælpen" (Thank you for the help). When you put it before an adjective, it means "too": "Kaffen er for kold" (The coffee is too cold). To say how long ago, put "for" before the time and "siden" (ago) after it: "for tre uger siden" (three weeks ago). To say something is meant for a person, use "til" (to) instead: "en gave til dig" (a gift for you).

sentence.da: Suppen er **for** varm.
sentence.en: The soup is too hot.

for det meste.explanation: "For det meste" means "mostly". It is literally "for the most". To say that something happens most of the time, put it after the verb: "Jeg tager for det meste bussen" (I mostly take the bus).

forms.da: Det er for det meste rart vejr.
Jeg læser for det meste om aftenen.
forms.en: I mostly read in the evening.

sentence.da: Vi spiser **for det meste** hjemme, men nogle gange ude.
sentence.en: We mostly eat at home, but sometimes out.

for eksempel.explanation: "For eksempel" means "for example". It is built from "for" (for) and "et eksempel" (an example). In writing, it is shortened to "fx": "Tag en frugt, fx et æble" (Take a fruit, for example an apple).

forms.da: Jeg kan godt lide frugt, for eksempel æbler.
forms.en: I like fruit, for example apples.

forms.da: Vi kan mødes, for eksempel i morgen.
forms.en: We can meet, for example tomorrow.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser frugt, **for eksempel** æbler.
sentence.en: I eat fruit, for example apples.

for evigt.explanation: "For evigt" means "forever". To complain that something takes a very long time, say: "Det tager en evighed" (It takes forever).

sentence.da: Jeg vil huske dette sted **for evigt**.
sentence.en: I will remember this place forever.

for længe siden.explanation: "For længe siden" means "a long time ago". To say exactly how long, name the time instead: "for to år siden" (two years ago).

forms.en: We met a long time ago
That was a long time ago

forms.da: Jeg boede der for længe siden
forms.en: I lived there a long time ago

sentence.da: Vi boede i Odense **for længe siden**.
sentence.en: We lived in Odense a long time ago.

for nylig.explanation: "For nylig" means "recently". Do not mix it up with "for tiden" (at the moment). To say something happened a short time ago, use "for nylig": "Hun ringede for nylig" (She called recently). To say what is true right now, use "for tiden": "Jeg bor for tiden i Odense" (I live in Odense at the moment).

forms.da: Jeg har for nylig købt en cykel
Vi har for nylig mødt ham

sentence.da: Jeg har **for nylig** købt en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I recently bought a new bike.

for pokker.explanation: "For pokker" means "darn it". It is a mild swear word. To show you are annoyed when something goes wrong, say it first: "For pokker, bussen kørte!" (Darn it, the bus left!)

forms.da: For pokker, jeg har glemt nøglen!
forms.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

sentence.da: **For pokker**, jeg har glemt nøglen!
sentence.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

for søren.explanation: "For søren" means "goodness". To react when something surprises you, say it first: "For søren, jeg har glemt min taske!" (Goodness, I forgot my bag!)

forms.da: For søren, er klokken allerede otte?

sentence.da: **For søren**, hvor er det varmt i dag!
sentence.en: Goodness, it is so hot today!

for tiden.explanation: "For tiden" means "at the moment". To say what is true in these days, use it at the start: "For tiden er der mange biler her" (These days there are many cars here). For this very second, use "lige nu" (right now): "Jeg spiser lige nu" (I am eating right now).

forms.da: Jeg bor i Aarhus for tiden
forms.en: I live in Aarhus at the moment
She works from home at the moment
These days it rains a lot

sentence.da: Jeg arbejder hjemme **for tiden**.
sentence.en: I am working from home at the moment.

foran.explanation: "Foran" means "in front of". To say where you stand, put it before the place: "Jeg står foran døren" (I stand in front of the door). To say the opposite, use "bag" (behind): "Jeg står bag døren" (I stand behind the door). Do not use "før" (before) for a place, because it is only for time: "før klokken fem" (before five o'clock).

sentence.da: Bilen holder **foran** huset.
sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

forbavset.explanation: "Forbavset" means "astonished". To say what astonished you, add "over" (at): "forbavset over resultatet" (astonished at the result).

sentence.da: Hun blev **forbavset**, da hun så gaven.
sentence.en: She was astonished when she saw the gift.

forbi.explanation: "Forbi" means "past". When you say something has ended, it means "over": "Sommeren er forbi" (The summer is over). To invite someone to visit, use it with "kom" (come): "Kom forbi i aften!" (Drop by tonight!)

sentence.da: Bussen kører **forbi** skolen.
sentence.en: The bus drives past the school.

forbløffende.explanation: "Forbløffende" means "astonishing". It describes the thing, not the person: "Resultatet er forbløffende" (The result is astonishing). To describe the person, use "forbløffet" (amazed): "Jeg er forbløffet" (I am amazed).

sentence.da: Det er **forbløffende**, hvor hurtigt barnet lærer at læse.
sentence.en: It is astonishing how fast the child learns to read.

forbløffet.explanation: "Forbløffet" means "amazed". To say what amazed you, add "over" (at): "forbløffet over resultatet" (amazed at the result). It describes how a person feels. For the thing that causes it, use "forbløffende" (astonishing): "Det er forbløffende" (It is astonishing).

sentence.da: Publikum var **forbløffet**, da tryllekunstneren forsvandt.
sentence.en: The audience was amazed when the magician disappeared.

forbrug.explanation: "Forbrug" means "consumption". It comes from the verb "at forbruge" (to consume). To talk about water, put "vand" (water) in front: "Vi sænker vores vandforbrug" (We are lowering our water use).

sentence.da: Vores **forbrug** af strøm er højt om vinteren, fordi det er koldt.
sentence.en: Our use of electricity is high in winter because it is cold.

forbudt.explanation: "Forbudt" means "forbidden". It comes from the verb "at forbyde" (to forbid). To say you may not enter a place, signs say "Adgang forbudt" (No entry).

sentence.da: Det er **forbudt** at køre her.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to drive here.

fordelagtig.explanation: "Fordelagtig" means "advantageous". It is built from "en fordel" (an advantage). To say it pays off to do something now, use the form "fordelagtigt" with "at": "Det er fordelagtigt at købe nu" (It is advantageous to buy now).

sentence.da: Banken tilbyder en meget **fordelagtig** rente.
sentence.en: The bank offers a very advantageous interest rate.

fordi.explanation: "Fordi" means "because". It answers "Hvorfor?" (Why?): "Hvorfor er du træt?" (Why are you tired?) - "Fordi jeg sover for lidt" (Because I sleep too little). Do not mix it up with "derfor" (that is why): "Jeg er træt, derfor går jeg i seng" (I am tired, that is why I go to bed).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver hjemme, **fordi** jeg er syg.
sentence.en: I stay home because I am sick.

fordomsfri.explanation: "Fordomsfri" means "unbiased". It is built from "en fordom" (a prejudice) and "fri" (free).

sentence.da: Hun er **fordomsfri** og møder alle med et åbent sind.
sentence.en: She is unbiased and meets everyone with an open mind.

fordomsfuld.explanation: "Fordomsfuld" means "prejudiced". It is built from "en fordom" (a prejudice) and "-fuld" (full of).

sentence.da: Man bør ikke være **fordomsfuld** over for nye naboer.
sentence.en: You should not be prejudiced toward new neighbors.

forelsket.explanation: "Forelsket" means "in love". To say someone fell in love, use "blive" (become) and "i" (in): "Jeg blev forelsket i hende" (I fell in love with her).

sentence.da: De er **forelsket** og smiler hele tiden.
sentence.en: They are in love and smile all the time.

foreløbig.explanation: "Foreløbig" means "for now". When something is a first version that is not final, it means "preliminary": "en foreløbig plan" (a preliminary plan).

forms.en: For now we know no more

sentence.da: Vi har **foreløbig** intet svar fra kommunen.
sentence.en: For the time being, we have no answer from the municipality.

foreningsliv.explanation: "Foreningsliv" means "club and association life". It is built from "en forening" (an association) and "et liv" (a life). The part "forening" is also in "en idrætsforening" (a sports club): "Jeg er medlem af en idrætsforening" (I am a member of a sports club).

sentence.da: I byens **foreningsliv** kan både børn og voksne spille og synge sammen.
sentence.en: In the town's club life, both children and adults can play and sing together.

forestående.explanation: "Forestående" means "upcoming". It is built from "fore" (ahead) and "stående" (standing), so it is literally "standing ahead".

sentence.da: Hele byen forbereder sig på den **forestående** storm.
sentence.en: The whole town is preparing for the impending storm.

forfra.explanation: "Forfra" means "from the beginning". When you say which side something comes from, it means "from the front": "Han kom forfra" (He came from the front). The opposite is "bagfra" (from behind): "Han kom bagfra" (He came from behind).

sentence.da: Jeg tog fejl, og nu må jeg begynde **forfra**.
sentence.en: I made a mistake, and now I have to start over.

forfærdelig.explanation: "Forfærdelig" means "terrible". It is stronger than "dårlig" (bad): "Maden er dårlig" (The food is bad) and "Maden er forfærdelig" (The food is terrible).

sentence.da: Det var en **forfærdelig** ulykke på motorvejen.
sentence.en: It was a terrible accident on the highway.

forgiftet.explanation: "Forgiftet" means "poisoned". It is built from "for-" and "gift" (poison). When you describe a tense atmosphere, it also means "poisoned": "en forgiftet stemning" (a poisoned atmosphere).

sentence.da: Fiskene døde, fordi vandet i søen var **forgiftet**.
sentence.en: The fish died because the water in the lake was poisoned.

forgængelig.explanation: "Forgængelig" means "transient". For food that spoils, use "letfordærvelig" (perishable) instead: "Fisk er letfordærvelig" (Fish is perishable).

sentence.da: Skønhed er **forgængelig**, men gode minder varer ved.
sentence.en: Beauty is transient, but good memories last.

forgæves.explanation: "Forgæves" means "in vain". Do not mix it up with "nytteløs" (useless), which says a thing has no use: "Det er nytteløst at skændes" (It is useless to argue).

sentence.da: Han prøvede **forgæves** at åbne den låste dør.
sentence.en: He tried in vain to open the locked door.

forhastet.explanation: "Forhastet" means "hasty". It comes from the verb "at haste" (to hurry). To say someone moves fast, use "hurtig" (fast) instead: "Hun er hurtig" (She is fast).

sentence.da: Han tog en **forhastet** beslutning og fortrød den bagefter.
sentence.en: He made a hasty decision and regretted it afterward.

forholdsvis.explanation: "Forholdsvis" means "relatively". It is built from "et forhold" (a ratio) and the ending "-vis". To say something is warm compared with what is normal, put it before the adjective: "forholdsvis varmt" (relatively warm).

sentence.da: Huset er gammelt, men taget er **forholdsvis** nyt.
sentence.en: The house is old, but the roof is relatively new.

forhåbentlig.explanation: "Forhåbentlig" means "hopefully". To say what you hope will happen, use it instead of "Jeg håber, at" (I hope that): "Jeg håber, at det bliver godt vejr" (I hope the weather will be good) becomes "Forhåbentlig bliver det godt vejr" (Hopefully the weather will be good).

sentence.da: **Forhåbentlig** kommer toget til tiden i dag.
sentence.en: Hopefully the train comes on time today.

forinden.explanation: "Forinden" means "beforehand". To say what to do beforehand, put it at the end: "Vi spiser klokken seks. Gå en tur forinden" (We eat at six. Take a walk beforehand). Do not mix it up with "inden" (before), which needs a word after it: "inden mødet" (before the meeting).

sentence.da: Mødet starter klokken ti, så læs mailen **forinden**.
sentence.en: The meeting starts at ten, so read the email beforehand.

forkert.explanation: "Forkert" means "wrong". To say a caller dialed the wrong number, use it before "nummer" (number): "Det er et forkert nummer" (It is a wrong number).

sentence.da: Fem plus fem er tolv. Det er **forkert**.
sentence.en: Five plus five is twelve. That is wrong.

forkælet.explanation: "Forkælet" means "spoiled", as in a child that is given everything. It comes from the verb "at forkæle" (to pamper). For food that has gone bad, use "fordærvet" (rotten): "Maden er fordærvet" (The food is rotten).

sentence.da: Barnet er **forkælet**, fordi det altid får sin vilje.
sentence.en: The child is spoiled because it always gets its way.

forkølet.explanation: "Forkølet" means "with a cold". To name the illness itself, use "en forkølelse" (a cold): "Jeg har en forkølelse" (I have a cold).

sentence.da: Jeg er **forkølet** og hoster meget.
sentence.en: I have a cold and cough a lot.

forladt.explanation: "Forladt" means "abandoned". It comes from the verb "at forlade" (to leave). When you describe how a person feels, it means "left alone": "Han følte sig forladt" (He felt abandoned).

sentence.da: Der står et **forladt** hus i skoven.
sentence.en: There is an abandoned house in the forest.

forlovet.explanation: "Forlovet" means "engaged", as in engaged to marry. To say who you are engaged to, add "med" (with): "Jeg er forlovet med Anna" (I am engaged to Anna).

sentence.da: Vi er **forlovet** og skal giftes næste år.
sentence.en: We are engaged and will get married next year.

formel.explanation: "Formel" means "formal". When you talk about math or science, the same spelling is "en formel" (a formula): "Jeg lærer en ny formel" (I am learning a new formula).

sentence.da: Kontrakten er en **formel** aftale, og begge parter skriver under.
sentence.en: The contract is a formal agreement, and both parties sign.

formentlig.explanation: "Formentlig" means "presumably". To answer a question with a short guess, say it alone: "Kommer han?" "Formentlig." (Is he coming? Presumably.)

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke tjekket, men han er **formentlig** hjemme.
sentence.en: I have not checked, but he is presumably home.

fornuft.explanation: "Fornuft" means "reason", as in the ability to think sensibly. Danish says "sund fornuft", literally "healthy reason", for "common sense": "Brug sund fornuft" (Use common sense).

sentence.da: Hun har meget **fornuft** og tager aldrig overilede beslutninger.
sentence.en: She has a lot of common sense and never makes rash decisions.

fornuftig.explanation: "Fornuftig" means "sensible". It is built from "fornuft" (reason) and the ending "-ig". To describe a person who thinks before acting, say: "Han er et fornuftigt menneske" (He is a sensible person).

sentence.da: Det er en **fornuftig** idé at tage en jakke med.
sentence.en: It is a sensible idea to bring a jacket.

fornærmet.explanation: "Fornærmet" means "offended". It comes from the verb "at fornærme" (to insult). To say what hurt someone's feelings, add "over" (about): "Hun er fornærmet over kommentaren" (She is offended by the comment).

sentence.da: Han blev **fornærmet**, da hun grinede af hans idé.
sentence.en: He was offended when she laughed at his idea.

forrest.explanation: "Forrest" means "at the front". Do not mix it up with "foran" (in front of), which needs a thing after it: "foran huset" (in front of the house).

forms.en: at the front of the line
at the front of the classroom

sentence.da: Børnene sidder **forrest**, så de kan se tavlen.
sentence.en: The children sit at the front so they can see the board.

forresten.explanation: "Forresten" means "by the way". It is one word in Danish. To add a thought after the verb, say: "Jeg kommer forresten i morgen" (I am coming tomorrow, by the way).

forms.en: By the way, where do you live?
I know that, by the way.

sentence.da: **Forresten**, jeg har købt billetter til lørdag.
sentence.en: By the way, I have bought tickets for Saturday.

forrige.explanation: "Forrige" means "last", as in the one before now. To say last month, use "i forrige måned" (last month). After "det" it keeps the same spelling: "det forrige hus" (the previous house).

sentence.da: Vi mødtes i **forrige** uge.
sentence.en: We met last week.

forsigtig.explanation: "Forsigtig" means "careful". To say what you must be careful with, add "med" (with): "Vær forsigtig med glasset" (Be careful with the glass).

sentence.da: Vær **forsigtig**, gulvet er glat!
sentence.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery!

forsikring.explanation: "En forsikring" means "insurance". To say you take out insurance, use the verb "at tegne" (literally, to draw): "Jeg tegner en forsikring" (I take out insurance).

sentence.da: Min **forsikring** dækker ikke vandskade.
sentence.en: My insurance does not cover water damage.

forsinket.explanation: "Forsinket" means "delayed". When you say that you yourself are late, it also means "late": "Jeg er forsinket" (I am late).

sentence.da: Toget er **forsinket** med tyve minutter.
sentence.en: The train is delayed by twenty minutes.

forskellig.explanation: "Forskellig" means "different". It is built from "en forskel" (a difference). When you list several kinds, it means "various": "forskellige farver" (various colors).

sentence.da: Vi har **forskellig** smag, men vi er gode venner.
sentence.en: We have different tastes, but we are good friends.

forskning.explanation: "Forskning" means "research". It comes from the verb "at forske" (to do research). To say you work with research, leave out "en": "Hun arbejder med forskning" (She works in research).

sentence.da: Staten giver penge til **forskning** i kræft og hjertesygdomme.
sentence.en: The state gives money to research on cancer and heart disease.

forskrækket.explanation: "Forskrækket" means "startled". To say someone startled you, use the verb "at forskrække" (to startle): "Du forskrækkede mig!" (You startled me!)

sentence.da: Hunden blev **forskrækket** over den høje lyd.
sentence.en: The dog was startled by the loud noise.

forstoppet.explanation: "Forstoppet" means "constipated". It is built from "for-" and "stoppet" (blocked up).

sentence.da: Hvis man er **forstoppet**, hjælper det at spise mere frugt.
sentence.en: If you are constipated, it helps to eat more fruit.

forståelig.explanation: "Forståelig" means "understandable". When you say a feeling or a reaction makes sense, use it: "en forståelig reaktion" (an understandable reaction).

sentence.da: Hans forklaring var kort og **forståelig**, så alle fulgte med.
sentence.en: His explanation was short and understandable, so everyone followed.

forståelsesfuld.explanation: "Forståelsesfuld" means "understanding". It is built from "forståelse" (understanding) and "-fuld" (full of). To say who someone is understanding toward, add "over for": "Hun er forståelsesfuld over for børnene" (She is understanding toward the children).

sentence.da: Min chef er **forståelsesfuld**, når børnene er syge.
sentence.en: My boss is understanding when the children are sick.

forstående.explanation: "Forstående" means "understanding". It is built from "at forstå" (to understand) and the ending "-ende", which works like the English "-ing".

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **forstående** nik, da jeg forklarede det.
sentence.en: She gave me an understanding nod when I explained it.

forstærkning.explanation: "En forstærkning" means "a reinforcement". To ask for extra people to help, say: "Vi har brug for forstærkning" (We need reinforcements). When you talk about making a sound louder, use it with "af" (of): "forstærkning af lyden" (boosting the sound).

sentence.da: Politiet bad om **forstærkning**, da folkemængden voksede.
sentence.en: The police asked for reinforcement when the crowd grew.

forsømt.explanation: "Forsømt" means "neglected". To describe a street or building that nobody has looked after, say: "Gaden ser forsømt ud" (The street looks neglected). To say people got too little care, say: "Børnene følte sig forsømt" (The children felt neglected). It comes from the verb "at forsømme" (to neglect).

sentence.da: Huset var **forsømt**, og taget var begyndt at lække.
sentence.en: The house was neglected, and the roof had started to leak.

fortabt.explanation: "Fortabt" means "lost", as in gone for good or beyond help. To say you cannot find your way, use "at fare vild" (to get lost) instead: "Jeg er faret vild" (I am lost).

sentence.da: Uden håb og venner følte han sig **fortabt**.
sentence.en: Without hope and friends, he felt lost.

fortjent.explanation: "Fortjent" means "deserved". It comes from the verb "at fortjene" (to deserve).

sentence.da: Efter en lang uge er weekenden **fortjent**.
sentence.en: After a long week, the weekend is well deserved.

fortrinsvis.explanation: "Fortrinsvis" means "mainly". The ending "-vis" is in other adverbs too, such as "delvis" (partly) and "heldigvis" (luckily). To say what you mainly eat, say: "Vi spiser fortrinsvis fisk" (We mainly eat fish).

sentence.da: Butikken sælger **fortrinsvis** dansk mad, men også lidt udenlandsk.
sentence.en: The shop mainly sells Danish food, but also a little foreign food.

fortrolig.explanation: "Fortrolig" means "confidential". When you know a subject well enough to feel at ease with it, it means "familiar", and "med" (with) follows it: "Han er fortrolig med reglerne" (He is familiar with the rules).

sentence.da: Jeg er ikke **fortrolig** med det nye system.
sentence.en: I am not familiar with the new system.

fortrolighed.explanation: "Fortrolighed" means "confidentiality". It is built from "fortrolig" (confidential) and the ending "-hed" (-ness). To say you tell something in confidence, use "i" (in) before it: "Vi taler sammen i fortrolighed" (We talk together in confidence).

sentence.da: Alt, hvad du siger til lægen, bliver behandlet i **fortrolighed**.
sentence.en: Everything you tell the doctor is treated in confidence.

fortroligt.explanation: "Fortroligt" means "confidential". It is the form of "fortrolig" (confidential) used after "er" (is) and after "et", as in "et fortroligt dokument" (a confidential document). When you tell someone something and want it kept private, it also means "in confidence": "Hun sagde det fortroligt til mig" (She told me that in confidence).

forms.en: I am telling you this in confidence

sentence.da: Det er **fortroligt**. Sig det ikke til andre.
sentence.en: It is confidential. Do not tell anyone else.

fortsat.explanation: "Fortsat" means "still", as in something that has not stopped. It comes from the verb "at fortsætte" (to continue).

forms.en: Have a good rest of your day!

sentence.da: Selv efter tre timer regner det **fortsat**.
sentence.en: Even after three hours it is still raining.

fortvivlet.explanation: "Fortvivlet" means "distraught". For a milder feeling, use "ked af det" (sad): "Jeg er ked af det" (I am sad).

sentence.da: Hun var **fortvivlet**, fordi hun ikke kunne finde sit barn.
sentence.en: She was distraught because she could not find her child.

forud.explanation: "Forud" means "ahead". To say something comes before an event, use "forud for" (ahead of): "Forud for mødet læser vi papirerne" (Before the meeting, we read the papers). To say you paid before getting something, say: "Jeg har betalt forud" (I have paid in advance). To say something is further along the road, use "forude" (ahead) instead: "Der er kø forude" (There is a traffic jam ahead).

sentence.da: Vi læser alle papirerne **forud** for mødet.
sentence.en: We read all the papers before the meeting.

forude.explanation: "Forude" means "ahead". To say what is further along the road you are driving, say: "Der er vejarbejde forude" (There are roadworks ahead). To say you walk in front of others, use "forud" (ahead) with "gå" (go) instead: "Jeg går forud" (I go ahead).

sentence.da: Der er kø **forude**, så vi kommer for sent.
sentence.en: There is a traffic jam ahead, so we will be late.

foruden.explanation: "Foruden" means "besides". It is built from "for" and "uden" (without). To say "except" instead, use "bortset fra" (apart from): "Alle kom bortset fra Peter" (Everyone came except Peter).

sentence.da: **Foruden** mig kom der tre venner til festen.
sentence.en: Besides me, three friends came to the party.

forudsat at.explanation: "Forudsat at" means "provided that". In the part after it, "ikke" (not) comes before the verb. To say a condition must not happen, say: "forudsat at han ikke kommer" (provided that he does not come).

forms.en: provided that the weather is nice

sentence.da: Vi tager til stranden, **forudsat at** det ikke regner.
sentence.en: We are going to the beach, provided that it does not rain.

forurening.explanation: "En forurening" means "pollution". It comes from the verb "at forurene" (to pollute). To say pollution of the air, join "luft" (air) to it: "luftforurening" (air pollution).

sentence.da: I byen gør **forurening** fra biler luften dårlig.
sentence.en: In the city, pollution from cars makes the air bad.

foruroligende.explanation: "Foruroligende" means "disturbing". It is built from "urolig" (uneasy). To say how a person feels, use "bekymret" (worried) instead: "Jeg er bekymret" (I am worried).

sentence.da: Det er **foruroligende**, at så mange børn ikke kan svømme.
sentence.en: It is disturbing that so many children cannot swim.

forventningsfuld.explanation: "Forventningsfuld" means "expectant". It is built from "en forventning" (an expectation) and "-fuld" (full of).

sentence.da: Pigen var meget **forventningsfuld** op til sin fødselsdag.
sentence.en: The girl was very expectant before her birthday.

forvirrende.explanation: "Forvirrende" means "confusing". To say how a person feels, use "forvirret" (confused) instead: "Jeg er forvirret" (I am confused).

sentence.da: Skiltene i byen er så **forvirrende**, at vi kører forkert.
sentence.en: The signs in the town are so confusing that we drive the wrong way.

forvirret.explanation: "Forvirret" means "confused". To say something makes people confused, use "forvirrende" (confusing) about it instead: "Reglen er forvirrende" (The rule is confusing).

sentence.da: Jeg er **forvirret**, fordi jeg ikke forstår det.
sentence.en: I am confused because I do not understand it.

forvirring.explanation: "Forvirring" means "confusion". It is the noun for "forvirret" (confused): "Jeg er helt forvirret" (I am totally confused).

sentence.da: Der var **forvirring**, fordi alle talte på samme tid.
sentence.en: There was confusion because everyone talked at the same time.

forældet.explanation: "Forældet" means "outdated". To say something looks or feels old-fashioned, use "gammeldags" (old-fashioned) instead: "et gammeldags køkken" (an old-fashioned kitchen).

sentence.da: Programmet er **forældet**, så det virker ikke på nye telefoner.
sentence.en: The program is outdated, so it does not work on new phones.

forældre.explanation: "Forældre" means "parents". To say one parent, use "en forælder" (a parent): "Hun er forælder til to børn" (She is a parent of two children).

sentence.da: Min mor og min far er mine **forældre**.
sentence.en: My mom and my dad are my parents.

forældreløs.explanation: "Forældreløs" means "orphaned". It is built from "forældre" (parents) and the ending "-løs" (-less), which is also in "hjemløs" (homeless) and "søvnløs" (sleepless).

sentence.da: Efter ulykken blev drengen **forældreløs** og kom til en plejefamilie.
sentence.en: After the accident the boy became an orphan and went to a foster family.

forældremyndighed.explanation: "En forældremyndighed" means "custody", as in the legal right to make decisions for a child. It is built from "forældre" (parents) and "en myndighed" (an authority). To say both parents share it, say: "Vi har fælles forældremyndighed" (We have joint custody).

sentence.da: Efter skilsmissen fik moren **forældremyndighed** over børnene.
sentence.en: After the divorce, the mother got custody of the children.

fra.explanation: "Fra" means "from". To say who gave a gift, use "fra": "en gave fra min mor" (a gift from my mother). To say who the gift is for, use "til" (to, for): "en gave til min mor" (a gift for my mother).

sentence.da: Toget kører **fra** København til Aarhus.
sentence.en: The train goes from Copenhagen to Aarhus.

fra nu af.explanation: "Fra nu af" means "from now on". To look back instead, use "indtil nu" (until now): "Indtil nu har jeg spist usundt" (Until now I have eaten unhealthily).

forms.da: Fra nu af spiser jeg sundt.
forms.en: From now on I will eat healthy.

forms.da: Fra nu af kommer jeg tidligt.
forms.en: From now on I will come early.

forms.da: Fra nu af er det mit job.
forms.en: From now on it will be my job.

sentence.da: Jeg går i seng klokken ti **fra nu af**.
sentence.en: I go to bed at ten from now on.

fra tid til anden.explanation: "Fra tid til anden" means "from time to time". Literally, it is "from time to other". When the phrase starts the sentence, the verb comes right after it: "Fra tid til anden kommer han forbi" (From time to time he comes by).

forms.da: Vi ses fra tid til anden
forms.en: We see each other from time to time

forms.da: Jeg ringer fra tid til anden
forms.en: I call from time to time

forms.da: Hun besøger os fra tid til anden
forms.en: She visits us from time to time

sentence.da: Vi spiser ude **fra tid til anden**, men ikke hver uge.
sentence.en: We eat out from time to time, but not every week.

fragt.explanation: "En fragt" means "shipping or freight". In "et fragtskib" (a cargo ship), "fragt" means the cargo that is carried.

sentence.da: Webshoppen tager 50 kroner i **fragt**.
sentence.en: The web shop charges 50 kroner for shipping.

frankrig.explanation: "Frankrig" means "France". To say you are there, use "i" (in): "Vi bor i Frankrig" (We live in France). To say you are going there, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Frankrig" (We are traveling to France).

sentence.da: Paris ligger i **Frankrig**.
sentence.en: Paris is in France.

fransk.explanation: "Fransk" means "French", as in from France. It also means the language. Unlike English, Danish spells it without a big first letter even for the language: "Jeg taler fransk" (I speak French).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Frankrig og taler **fransk**.
sentence.en: She comes from France and speaks French.

franskbrød.explanation: "Et franskbrød" means "a white loaf". It is made of "fransk" (French) and "brød" (bread). To say dark rye bread instead, use "rugbrød" (rye bread): "Jeg vil have rugbrød med ost" (I want rye bread with cheese).

sentence.da: **Franskbrød** er lyst og blødt brød.
sentence.en: White bread is light, soft bread.

fraskilt.explanation: "Fraskilt" means "divorced". It comes from the verb "at skille" (to separate). To talk about the event of getting divorced, say "at blive skilt" (to get divorced): "De blev skilt i fjor" (They got divorced last year).

sentence.da: Min mor er **fraskilt** og bor alene.
sentence.en: My mom is divorced and lives alone.

fravær.explanation: "Et fravær" means "an absence". To give the number of days someone has missed, say: "Hun har fem dages fravær" (She has five days of absence).

sentence.da: Eleven har meget **fravær**, fordi hun ofte er syg.
sentence.en: The student has a lot of absence because she is often ill.

fraværende.explanation: "Fraværende" means "absent". To say someone is not there, say: "Eleven er fraværende i dag" (The student is absent today). To say someone is there but their mind is elsewhere, it means "absent-minded": "Han virker fraværende i dag" (He seems absent-minded today).

sentence.da: Han sidder ved bordet, men er helt **fraværende**.
sentence.en: He sits at the table, but is completely absent-minded.

fred.explanation: "Fred" means "peace". To tell someone to stop bothering you, say "Lad mig være i fred" (Leave me alone). Literally, it is "let me be in peace".

sentence.da: Landet har haft **fred** i mange år.
sentence.en: The country has had peace for many years.

fredag.explanation: "Fredag" means "a Friday". To say the coming Friday, use "på fredag": "Vi ses på fredag" (See you on Friday). To say every Friday, use "om fredagen": "Om fredagen spiser vi pizza" (On Fridays we eat pizza). Unlike English, Danish spells day names without a big first letter.

sentence.da: Efter torsdag kommer **fredag**.
sentence.en: After Thursday comes Friday.

fredelig.explanation: "Fredelig" means "peaceful". It is built from "fred" (peace). To describe a protest without fighting, say: "en fredelig demonstration" (a peaceful protest).

sentence.da: Landsbyen er stille og **fredelig**.
sentence.en: The village is quiet and peaceful.

frelse.explanation: "En frelse" means "a salvation". When help arrives just in time, it means "godsend": "Din hjælp var en frelse" (Your help was a godsend).

sentence.da: I kristendommen handler **frelse** om tilgivelse for synd.
sentence.en: In Christianity, salvation is about forgiveness of sin.

fremfor.explanation: "Fremfor" means "rather than". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "for" (for). To say you choose one thing over another, say: "Jeg tager toget fremfor flyet" (I take the train rather than the plane).

sentence.da: Mange danskere cykler **fremfor** at køre bil.
sentence.en: Many Danes bike rather than drive a car.

fremgang.explanation: "En fremgang" means "progress". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "en gang" (a going), so it is literally "going forward". To say someone is improving, say: "Eleven gør fremgang i dansk" (The student is making progress in Danish).

sentence.da: Efter tre måneders træning kan jeg se **fremgang**.
sentence.en: After three months of training I can see progress.

fremmed.explanation: "Fremmed" means "strange". To describe something from another country, it means "foreign": "Hun taler et fremmed sprog" (She speaks a foreign language). To say a person you do not know, use "en fremmed" (a stranger): "Tal ikke med fremmede" (Do not talk to strangers).

sentence.da: Det er et **fremmed** sprog for mig.
sentence.en: It is a foreign language to me.

fremover.explanation: "Fremover" means "from now on". To say a new habit starts today, say: "Fremover står jeg tidligt op" (From now on I get up early). When the word starts the sentence, the verb comes right after it.

forms.en: From now on I take the bike
We will see each other more often from now on
From now on you must call first

sentence.da: Jeg vil **fremover** gå i seng klokken ti.
sentence.en: From now on I will go to bed at ten.

fremragende.explanation: "Fremragende" means "excellent". To say someone stands out because of importance or position, use "fremtrædende" (prominent): "et fremtrædende medlem af klubben" (a prominent member of the club).

sentence.da: Hans karakterer er **fremragende**, fordi han læser hver dag.
sentence.en: His grades are excellent because he studies every day.

fremtidig.explanation: "Fremtidig" means "future". To say the time that is coming, use "fremtiden" (the future): "Fremtiden ser lys ud" (The future looks bright).

sentence.da: Hun er en **fremtidig** kollega.
sentence.en: She is a future colleague.

fremtrædende.explanation: "Fremtrædende" means "prominent". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at træde" (to step).

sentence.da: Hun er en **fremtrædende** forsker inden for medicin.
sentence.en: She is a prominent researcher in medicine.

fri.explanation: "Fri" means "off", as in time away from work or school: "Jeg har fri i morgen" (I am off tomorrow). It also means "free", as in not controlled: "Du har frit valg" (You have a free choice). To say "free of charge", use "gratis" instead: "Kaffen er gratis" (The coffee is free of charge).

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fri** fra arbejde.
sentence.en: Today I am off work.

frisk.explanation: "Frisk" means "fresh". To say a person is healthy, use it about the person: "Er du frisk igen?" (Are you well again?).

sentence.da: Jeg købte mælken i dag. Den er **frisk**.
sentence.en: I bought the milk today. It is fresh.

fritid.explanation: "Fritid" means "free time". It is built from "fri" (free) and "tid" (time). To ask about someone's free time, say: "Hvad laver du i din fritid?" (What do you do in your free time?).

sentence.da: I min **fritid** går jeg ture.
sentence.en: In my free time I go for walks.

frivillig.explanation: "Frivillig" means "voluntary". To talk about a person who volunteers, use "en frivillig" (a volunteer): "Vi har brug for frivillige" (We need volunteers).

sentence.da: Deltagelsen er **frivillig**, og man kan sige nej.
sentence.en: Taking part is voluntary, and you can say no.

frodig.explanation: "Frodig" means "lush". To describe thick green growth, say: "en frodig skov" (a lush forest).

sentence.da: Efter al regnen er haven blevet **frodig** og grøn.
sentence.en: After all the rain, the garden has become lush and green.

frokost.explanation: "Frokost" means "lunch". To ask about the meal, say: "Hvad skal vi have til frokost?" (What are we having for lunch?).

sentence.da: Klokken er tolv. Vi spiser **frokost**.
sentence.en: It is twelve o'clock. We eat lunch.

frossen.explanation: "Frossen" means "frozen". To say a person feels cold, use "at fryse" (to freeze) instead: "Jeg fryser" (I am cold).

sentence.da: Pizzaen i fryseren er **frossen**.
sentence.en: The pizza in the freezer is frozen.

frost.explanation: "Frost" means "frost". It is the noun for "at fryse" (to freeze): "Vandet fryser" (The water freezes).

sentence.da: Når der er **frost**, fryser vandet til is.
sentence.en: When there is frost, the water freezes to ice.

frostklar.explanation: "Frostklar" means "crisp, frosty". It is made of "frost" (frost) and "klar" (clear). To describe the weather today, say: "Det er frostklart i dag" (It is crisp and frosty today).

sentence.da: Det var en **frostklar** nat med tusindvis af stjerner.
sentence.en: It was a crisp, frosty night with thousands of stars.

frostvarer.explanation: "En frostvare" means "a frozen product". It is made of "frost" (frost) and "en vare" (a product). The plural "frostvarer" means "frozen foods": "Jeg køber frostvarer" (I buy frozen foods).

sentence.da: I fryseren holder **frostvarer** som ærter og fisk sig længe.
sentence.en: In the freezer, frozen foods like peas and fish keep for a long time.

frustreret.explanation: "Frustreret" means "frustrated". To say how you feel, say: "Jeg er frustreret over computeren" (I am frustrated with the computer). To say something causes the feeling, use "frustrerende" (frustrating): "Det er frustrerende" (It is frustrating).

sentence.da: Han er **frustreret**, fordi printeren ikke virker.
sentence.en: He is frustrated because the printer does not work.

frygt.explanation: "En frygt" means "a fear". To say you are afraid, use "bange" (afraid) instead: "Jeg er bange" (I am afraid).

sentence.da: Hun kunne ikke skjule sin **frygt**.
sentence.en: She could not hide her fear.

sentence.da: Stormen var **frygtelig**, og træer faldt om.
sentence.en: The storm was terrible, and trees fell over.

frygtløs.explanation: "Frygtløs" means "fearless". It is built from "frygt" (fear) and the ending "-løs" (-less). To say someone acts even when afraid, use "modig" (brave): "Hun er modig" (She is brave).

sentence.da: Hun er **frygtløs** og springer fra tre meters højde.
sentence.en: She is fearless and jumps from a height of three meters.

fræk.explanation: "Fræk" means "cheeky". To say a child is testing the limits, say: "Hvor er du fræk!" (How cheeky you are!). To describe a daring joke, say: "en fræk vittighed" (a cheeky joke).

sentence.da: Den lille dreng var meget **fræk** i dag.
sentence.en: The little boy was very naughty today.

fugtig.explanation: "Fugtig" means "damp". To say something is soaked through, use "våd" (wet) instead: "Mine sko er våde" (My shoes are wet).

sentence.da: Luften i badeværelset er meget **fugtig**.
sentence.en: The air in the bathroom is very humid.

fugtighed.explanation: "Fugtighed" means "humidity". It is built from "fugtig" (damp) and the ending "-hed" (-ness).

sentence.da: Der er høj **fugtighed** i badeværelset efter et varmt bad.
sentence.en: There is high humidity in the bathroom after a hot bath.

fugtigt.explanation: "Fugtigt" means "humid". It is the form of "fugtig" (damp) used after "er" (is) and after "et", as in "et fugtigt rum" (a damp room). To say a thing is a little wet, say: "Håndklædet er stadig fugtigt" (The towel is still damp). To say it is soaked, use "vådt" (wet): "Gulvet er vådt" (The floor is wet).

sentence.da: Der er **fugtigt** i kælderen.
sentence.en: It is damp in the basement.

fuld.explanation: "Fuld" means "full". When it describes a person, it means "drunk": "Han er fuld" (He is drunk). To say you are full after a meal, use "mæt" (full) instead: "Jeg er mæt" (I am full).

sentence.da: Bussen er helt **fuld** af mennesker.
sentence.en: The bus is completely full of people.

fuldført.explanation: "Fuldført" means "completed". It comes from the verb "at fuldføre" (to complete). To say you finished a course, say: "Jeg har fuldført kurset" (I have completed the course).

sentence.da: Opgaven er **fuldført**, når alle punkter er markeret.
sentence.en: The task is completed when all items are marked.

fuldkommen.explanation: "Fuldkommen" means "perfect". When you describe a state or feeling as total, it means "complete": "fuldkommen tavshed" (complete silence).

sentence.da: Hun følte en **fuldkommen** ro, da hun så havet.
sentence.en: She felt a perfect calm when she saw the sea.

fuldkorn.explanation: "Fuldkorn" means "whole grain". To name a food made from it, put the food after it: "fuldkornspasta" (whole-grain pasta).

sentence.da: **Fuldkorn** er sundt, fordi det har mange fibre.
sentence.en: Whole grain is healthy because it has a lot of fiber.

fuldstændig.explanation: "Fuldstændig" means "completely". To say someone is completely right, say: "Hun har fuldstændig ret" (She is completely right). When it describes a thing with no part missing, it means "complete": "et fuldstændigt svar" (a complete answer).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fuldstændig** glemt hans navn.
sentence.en: I have completely forgotten his name.

fuldt booket.explanation: "Fuldt booket" means "fully booked". It is made of "fuldt" (fully) and "booket" (booked). For tickets to a show, say "udsolgt" (sold out) instead: "Koncerten er udsolgt" (The concert is sold out).

forms.da: Vi er fuldt booket i juli.
forms.en: We are fully booked in July.

sentence.da: Desværre er hotellet **fuldt booket** i weekenden.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, the hotel is fully booked this weekend.

fyldestgørende.explanation: "Fyldestgørende" means "satisfactory". To say a report covers everything needed, say: "Rapporten er fyldestgørende" (The report is satisfactory).

sentence.da: Lærerens forklaring var kort, men **fyldestgørende**.
sentence.en: The teacher's explanation was short but satisfactory.

fyldig.explanation: "Fyldig" means "rich", as in a taste with body. To describe a voice with depth, say: "en fyldig stemme" (a rich voice).

sentence.da: Vinen er **fyldig**, med smag af mørke bær.
sentence.en: The wine is full-bodied, with a taste of dark berries.

fyldt.explanation: "Fyldt" means "full". It comes from the verb "at fylde" (to fill). To say a person has eaten enough, use "mæt" (full) instead: "Jeg er mæt" (I am full).

sentence.da: Hans lommer er **fyldt** med slik.
sentence.en: His pockets are filled with candy.

fyrre.explanation: "Fyrre" means "forty". To tell it apart from "fire" (four), compare "fire kroner" (four kroner) and "fyrre kroner" (forty kroner). In numbers like 41, the one comes first: "enogfyrre" (forty-one), literally "one and forty".

sentence.da: Jeg er **fyrre** år gammel.
sentence.en: I am forty years old.
